Initially an indie film favorite, actor Jon Favreau has progressed to strong mainstream visibility into the millennium and, after nearly two decades in the business, is still enjoying character stardom as well as earning notice as a writer/producer/director.  
  
The amiable, husky-framed actor with the tight, crinkly hair was born in Queens, New York on October 19, 1966, the only child of Madeleine (Balkoff), an elementary school teacher, and Charles Favreau, a special education teacher. His father has French-Canadian, German, and Italian ancestry, and his mother was from a Russian Jewish family. He attended the Bronx High School of Science before furthering his studies at Queens College in 1984. Dropping out just credits away from receiving his degree, Jon moved to Chicago where he focused on comedy and performed at several Chicago improvisational theaters, including the ImprovOlympic and the Improv Institute. He also found a couple of bit parts in films.  
  
While there, he earned another bit role in the film, [Rudy (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108002/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and met fellow cast mate [Vince Vaughn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000681/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Their enduring personal friendship would play an instrumental role in furthering both their professional careers within just a few years. Jon broke into TV with a role on the classic series, [Seinfeld (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098904/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) (as "Eric the Clown"). After filming rudimentary roles in the movies [Mrs. Parker and the Vicious Circle (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110588/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Notes from Underground (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114005/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Batman Forever (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112462/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), he decided to do some risk taking by writing himself and friend Vaughn into what would become their breakthrough film. [Swingers (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0117802/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), which he also co-produced, centers on Jon as a luckless, struggling actor type who is emotionally shattered after losing his girlfriend, but is pushed back into the L.A. social scene via the help of cool, worldly, outgoing actor/buddy Vaughn. These two blueprint roles went on to define the character types of both actors on film.  
  
In 1997, Jon appeared favorably on several episodes of the popular TV sitcom, [Friends (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108778/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), as "Pete Becker", the humdrum but extremely wealthy suitor for [Courteney Cox](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001073/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s "Monica" character, and also appeared to fine advantage on the [Tracey Takes On... (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115396/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) comedy series. He later took on the biopic mini-movie, [Rocky Marciano (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0183718/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), portraying the prizefighter himself in a highly challenging dramatic role and received excellent reviews. Other engagingly offbeat "everyman" films roles came Jon's way -- the ex-athlete in the working class film, [Dogtown (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119001/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); a soon-to-be groom whose bachelor party goes horribly awry in the comedy thriller [Very Bad Things (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0124198/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); a newlywed opposite [Famke Janssen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000463/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) in [Love & Sex (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0234137/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); a wild and crazy linebacker in [The Replacements (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0191397/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); as [Ben Affleck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000255/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s legal partner in [Daredevil (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0287978/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); and another down-and-out actor in [The Big Empty (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0321442/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He wrote and directed himself and Vaughn as two fellow boxers who involve themselves in criminal activity in [Made (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0227005/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Both he and Vaughn produced. He also directed the highly popular [Will Ferrell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002071/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) comedy [Elf (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0319343/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), in which he had a small part.  
  
Jon went on to re-team favorably with his friend, [Vince Vaughn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000681/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), who enjoyed a meteoric rise into the comedy star ranks, in such light-weight features as [The Break-Up (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0452594/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Four Christmases (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0369436/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Couples Retreat (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1078940/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), the last of which he co-wrote with Vaughn.  
  
Jon has made even greater strides as a writer, producer and/or director in recent years with the exciting mega-box office action-packed [Iron Man (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0371746/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), starring [Robert Downey Jr.](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000375/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and its sequels, [Iron Man 2 (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1228705/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Iron Man 3 (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1300854/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Jon's character of "Happy Hogan" would be featured in a number of Marvel Comic adventures. Other offerings behind the scenes have included the adventure dramedy [Chef (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2883512/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), in which he also starred in the title role; the revamped film version of [The Avengers (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0848228/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) also starring Downey Jr., and it's sequels [Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2395427/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Avengers: Infinity War (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt4154756/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Avengers: Endgame (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt4154796/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); and the animated Disney features [The Jungle Book (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3040964/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [The Lion King (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6105098/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and the TV series [The Chef Show (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt10359446/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
Favreau's marriage to Joya Tillem on November 24, 2000, produced son Max and two daughters, Madeleine and Brighton Rose. Joya is the niece of KGO (AM) lawyer and talk show host, Len Tillem. On the sly, the actor/writer/producer/director enjoys playing on the World Poker Tour.

Initially an indie film favorite, actor Jon Favreau has progressed to strong mainstream visibility into the millennium and, after nearly two decades in the business, is still enjoying character stardom as well as earning notice as a writer/producer/director.  
  
The amiable, husky-framed actor with the tight, crinkly hair was born in Queens, New York on October 19, 1966, the only child of Madeleine (Balkoff), an elementary school teacher, and Charles Favreau, a special education teacher. His father has French-Canadian, German, and Italian ancestry, and his mother was from a Russian Jewish family. He attended the Bronx High School of Science before furthering his studies at Queens College in 1984. Dropping out just credits away from receiving his degree, Jon moved to Chicago where he focused on comedy and performed at several Chicago improvisational theaters, including the ImprovOlympic and the Improv Institute. He also found a couple of bit parts in films.  
  
While there, he earned another bit role in the film, [Rudy (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108002/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and met fellow cast mate [Vince Vaughn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000681/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Their enduring personal friendship would play an instrumental role in furthering both their professional careers within just a few years. Jon broke into TV with a role on the classic series, [Seinfeld (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098904/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) (as "Eric the Clown"). After filming rudimentary roles in the movies [Mrs. Parker and the Vicious Circle (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110588/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Notes from Underground (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114005/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Batman Forever (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112462/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), he decided to do some risk taking by writing himself and friend Vaughn into what would become their breakthrough film. [Swingers (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0117802/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), which he also co-produced, centers on Jon as a luckless, struggling actor type who is emotionally shattered after losing his girlfriend, but is pushed back into the L.A. social scene via the help of cool, worldly, outgoing actor/buddy Vaughn. These two blueprint roles went on to define the character types of both actors on film.  
  
In 1997, Jon appeared favorably on several episodes of the popular TV sitcom, [Friends (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108778/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), as "Pete Becker", the humdrum but extremely wealthy suitor for [Courteney Cox](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001073/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s "Monica" character, and also appeared to fine advantage on the [Tracey Takes On... (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115396/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) comedy series. He later took on the biopic mini-movie, [Rocky Marciano (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0183718/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), portraying the prizefighter himself in a highly challenging dramatic role and received excellent reviews. Other engagingly offbeat "everyman" films roles came Jon's way -- the ex-athlete in the working class film, [Dogtown (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119001/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); a soon-to-be groom whose bachelor party goes horribly awry in the comedy thriller [Very Bad Things (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0124198/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); a newlywed opposite [Famke Janssen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000463/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) in [Love & Sex (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0234137/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); a wild and crazy linebacker in [The Replacements (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0191397/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); as [Ben Affleck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000255/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s legal partner in [Daredevil (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0287978/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); and another down-and-out actor in [The Big Empty (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0321442/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He wrote and directed himself and Vaughn as two fellow boxers who involve themselves in criminal activity in [Made (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0227005/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Both he and Vaughn produced. He also directed the highly popular [Will Ferrell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002071/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) comedy [Elf (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0319343/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), in which he had a small part.  
  
Jon went on to re-team favorably with his friend, [Vince Vaughn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000681/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), who enjoyed a meteoric rise into the comedy star ranks, in such light-weight features as [The Break-Up (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0452594/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Four Christmases (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0369436/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Couples Retreat (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1078940/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), the last of which he co-wrote with Vaughn.  
  
Jon has made even greater strides as a writer, producer and/or director in recent years with the exciting mega-box office action-packed [Iron Man (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0371746/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), starring [Robert Downey Jr.](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000375/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and its sequels, [Iron Man 2 (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1228705/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Iron Man 3 (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1300854/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Jon's character of "Happy Hogan" would be featured in a number of Marvel Comic adventures. Other offerings behind the scenes have included the adventure dramedy [Chef (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2883512/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), in which he also starred in the title role; the revamped film version of [The Avengers (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0848228/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) also starring Downey Jr., and it's sequels [Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2395427/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Avengers: Infinity War (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt4154756/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Avengers: Endgame (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt4154796/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); and the animated Disney features [The Jungle Book (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3040964/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [The Lion King (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6105098/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and the TV series [The Chef Show (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt10359446/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
Favreau's marriage to Joya Tillem on November 24, 2000, produced son Max and two daughters, Madeleine and Brighton Rose. Joya is the niece of KGO (AM) lawyer and talk show host, Len Tillem. On the sly, the actor/writer/producer/director enjoys playing on the World Poker Tour.

_**Iron Man**_ is a 2008 American [superhero film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superhero_film "Superhero film") based on the [Marvel Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics") character [Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man "Iron Man"). Produced by [Marvel Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Studios "Marvel Studios") and distributed by [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures"),[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-Distributor-2) it is [the first film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Marvel_Cinematic_Universe_films "List of Marvel Cinematic Universe films") in the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") (MCU). Directed by [Jon Favreau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau "Jon Favreau") and written by the teams of [Mark Fergus & Hawk Ostby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Fergus_&_Hawk_Ostby "Mark Fergus & Hawk Ostby") and [Art Marcum & Matt Holloway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Marcum_&_Matt_Holloway "Art Marcum & Matt Holloway"), the film stars [Robert Downey Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Downey_Jr. "Robert Downey Jr.") as [Tony Stark / Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Stark_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Tony Stark (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") alongside [Terrence Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrence_Howard "Terrence Howard"), [Jeff Bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Bridges "Jeff Bridges"), [Gwyneth Paltrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwyneth_Paltrow "Gwyneth Paltrow"), [Leslie Bibb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leslie_Bibb "Leslie Bibb"), and [Shaun Toub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Toub "Shaun Toub"). In the film, world-famous industrialist and master engineer Stark builds a [mechanized suit of armor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man's_armor_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Iron Man's armor (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") to escape from captivity by [a terrorist group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Rings_(organization) "Ten Rings (organization)"), and then uses the suit to become the superhero Iron Man.

A film featuring Iron Man was in development at [Universal Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures"), [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox"), and [New Line Cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Line_Cinema "New Line Cinema") at various times since 1990 before Marvel Studios reacquired the rights in 2005. Marvel put the project in production as its first self-financed film, with Paramount Pictures distributing. Favreau signed on as director in April 2006 and faced opposition from Marvel when trying to cast Downey in the title role; the actor was signed in September. Filming took place from March to June 2007, primarily in California to differentiate the film from numerous other superhero stories that are set in New York City. During filming, the actors were free to create their own dialogue because pre-production was focused on the story and action. Rubber and metal versions of the armor, created by [Stan Winston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Winston "Stan Winston")'s company, were mixed with [computer-generated imagery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-generated_imagery "Computer-generated imagery") to create the title character.

_Iron Man_ premiered in [Sydney, Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney,_Australia "Sydney, Australia"), on April 14, 2008, and was released in the United States on May 2 as the first film in [Phase One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe:_Phase_One "Marvel Cinematic Universe: Phase One") of the MCU. It was a commercial success, grossing over $585 million and becoming the [eighth-highest grossing film of 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2008 in film"). It also received positive reviews from critics, who praised Downey's performance and Favreau's balance of character development and special effects. _Iron Man_ was nominated for [Best Sound Editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Sound_Editing "Academy Award for Best Sound Editing") and [Best Visual Effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Visual_Effects "Academy Award for Best Visual Effects") at the [81st Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards"), among [numerous other accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accolades_received_by_Iron_Man_(2008_film) "List of accolades received by Iron Man (2008 film)"), and was named one of the ten best films of the year by the [American Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Film_Institute "American Film Institute"). In 2022, the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress") selected the film for preservation in the United States [National Film Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Registry "National Film Registry") for being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant". Two sequels have been released: _[Iron Man 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_2 "Iron Man 2")_ (2010) and _[Iron Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_3 "Iron Man 3")_ (2013).

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Iron_Man_(2008_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

[Tony Stark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Stark_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Tony Stark (Marvel Cinematic Universe)"), who has inherited the defense contractor [Stark Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stark_Industries_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Stark Industries (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") from his late father [Howard Stark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Stark_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Howard Stark (Marvel Cinematic Universe)"), tours in [war-torn Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Afghanistan_(2001%E2%80%932021) "War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)") with his best friend and military liaison, [James "Rhodey" Rhodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rhodes_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "James Rhodes (Marvel Cinematic Universe)"), to demonstrate the new "Jericho" missile. After the demonstration, his convoy is ambushed by a terrorist group, the [Ten Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Rings_(organization) "Ten Rings (organization)"), and Stark is gravely wounded by a missile used by the attackers—one of his company's own. He is captured and imprisoned in a cave by the Ten Rings. [Yinsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho_Yinsen_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Ho Yinsen (Marvel Cinematic Universe)"), a fellow captive and doctor, implants an electromagnet into Stark's chest to keep the shrapnel shards that wounded him from reaching his heart and killing him. Ten Rings leader [Raza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raza_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Raza (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") offers Stark freedom in exchange for building a Jericho missile for the group, but he and Yinsen believe that Raza will not keep his word.

Stark and Yinsen secretly build a small, powerful electric generator called an [arc reactor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arc_reactor_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Arc reactor (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") to power Stark's electromagnet and construct a prototype [armored suit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man's_armor_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Iron Man's armor (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") to aid in their escape. Although they keep the suit hidden, the Ten Rings discover their intentions and attack the workshop. Yinsen sacrifices himself to divert them while the suit powers up. The armored Stark battles his way out of the cave to find the dying Yinsen, then burns the Ten Rings' weapons and flies away, crashing in the desert and destroying the suit. After being rescued by Rhodes, Stark returns home and announces that his company will cease manufacturing weapons. [Obadiah Stane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obadiah_Stane_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Obadiah Stane (Marvel Cinematic Universe)"), his father's old partner and the company's manager, advises Stark that this will bankrupt Stark Industries and ruin his father's legacy. In his home workshop, Stark builds a sleeker, more powerful version of his improvised armor suit as well as a more powerful arc reactor for it and his chest after testing a prototype. Personal assistant [Pepper Potts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepper_Potts_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Pepper Potts (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") places the original reactor inside a small glass showcase. Though Stane requests details, a suspicious Stark decides to keep his work to himself.

At a charity event, reporter [Christine Everhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christine_Everhart_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Christine Everhart (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") informs Stark that his company's weapons were recently delivered to the Ten Rings and are being used to attack Yinsen's home village. Stark dons his new armor and flies to Afghanistan, where he fends off the terrorists and saves the villagers. While flying home, Stark is intercepted by the [Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") and reveals his secret identity to Rhodes over the phone to end the attack. Meanwhile, the Ten Rings gather the pieces of Stark's prototype suit and meet with Stane, who has been trafficking arms to the Ten Rings and has staged a [coup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coup "Coup") to replace Stark as Stark Industries' CEO by hiring the Ten Rings to kill him. He subdues Raza, has his group killed, and reverse-engineers a massive new armor suit from the wreckage. Seeking to track his company's illegal shipments, Stark sends Potts to hack into its database. She discovers that Stane hired the Ten Rings to kill Stark, but the group altered their plans when they realized they had a direct route to Stark's weapons. Potts meets with Agent [Phil Coulson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Coulson "Phil Coulson") of [S.H.I.E.L.D.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.H.I.E.L.D._(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "S.H.I.E.L.D. (Marvel Cinematic Universe)"), an intelligence agency, to inform him of Stane's activities.

Stane's scientists are unable to replicate Stark's miniaturized arc reactor, so Stane enters Stark's home, stuns Stark, and steals the one from his chest. Stark manages to replace it with his original reactor. Potts and several S.H.I.E.L.D. agents attempt to arrest Stane, but he dons his suit and overpowers them. Stark fights Stane but is outmatched without his new reactor to run his suit at full capacity. The fight carries Stark and Stane to the top of the Stark Industries building, where Stark instructs Potts to overload the large arc reactor powering the building. This unleashes a massive electrical surge that causes Stane to fall into the reactor, and he is killed in the explosion. The next day, at a press conference, Stark publicly admits to being the superhero the press has dubbed "Iron Man".

In a [post-credits scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-credits_scene "Post-credits scene"), S.H.I.E.L.D. director [Nick Fury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Fury_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Nick Fury (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") visits Stark at his home, telling him that he has become part of a "bigger universe", and that he wants to discuss the "[Avenger Initiative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers_Initiative_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Avengers Initiative (Marvel Cinematic Universe)")".

*   [Robert Downey Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Downey_Jr. "Robert Downey Jr.") as [Tony Stark / Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Stark_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Tony Stark (Marvel Cinematic Universe)"):   
An [industrialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrialist "Industrialist"), genius inventor, and playboy, he is CEO of [Stark Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stark_Industries "Stark Industries") and chief weapons manufacturer for the [U.S. military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._military "U.S. military"). Director [Jon Favreau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau "Jon Favreau") felt that Downey's past made him an appropriate choice for the part[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-DowneyUSAToday-6) and that the actor could not only make Stark a "likable asshole," but also portray an authentic emotional journey, once he had won over the audience.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-FavreauWonderCon2008-7) Favreau was also attracted to Downey because of his performance in _[Kiss Kiss Bang Bang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss\_Kiss\_Bang\_Bang "Kiss Kiss Bang Bang")_ (2005). Downey frequently spoke with that film's director, [Shane Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Black "Shane Black"), about the script and dialogue in _Iron Man_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-KissKissBangBang-8) Downey had an office next to Favreau during pre-production, which allowed him greater involvement in the screenwriting process,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-EmpireJuly2007-9) especially when it came to adding humor to the film.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-EmpireApril2008-10) Downey explained, "What I usually hate about these [superhero] movies [is] when suddenly the guy that you were digging turns into [Dudley Do-Right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dudley_Do-Right "Dudley Do-Right"), and then you're supposed to buy into all his 'Let's go do some good!' That [Eliot Ness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliot_Ness "Eliot Ness")-in-a-cape-type thing. What was really important to me was to not have him change so much that he's unrecognizable. When someone used to be a schmuck and they're not anymore, hopefully they still have a sense of humor."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-FavreauStarkQuote-11) To get into shape, Downey spent five days a week weight training and practiced martial arts,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-DowneyUSAToday-6) which he said benefited him because "it's hard not to have a personality meltdown ... after about several hours in that suit. I'm calling up every therapeutic moment I can think of to just get through the day."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-StarlogApr2008-12)
*   [Terrence Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrence_Howard "Terrence Howard") as [James "Rhodey" Rhodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rhodes_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "James Rhodes (Marvel Cinematic Universe)"):   
A friend of Stark's and the liaison between Stark Industries and the [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") in the department of acquisitions, specifically weapons development. Favreau cast Howard because he felt he could play [War Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_Machine "War Machine") in a sequel.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-trilogy-13) Howard prepared for the role by visiting [Nellis Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nellis_Air_Force_Base "Nellis Air Force Base") on March 16, 2007, where he ate with the pilots and observed [HH-60 Pave Hawk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HH-60_Pave_Hawk "HH-60 Pave Hawk") rescue helicopters and [F-22 Raptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-22_Raptor "F-22 Raptor").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-HowardNellis-14) While Rhodes is roguish in the comics after he meets Stark, his previous role as a disciplinarian creates a dynamic tension with Stark's character. He is unsure whether Stark's actions are acceptable. "Rhodey is completely disgusted with the way Tony has lived his life, but at a certain point he realizes that perhaps there is a different way," Howard said. "Whose life is the right way: Is it the strict military life, or the life of an independent?"[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-StarlogApr2008-12) Howard and his father are Iron Man fans, partly because Rhodes was one of the few black superheroes when Howard was a child.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-RhodesFirst-15) Howard admired Downey as an actor since the latter appeared in _[Weird Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weird\_Science\_(film) "Weird Science (film)")_ (1985); the two competed physically on set.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-HowardCompete-16) Howard signed a three-picture deal with Marvel Studios.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-HowardContract-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-MCUReignExcerpt-18)
*   [Jeff Bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Bridges "Jeff Bridges") as [Obadiah Stane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obadiah_Stane_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Obadiah Stane (Marvel Cinematic Universe)"):   
Stark's business second-in-command, mentor, and friend, who turns on him to take over the company, eventually building a giant exosuit to fight Stark. Bridges read the comics as a boy and liked Favreau's modern, realistic approach. He shaved his head, something he had wanted to do for some time, and grew a beard for the role. Bridges researched the [Book of Obadiah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Obadiah "Book of Obadiah"), and was surprised to learn retribution is a major theme in that book of the Bible, something that Stane represents.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-ProductionNotes-19) Many of Stane's scenes were cut to focus more on Stark, but the writers felt Bridges's performance allowed the application of "less is more" when editing the film.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_(2008_film)#cite_note-BridgesCut-20)
*   [Gwyneth Paltrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwyneth_Paltrow "Gwyneth Paltrow") as [Virginia "Pepper" Potts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepper_Potts_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Pepper Potts (Marvel Cinematic Universe)"):   
Stark's personal assistant and budding love interest. Paltrow asked Marvel to send her any comics they would consider relevant to her understanding of the character, whom she considered to be very smart, level-headed, and grounded. She said she liked "the fact that there's a sexuality that's not blatant."
