**Jonathan Kolia Favreau** ([/ˈ f æ v r oʊ/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_FAV-roh_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born October 19, 1966)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-EW.com-1) is an American actor and filmmaker. He has received numerous accolades including an [Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Awards "Emmy Awards") and two [Saturn Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Awards "Saturn Awards").

As an actor, Favreau has appeared in many films such as _[Rudy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy\_(film) "Rudy (film)")_ (1993), _[PCU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCU\_(film) "PCU (film)")_ (1994), _[Swingers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swingers\_(1996\_film) "Swingers (1996 film)")_ (1996), _[Very Bad Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Very\_Bad\_Things "Very Bad Things")_ (1998), _[Deep Impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep\_Impact\_(film) "Deep Impact (film)")_ (1998), _[The Replacements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Replacements\_(film) "The Replacements (film)")_ (2000), _[Daredevil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daredevil\_(film) "Daredevil (film)")_ (2003), _[Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wimbledon\_(film) "Wimbledon (film)")_ (2004), _[The Break-Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Break-Up "The Break-Up")_ (2006), _[Four Christmases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four\_Christmases "Four Christmases")_ (2008), _[Couples Retreat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couples\_Retreat "Couples Retreat")_ (2009), _[I Love You, Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Love\_You,\_Man "I Love You, Man")_ (2009), _[People Like Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_Like\_Us\_(2012\_film) "People Like Us (2012 film)")_ (2012), _[The Wolf of Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wolf\_of\_Wall\_Street\_(2013\_film) "The Wolf of Wall Street (2013 film)")_ (2013), and _[Chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chef\_(2014\_film) "Chef (2014 film)")_ (2014).

As a filmmaker, Favreau has been significantly involved with the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe"). He directed, produced, and appeared as [Happy Hogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_Hogan_(character) "Happy Hogan (character)") in the films _[Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_(2008\_film) "Iron Man (2008 film)")_ (2008) and _[Iron Man 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_2 "Iron Man 2")_ (2010). He also served as an executive producer or appeared as the character in the films _[The Avengers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Avengers\_(2012\_film) "The Avengers (2012 film)")_ (2012), _[Iron Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_3 "Iron Man 3")_ (2013), _[Avengers: Age of Ultron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Age\_of\_Ultron "Avengers: Age of Ultron")_ (2015), _[Spider-Man: Homecoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Homecoming "Spider-Man: Homecoming")_ (2017), _[Avengers: Infinity War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Infinity\_War "Avengers: Infinity War")_ (2018), _[Avengers: Endgame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Endgame "Avengers: Endgame")_ (2019), _[Spider-Man: Far From Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Far\_From\_Home "Spider-Man: Far From Home")_ (2019), _[Spider-Man: No Way Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_No\_Way\_Home "Spider-Man: No Way Home")_ (2021), and _[Deadpool & Wolverine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool\_&\_Wolverine "Deadpool & Wolverine")_ (2024).

He has also directed the films _[Elf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf\_(film) "Elf (film)")_ (2003), _[Zathura: A Space Adventure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zathura:\_A\_Space\_Adventure "Zathura: A Space Adventure")_ (2005), _[Cowboys & Aliens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboys\_&\_Aliens "Cowboys & Aliens")_ (2011), _[Chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chef\_(2014\_film) "Chef (2014 film)")_ (2014), _[The Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jungle\_Book\_(2016\_film) "The Jungle Book (2016 film)")_ (2016), _[The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King\_(2019\_film) "The Lion King (2019 film)")_ (2019), and _[The Mandalorian and Grogu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian\_and\_Grogu "The Mandalorian and Grogu")_ (2026). Favreau has been known for his work on the _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_ franchise with [Dave Filoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Filoni "Dave Filoni"), creating the [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") original series _[The Mandalorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian "The Mandalorian")_ (2019–2023), which Filoni helped develop, with both serving as executive producers. Alongside Filoni, he serves as an executive producer on all of the show's spin-off series, including _[The Book of Boba Fett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Book\_of\_Boba\_Fett "The Book of Boba Fett")_, _[Ahsoka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahsoka\_(TV\_series) "Ahsoka (TV series)")_, and _[Skeleton Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_Skeleton\_Crew "Star Wars: Skeleton Crew")_. He produces films under his production company banner, [Fairview Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairview_Portals "Fairview Portals"), and also presented the variety series _[Dinner for Five](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinner\_for\_Five "Dinner for Five")_ and the cooking series _[The Chef Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chef\_Show "The Chef Show")_.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Favreau was born in [Flushing, Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flushing,_Queens "Flushing, Queens"), New York, on October 19, 1966,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-EW.com-1) the only child of Madeleine, an elementary school teacher who died of [leukemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leukemia "Leukemia") in 1979, and Charles Favreau, a [special education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_education "Special education") teacher.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-2) His mother was [Ashkenazi Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jewish "Ashkenazi Jewish")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-5) and his father is a Catholic of [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italians "Italians") and [French-Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French-Canadian "French-Canadian") ancestry.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-8) Favreau dropped out of [Hebrew school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_school "Hebrew school") to pursue acting. However, following his mother's death, both sides of his family worked to ensure he had a [bar mitzvah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_and_Bat_Mitzvah "Bar and Bat Mitzvah") ceremony.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-9)

Favreau graduated from [The Bronx High School of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx_High_School_of_Science "The Bronx High School of Science"), a school for gifted students, in 1984[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-10) and attended [Queens College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_College,_New_York "Queens College, New York") from 1984 to 1987,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-qc-11) before dropping out. His friend from college, Mitchell Pollack, has said that Favreau went by the nickname "Johnny Hack" because of his abilities in the game [Hacky Sack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacky_Sack "Hacky Sack").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-12) He briefly worked for [Bear Stearns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear_Stearns "Bear Stearns") on [Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street "Wall Street") before returning to Queens College for a semester in early 1988. He dropped out of college for good (a few credits shy of completing his degree),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-qc-11) and moved to [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") in the summer of 1988 to pursue a career in comedy.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-13) He performed at several Chicago improvisational theaters, including the [ImprovOlympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ImprovOlympic "ImprovOlympic") and the [Improv Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Improv_Institute "Improv Institute").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-14)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 1992–2000: Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1992–2000: Early career")]

While in Chicago, Favreau landed his first film role alongside [Sean Astin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Astin "Sean Astin") as tutor D-Bob in the [sleeper hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeper_hit "Sleeper hit")_[Rudy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy\_(film) "Rudy (film)")_ (1993).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-15) Favreau met [Vince Vaughn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Vaughn "Vince Vaughn") – who played a small role in this film – during shooting. The next year, he appeared in the college film _[PCU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCU\_(film) "PCU (film)")_ alongside [Jeremy Piven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Piven "Jeremy Piven"), and the 1994 episode of _[Seinfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seinfeld "Seinfeld")_ titled "[The Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fire_(Seinfeld_episode) "The Fire (Seinfeld episode)")" as Eric the Clown.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-16)

Favreau then moved to Los Angeles, where he made his breakthrough in 1996 as an actor-screenwriter with the film _[Swingers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swingers\_(1996\_film) "Swingers (1996 film)")_, which was also Vaughn's breakthrough role as the character Trent Walker, a [foil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foil_(literature) "Foil (literature)") to Favreau's heartbroken Mike Peters.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-17) In 1997, he appeared on the television sitcom _[Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends "Friends")_, portraying Pete Becker – [Monica Geller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monica_Geller "Monica Geller")'s millionaire boyfriend who competes in the [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") (UFC) – for several episodes.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-18) Favreau made appearances in the sketch-comedy series, _[Tracey Takes On...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracey\_Takes\_On... "Tracey Takes On...")_ in both 1996 and 1997.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-19)

Favreau landed the role of Gus Partenza in _[Deep Impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep\_Impact\_(film) "Deep Impact (film)")_ (1998), and that same year rejoined Piven in _[Very Bad Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Very\_Bad\_Things "Very Bad Things")_ (1998).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-20) In 1999, he starred in the television film _[Rocky Marciano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky\_Marciano\_(film) "Rocky Marciano (film)")_, based on the life of world heavyweight champion, [Rocky Marciano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Marciano "Rocky Marciano").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-21) He later appeared in _[Love & Sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_&\_Sex "Love & Sex")_ (2000), co-starring [Famke Janssen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famke_Janssen "Famke Janssen").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-22) Favreau appeared in 2000's _[The Replacements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Replacements\_(film) "The Replacements (film)")_ as maniacal linebacker Daniel Bateman, and that same year he played himself in _[The Sopranos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sopranos "The Sopranos")_ episode ["D-Girl"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D-Girl_(The_Sopranos) "D-Girl (The Sopranos)"), as a Hollywood director who feigns interest in developing mob associate [Christopher Moltisanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Moltisanti "Christopher Moltisanti")'s screenplay in order to collect material for his own screenplay.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-24)

### 2001–2015: Actor–director

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2001–2015: Actor–director")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Jon_Favreau-2008.jpg/250px-Jon_Favreau-2008.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jon_Favreau-2008.jpg)

Favreau at an _[Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_(2008\_film) "Iron Man (2008 film)")_ photocall in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City") in 2008

In 2001, he made his film directorial debut with another self-penned screenplay, _[Made](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Made\_(2001\_film) "Made (2001 film)")_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-25)_Made_ once again teamed him up with his _Swingers_ co-star [Vince Vaughn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Vaughn "Vince Vaughn"). Favreau also starred in a TV series called _[Dinner for Five](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinner\_for\_Five "Dinner for Five")_, which aired on the cable TV channel [IFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Film_Channel "Independent Film Channel") from 2001 to 2005.

He was a guest-director for an episode of the college [dramedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dramedy "Dramedy")_[Undeclared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undeclared\_(TV\_show) "Undeclared (TV show)")_ in 2001, and Favreau got some screen time as lawyer [Foggy Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foggy_Nelson "Foggy Nelson") in the 2003 movie _[Daredevil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daredevil\_(film) "Daredevil (film)")_ (2003) (considerably more in the [director's cut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director's_cut "Director's cut") version).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-27) He also starred in _[The Big Empty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Big\_Empty\_(2003\_film) "The Big Empty (2003 film)")_ (2003), directed by [Steve Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Anderson_(director) "Steve Anderson (director)"). His character was John Person, an out of work actor given a strange mission to deliver a blue suitcase to a man named Cowboy in the desert.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-28) Favreau is credited as a screenwriter for the 2002 film _The First $20 Million Is Always the Hardest_.

He scored his first financial success as a director of the hit comedy _[Elf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf\_(film) "Elf (film)")_ (2003) starring [Will Ferrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Ferrell "Will Ferrell"), [Zooey Deschanel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooey_Deschanel "Zooey Deschanel"), [James Caan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Caan_(actor) "James Caan (actor)"), and [Peter Dinklage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Dinklage_(actor) "Peter Dinklage (actor)"). Also in 2003, Favreau had a small part in _[Something's Gotta Give](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Something's\_Gotta\_Give\_(film) "Something's Gotta Give (film)")_ (a film starring [Diane Keaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Keaton "Diane Keaton") and [Jack Nicholson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Nicholson "Jack Nicholson")); Favreau played Leo, Harry Sanborn's (Nicholson) personal assistant, who visited Harry in the hospital.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-29) In 2005, Favreau directed the [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zathura_(film) "Zathura (film)") of the children's book _[Zathura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zathura "Zathura")_. It received positive reviews, but was not commercially successful.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-31) Favreau continued to make regular appearances in film and television. He reunited with friend Vaughn in the romantic comedy _[The Break-Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Break-Up "The Break-Up")_ and appeared in _[My Name Is Earl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Name\_Is\_Earl "My Name Is Earl")_ as a reprehensible fast food manager. Favreau also made a guest appearance in Vaughn's _[Wild West Comedy Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild\_West\_Comedy\_Show:\_30\_Days\_&\_30\_Nights\_%E2%80%93\_Hollywood\_to\_the\_Heartland "Wild West Comedy Show: 30 Days & 30 Nights – Hollywood to the Heartland")_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-32)

Also in 2005, Favreau appeared as a guest judge and executive representative of Sony Corporation in week five of the [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") business-focused primetime reality TV show, _[The Apprentice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Apprentice\_(American\_TV\_series)\_season\_4#Week\_5:\_Lost\_in\_Space "The Apprentice (American TV series) season 4")_. He was called upon to judge the efforts of the show's two teams of contestants, who were assigned the task of designing and building a float to publicize his 2005 Sony Pictures movie, _[Zathura: A Space Adventure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zathura:\_A\_Space\_Adventure "Zathura: A Space Adventure")_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-33)

On April 28, 2006, it was announced that Favreau was signed to direct the long-awaited _[Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_(2008\_film) "Iron Man (2008 film)")_ movie.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-34) Released on May 2, 2008, the film was a huge critical[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-35) and commercial[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-36) success, solidifying Favreau's reputation as a director.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-37) In 2022, the film was selected for preservation in the United States [National Film Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Registry "National Film Registry") by the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress") as being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant". It is one of three superhero movies to achieve this honor alongside [Richard Donner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Donner "Richard Donner")'s _[Superman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman\_(1978\_film) "Superman (1978 film)")_ and [Christopher Nolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan "Christopher Nolan")'s _[The Dark Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_Knight "The Dark Knight")_. _Iron Man_ was the first [Marvel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics")-produced movie under their alliance with [Paramount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures"), and Favreau served as the director and an executive producer. During early scenes in _Iron Man,_ Favreau appears as Tony Stark's driver, [Happy Hogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_Hogan_(character) "Happy Hogan (character)"). He wrote two issues of a planned mini-series for [Marvel Knights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Knights "Marvel Knights") titled _Iron Man: Viva Las Vegas_, that debuted in September 2008 before being canceled in November 2008. Favreau also directed and executive produced the film's sequel, _[Iron Man 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_2 "Iron Man 2")_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-38) Favreau said in December 2010 that he would not direct _[Iron Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_3 "Iron Man 3")_ but remain an executive producer.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-39)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Favreau.png/250px-Favreau.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Favreau.png)

Favreau with Robert McCurdy, Cole Dabney, [Jaime Pressly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaime_Pressly "Jaime Pressly") after press junket interview for _[I Love You, Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Love\_You,\_Man "I Love You, Man")_ at [SXSW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SXSW "SXSW") 2009

Favreau was the third director attached to _[John Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John\_Carter\_(film) "John Carter (film)")_, the film adaptation of [Edgar Rice Burroughs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Rice_Burroughs "Edgar Rice Burroughs")' swashbuckling [space hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carter_of_Mars "John Carter of Mars"). While he did not ultimately direct it, he did appear in a cameo in the film, as a bookie.

In 2008, he played Denver, a bully-type bigger brother to Vaughn in _[Four Christmases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four\_Christmases "Four Christmases")._ Favreau co-starred in 2009's _[Couples Retreat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couples\_Retreat "Couples Retreat")_, a comedy chronicling four couples who partake in therapy sessions at a tropical island resort, which he wrote. The film saw him co-star with Vaughn again, while [Kristin Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristin_Davis "Kristin Davis") played his wife.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-40) He voices the character Pre Vizsla, the leader of the Mandalorian Death Watch, in the animated series, _[Star Wars: The Clone Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Clone\_Wars "Star Wars: The Clone Wars")_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-41) In September 2009, he signed up to direct _[Cowboys & Aliens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboys\_&\_Aliens "Cowboys & Aliens")_ based on the [graphic novel of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboys_&_Aliens_(comics) "Cowboys & Aliens (comics)") created by [Scott Mitchell Rosenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Mitchell_Rosenberg "Scott Mitchell Rosenberg").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-42) The [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_film "Science fiction film")[Western film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_film "Western film") was released in 2011, starring [Daniel Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Craig "Daniel Craig") and [Harrison Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford "Harrison Ford"), and is considered to be a financial disappointment, taking $174.8 million in box office receipts on a $163 million budget and received mixed reviews, with critics generally praising its acting while criticizing other aspects.

In 2012, Favreau directed the pilot for the NBC show, _[Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolution\_(TV\_series) "Revolution (TV series)"),_ and served as one of the show's executive producers, alongside [J. J. Abrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._J._Abrams "J. J. Abrams").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-43) In 2013, Favreau directed an episode (Season 9, Episode 16) of NBC's [_The Office_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Office_(American_TV_series) "The Office (American TV series)").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-44) That same year he filmed a pilot for a TV series based on the novel _[About a Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/About\_a\_Boy\_(novel) "About a Boy (novel)")_, but set in San Francisco.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-45) He also directed the _[Destiny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny\_(game) "Destiny (game)")_ trailer "The Law of the Jungle".

In 2014, Favreau wrote, co-produced, directed, and starred in _[Chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chef\_(2014\_film) "Chef (2014 film)")_. Favreau played a chef who, after a public altercation with a food critic, quits his job at a popular Los Angeles restaurant to operate a [food truck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_truck "Food truck") with his young son. It co-stars [Sofía Vergara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sof%C3%ADa_Vergara "Sofía Vergara"), [John Leguizamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Leguizamo "John Leguizamo"), [Scarlett Johansson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarlett_Johansson "Scarlett Johansson"), [Oliver Platt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Platt "Oliver Platt"), [Bobby Cannavale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Cannavale "Bobby Cannavale") and [Dustin Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dustin_Hoffman "Dustin Hoffman"), along with [Robert Downey Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Downey_Jr. "Robert Downey Jr.") in a cameo role. Favreau wrote the script after directing several big-budget films, wanting to go "back to basics" and to create a film about cooking. It was well received by critics, who praised the direction, music, writing, story, and performances grossing $45 million against a production budget of $11 million.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-46)

### 2016–present: Franchise work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2016–present: Franchise work")]

Favreau directed and produced the live-action adaptation of _[The Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jungle\_Book\_(2016\_film) "The Jungle Book (2016 film)")_, for [Walt Disney Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Pictures "Walt Disney Pictures"), which was released on April 15, 2016, to critical and commercial acclaim.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-47) That same year, it was reported that Favreau would direct a [CGI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-generated_imagery "Computer-generated imagery") adaptation of [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company")'s _[The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King\_(2019\_film) "The Lion King (2019 film)")_,[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-LionKing-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-49) marking his first time directing a musical.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-LionKing-48)[Donald Glover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Glover "Donald Glover") voiced Simba,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-50) and [James Earl Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Earl_Jones "James Earl Jones") reprised his role as Mufasa from the [original film.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lion_King "The Lion King")[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-51) The film was released in July 2019. On July 29, _The Lion King_ surpassed _The Jungle Book_ to become Favreau's highest-grossing film as director, while also surpassing the original film.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-52) Simultaneous with his directorial projects, he worked as a consultant on 24 episodes of _[The Orville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Orville "The Orville")_ from 2017 to 2019.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-53)

He returned as [Happy Hogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_Hogan_(character) "Happy Hogan (character)") in the film _[Spider-Man: Homecoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Homecoming "Spider-Man: Homecoming")_ (2017), and co-executive produced _[Avengers: Infinity War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Infinity\_War "Avengers: Infinity War")_ (2018). Favreau filmed a scene for _Avengers: Infinity War_, but was cut, ending up on the Blu-Ray release. In 2017, Favreau directed the pilot episode of [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS")' _[Young Sheldon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Sheldon "Young Sheldon")_.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-54) On March 8, 2018, Lucasfilm announced that Favreau would executive produce and write a live-action _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_ television series, titled _[The Mandalorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian "The Mandalorian")_, for [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-56) The series premiered on November 12, 2019, alongside the streaming service and was co-produced by Favreau's production company [Golem Creations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golem_Creations "Golem Creations"). Jon Favreau also lent his voice to the character of Paz Vizsla, who was portrayed by Tait Fletcher.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-57)

During that same year, Favreau appeared in _[Solo: A Star Wars Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solo:\_A\_Star\_Wars\_Story "Solo: A Star Wars Story")_ voicing Rio Durant, "a very cool and important alien character" and member of Beckett's crew.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-58) In the 2019 film _[Avengers: Endgame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Endgame "Avengers: Endgame")_, Favreau reprised his role as Happy Hogan in a cameo near the end of the film. The film, directed by the [Russo brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo_brothers "Russo brothers"),[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-FavreauPaltrowAvengers4-59) was executive-produced by Favreau.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-60)_Avengers: Endgame_ was released on April 26, 2019. In 2019, Favreau also appeared in the sequel to _[Spider-Man: Homecoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Homecoming "Spider-Man: Homecoming")_, _[Spider-Man: Far From Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Far\_From\_Home "Spider-Man: Far From Home")_.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-61)

In May of the same year, it was also announced that Favreau would co-host and executive produce a cooking show for [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") along with co-host [Roy Choi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Choi "Roy Choi"), called _[The Chef Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chef\_Show "The Chef Show")_. It premiered in June 2019.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-62) In December 2021 and July 2024, Favreau reprised his role as Happy Hogan in _[Spider-Man: No Way Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_No\_Way\_Home "Spider-Man: No Way Home")_ and _[Deadpool & Wolverine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool\_&\_Wolverine "Deadpool & Wolverine")_. In May 2022, Favreau produced the documentary series _[Prehistoric Planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistoric\_Planet\_(2022\_TV\_series) "Prehistoric Planet (2022 TV series)")_ alongside the [BBC Studios Natural History Unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Studios_Natural_History_Unit "BBC Studios Natural History Unit") for [Apple TV+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_TV+ "Apple TV+").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-63)

In January 2024, [Lucasfilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucasfilm "Lucasfilm") announced that a feature film titled _[The Mandalorian and Grogu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian\_and\_Grogu "The Mandalorian and Grogu")_ was in active development, with Favreau directing, writing, and co-producing alongside [Kathleen Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathleen_Kennedy_(producer) "Kathleen Kennedy (producer)") and [Dave Filoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Filoni "Dave Filoni").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-64) The film released on May 22 2026.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-65)

In March 2025, it was reported that Favreau was developing a [live-action animation hybrid series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswald_(2027_TV_series) "Oswald (2027 TV series)") based on _[Oswald the Lucky Rabbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswald\_the\_Lucky\_Rabbit "Oswald the Lucky Rabbit")_ for Disney+ as writer and producer.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-66)

## Unreleased projects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Unreleased projects")]

In 1997, Favreau was working on a [Miramax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miramax "Miramax") project _The Marshal of Revelation_, an offbeat [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_film "Western film") featuring "a [Hasidic Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasidic_Jew "Hasidic Jew") gunslinger."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-67)

A [motion-captured](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_capture "Motion capture") animated film titled _Neanderthals_[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-68) was in development at [Sony Pictures Animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Pictures_Animation "Sony Pictures Animation") in the mid-2000s that Favreau would have written and produced, but the project was cancelled sometime in 2008[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-69) after four years in development.

In November 2010, it was reported that Favreau would direct a film titled _Magic Kingdom_, based on [The Walt Disney Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company")'s theme park [of the same name.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_Kingdom "Magic Kingdom")[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-70) In July 2012, Favreau reported that he was officially working on the film.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-72) In 2014, he stated that he still had interest in the project, and that he could direct it after finishing filming _[The Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jungle\_Book\_(2016\_film) "The Jungle Book (2016 film)")_ (2016).[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-73)

In October 2012, Favreau was attached to direct the racing film _Battle for Bonneville_ about the story of [Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Arfons "Art Arfons") and [Walt Arfons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Arfons "Walt Arfons"), with [Ryan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Reynolds "Ryan Reynolds") set to star as one of the leads. [New Regency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Regency "New Regency") was in negotiations to acquire the package. The script was written by [Dan Gilroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Gilroy "Dan Gilroy"). Favreau also was additionally developing to direct _[Jersey Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey\_Boys\_(film) "Jersey Boys (film)")_ at the time, and wanted to follow it with _Battle for Bonneville_.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-74)

In November 2012, it was said that Favreau – along with [David Fincher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Fincher "David Fincher"), [Brad Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Bird "Brad Bird"), [Matthew Vaughn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Vaughn "Matthew Vaughn") and [Ben Affleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck "Ben Affleck") – was being considered to direct _[Star Wars: The Force Awakens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Force\_Awakens "Star Wars: The Force Awakens")_, but the choice fell on [J. J. Abrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._J._Abrams "J. J. Abrams").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-75) In June 2015, Favreau stated that although he would not be working on the [_Star Wars_ anthology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars "Star Wars") films, he could work on future _Star Wars_ movies at some point.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-76) Favreau later worked with the franchise on the live action series _[The Mandalorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian "The Mandalorian")_.

In December 2013, [Will Ferrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Ferrell "Will Ferrell") stated that he did not want to make a sequel to _[Elf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf\_(film) "Elf (film)")_.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-77) Despite this, during an interview in January 2016, Favreau stated that a sequel could possibly be made.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-78) The next month however, Ferrell reiterated that it was unlikely that the sequel would happen and that he still did not want to return to the role.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-79)

In April 2016, it was reported that Favreau would return to direct [the sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Jungle_Book_(2016_film)#Future "The Jungle Book (2016 film)") to his critically acclaimed live-action adaptation of _[The Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jungle\_Book\_(1967\_film) "The Jungle Book (1967 film)")_.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-81) Early pre-production of the sequel had begun by June 12, 2018, with [Justin Marks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Marks_(writer) "Justin Marks (writer)"), who wrote the previous film, having written an early draft for the film.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-JungleBook2Unusued-82)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Favreau married Joya Tillem, a physician, on November 24, 2000.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-83) The couple have a son and two daughters.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-84) Tillem is the niece of lawyer/talk show host [Len Tillem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Len_Tillem "Len Tillem").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-85)

Favreau credits the role-playing game _[Dungeons & Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungeons\_&\_Dragons "Dungeons & Dragons")_ with giving him "a really strong background in imagination, storytelling, understanding how to create tone and a sense of balance."[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-86)

## Golem Creations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Golem Creations")]

Golem Creations Ltd. LLC is a television [production company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Production_company "Production company") created by Jon Favreau on August 30, 2018.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-CABR-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-THR_Interview-88) In an interview with _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_, Favreau cited his fascination with the overlap of technology and storytelling and that he gave the company its name because a [golem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golem "Golem") was like technology; it could be used to protect or destroy if control was lost of it.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-THR_Interview-88) The company most recently produced _[The Mandalorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian "The Mandalorian")_, _[The Book of Boba Fett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Book\_of\_Boba\_Fett "The Book of Boba Fett")_, _[Ahsoka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahsoka\_(TV\_series) "Ahsoka (TV series)")_, and _[Star Wars: Skeleton Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_Skeleton\_Crew "Star Wars: Skeleton Crew")_ television shows, in partnership with [Lucasfilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucasfilm "Lucasfilm"), and the [Apple TV+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_TV+ "Apple TV+") documentary series _[Prehistoric Planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistoric\_Planet "Prehistoric Planet")_.

**Jonathan Kolia Favreau** ([/ˈ f æ v r oʊ/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_FAV-roh_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born October 19, 1966)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-EW.com-1) is an American actor and filmmaker. He has received numerous accolades including an [Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Awards "Emmy Awards") and two [Saturn Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Awards "Saturn Awards").

As an actor, Favreau has appeared in many films such as _[Rudy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy\_(film) "Rudy (film)")_ (1993), _[PCU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCU\_(film) "PCU (film)")_ (1994), _[Swingers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swingers\_(1996\_film) "Swingers (1996 film)")_ (1996), _[Very Bad Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Very\_Bad\_Things "Very Bad Things")_ (1998), _[Deep Impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep\_Impact\_(film) "Deep Impact (film)")_ (1998), _[The Replacements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Replacements\_(film) "The Replacements (film)")_ (2000), _[Daredevil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daredevil\_(film) "Daredevil (film)")_ (2003), _[Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wimbledon\_(film) "Wimbledon (film)")_ (2004), _[The Break-Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Break-Up "The Break-Up")_ (2006), _[Four Christmases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four\_Christmases "Four Christmases")_ (2008), _[Couples Retreat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couples\_Retreat "Couples Retreat")_ (2009), _[I Love You, Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Love\_You,\_Man "I Love You, Man")_ (2009), _[People Like Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_Like\_Us\_(2012\_film) "People Like Us (2012 film)")_ (2012), _[The Wolf of Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wolf\_of\_Wall\_Street\_(2013\_film) "The Wolf of Wall Street (2013 film)")_ (2013), and _[Chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chef\_(2014\_film) "Chef (2014 film)")_ (2014).

As a filmmaker, Favreau has been significantly involved with the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe"). He directed, produced, and appeared as [Happy Hogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_Hogan_(character) "Happy Hogan (character)") in the films _[Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_(2008\_film) "Iron Man (2008 film)")_ (2008) and _[Iron Man 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_2 "Iron Man 2")_ (2010). He also served as an executive producer or appeared as the character in the films _[The Avengers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Avengers\_(2012\_film) "The Avengers (2012 film)")_ (2012), _[Iron Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_3 "Iron Man 3")_ (2013), _[Avengers: Age of Ultron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Age\_of\_Ultron "Avengers: Age of Ultron")_ (2015), _[Spider-Man: Homecoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Homecoming "Spider-Man: Homecoming")_ (2017), _[Avengers: Infinity War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Infinity\_War "Avengers: Infinity War")_ (2018), _[Avengers: Endgame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Endgame "Avengers: Endgame")_ (2019), _[Spider-Man: Far From Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Far\_From\_Home "Spider-Man: Far From Home")_ (2019), _[Spider-Man: No Way Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_No\_Way\_Home "Spider-Man: No Way Home")_ (2021), and _[Deadpool & Wolverine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool\_&\_Wolverine "Deadpool & Wolverine")_ (2024).

He has also directed the films _[Elf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf\_(film) "Elf (film)")_ (2003), _[Zathura: A Space Adventure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zathura:\_A\_Space\_Adventure "Zathura: A Space Adventure")_ (2005), _[Cowboys & Aliens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboys\_&\_Aliens "Cowboys & Aliens")_ (2011), _[Chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chef\_(2014\_film) "Chef (2014 film)")_ (2014), _[The Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jungle\_Book\_(2016\_film) "The Jungle Book (2016 film)")_ (2016), _[The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King\_(2019\_film) "The Lion King (2019 film)")_ (2019), and _[The Mandalorian and Grogu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian\_and\_Grogu "The Mandalorian and Grogu")_ (2026). Favreau has been known for his work on the _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_ franchise with [Dave Filoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Filoni "Dave Filoni"), creating the [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") original series _[The Mandalorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian "The Mandalorian")_ (2019–2023), which Filoni helped develop, with both serving as executive producers. Alongside Filoni, he serves as an executive producer on all of the show's spin-off series, including _[The Book of Boba Fett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Book\_of\_Boba\_Fett "The Book of Boba Fett")_, _[Ahsoka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahsoka\_(TV\_series) "Ahsoka (TV series)")_, and _[Skeleton Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_Skeleton\_Crew "Star Wars: Skeleton Crew")_. He produces films under his production company banner, [Fairview Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairview_Portals "Fairview Portals"), and also presented the variety series _[Dinner for Five](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinner\_for\_Five "Dinner for Five")_ and the cooking series _[The Chef Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chef\_Show "The Chef Show")_.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Favreau was born in [Flushing, Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flushing,_Queens "Flushing, Queens"), New York, on October 19, 1966,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-EW.com-1) the only child of Madeleine, an elementary school teacher who died of [leukemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leukemia "Leukemia") in 1979, and Charles Favreau, a [special education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_education "Special education") teacher.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-2) His mother was [Ashkenazi Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jewish "Ashkenazi Jewish")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-5) and his father is a Catholic of [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italians "Italians") and [French-Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French-Canadian "French-Canadian") ancestry.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-8) Favreau dropped out of [Hebrew school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_school "Hebrew school") to pursue acting. However, following his mother's death, both sides of his family worked to ensure he had a [bar mitzvah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_and_Bat_Mitzvah "Bar and Bat Mitzvah") ceremony.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-9)

Favreau graduated from [The Bronx High School of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx_High_School_of_Science "The Bronx High School of Science"), a school for gifted students, in 1984[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-10) and attended [Queens College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_College,_New_York "Queens College, New York") from 1984 to 1987,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-qc-11) before dropping out. His friend from college, Mitchell Pollack, has said that Favreau went by the nickname "Johnny Hack" because of his abilities in the game [Hacky Sack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacky_Sack "Hacky Sack").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-12) He briefly worked for [Bear Stearns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear_Stearns "Bear Stearns") on [Wall Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street "Wall Street") before returning to Queens College for a semester in early 1988. He dropped out of college for good (a few credits shy of completing his degree),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-qc-11) and moved to [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") in the summer of 1988 to pursue a career in comedy.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-13) He performed at several Chicago improvisational theaters, including the [ImprovOlympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ImprovOlympic "ImprovOlympic") and the [Improv Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Improv_Institute "Improv Institute").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-14)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 1992–2000: Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1992–2000: Early career")]

While in Chicago, Favreau landed his first film role alongside [Sean Astin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Astin "Sean Astin") as tutor D-Bob in the [sleeper hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeper_hit "Sleeper hit")_[Rudy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudy\_(film) "Rudy (film)")_ (1993).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-15) Favreau met [Vince Vaughn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Vaughn "Vince Vaughn") – who played a small role in this film – during shooting. The next year, he appeared in the college film _[PCU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCU\_(film) "PCU (film)")_ alongside [Jeremy Piven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Piven "Jeremy Piven"), and the 1994 episode of _[Seinfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seinfeld "Seinfeld")_ titled "[The Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fire_(Seinfeld_episode) "The Fire (Seinfeld episode)")" as Eric the Clown.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-16)

Favreau then moved to Los Angeles, where he made his breakthrough in 1996 as an actor-screenwriter with the film _[Swingers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swingers\_(1996\_film) "Swingers (1996 film)")_, which was also Vaughn's breakthrough role as the character Trent Walker, a [foil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foil_(literature) "Foil (literature)") to Favreau's heartbroken Mike Peters.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-17) In 1997, he appeared on the television sitcom _[Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends "Friends")_, portraying Pete Becker – [Monica Geller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monica_Geller "Monica Geller")'s millionaire boyfriend who competes in the [Ultimate Fighting Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") (UFC) – for several episodes.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-18) Favreau made appearances in the sketch-comedy series, _[Tracey Takes On...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracey\_Takes\_On... "Tracey Takes On...")_ in both 1996 and 1997.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-19)

Favreau landed the role of Gus Partenza in _[Deep Impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep\_Impact\_(film) "Deep Impact (film)")_ (1998), and that same year rejoined Piven in _[Very Bad Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Very\_Bad\_Things "Very Bad Things")_ (1998).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-20) In 1999, he starred in the television film _[Rocky Marciano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky\_Marciano\_(film) "Rocky Marciano (film)")_, based on the life of world heavyweight champion, [Rocky Marciano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Marciano "Rocky Marciano").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-21) He later appeared in _[Love & Sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_&\_Sex "Love & Sex")_ (2000), co-starring [Famke Janssen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famke_Janssen "Famke Janssen").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-22) Favreau appeared in 2000's _[The Replacements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Replacements\_(film) "The Replacements (film)")_ as maniacal linebacker Daniel Bateman, and that same year he played himself in _[The Sopranos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sopranos "The Sopranos")_ episode ["D-Girl"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D-Girl_(The_Sopranos) "D-Girl (The Sopranos)"), as a Hollywood director who feigns interest in developing mob associate [Christopher Moltisanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Moltisanti "Christopher Moltisanti")'s screenplay in order to collect material for his own screenplay.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-24)

### 2001–2015: Actor–director

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2001–2015: Actor–director")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Jon_Favreau-2008.jpg/250px-Jon_Favreau-2008.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jon_Favreau-2008.jpg)

Favreau at an _[Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_(2008\_film) "Iron Man (2008 film)")_ photocall in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City") in 2008

In 2001, he made his film directorial debut with another self-penned screenplay, _[Made](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Made\_(2001\_film) "Made (2001 film)")_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-25)_Made_ once again teamed him up with his _Swingers_ co-star [Vince Vaughn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Vaughn "Vince Vaughn"). Favreau also starred in a TV series called _[Dinner for Five](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinner\_for\_Five "Dinner for Five")_, which aired on the cable TV channel [IFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Film_Channel "Independent Film Channel") from 2001 to 2005.

He was a guest-director for an episode of the college [dramedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dramedy "Dramedy")_[Undeclared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undeclared\_(TV\_show) "Undeclared (TV show)")_ in 2001, and Favreau got some screen time as lawyer [Foggy Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foggy_Nelson "Foggy Nelson") in the 2003 movie _[Daredevil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daredevil\_(film) "Daredevil (film)")_ (2003) (considerably more in the [director's cut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director's_cut "Director's cut") version).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-27) He also starred in _[The Big Empty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Big\_Empty\_(2003\_film) "The Big Empty (2003 film)")_ (2003), directed by [Steve Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Anderson_(director) "Steve Anderson (director)"). His character was John Person, an out of work actor given a strange mission to deliver a blue suitcase to a man named Cowboy in the desert.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-28) Favreau is credited as a screenwriter for the 2002 film _The First $20 Million Is Always the Hardest_.

He scored his first financial success as a director of the hit comedy _[Elf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf\_(film) "Elf (film)")_ (2003) starring [Will Ferrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Ferrell "Will Ferrell"), [Zooey Deschanel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooey_Deschanel "Zooey Deschanel"), [James Caan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Caan_(actor) "James Caan (actor)"), and [Peter Dinklage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Dinklage_(actor) "Peter Dinklage (actor)"). Also in 2003, Favreau had a small part in _[Something's Gotta Give](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Something's\_Gotta\_Give\_(film) "Something's Gotta Give (film)")_ (a film starring [Diane Keaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Keaton "Diane Keaton") and [Jack Nicholson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Nicholson "Jack Nicholson")); Favreau played Leo, Harry Sanborn's (Nicholson) personal assistant, who visited Harry in the hospital.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-29) In 2005, Favreau directed the [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zathura_(film) "Zathura (film)") of the children's book _[Zathura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zathura "Zathura")_. It received positive reviews, but was not commercially successful.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-31) Favreau continued to make regular appearances in film and television. He reunited with friend Vaughn in the romantic comedy _[The Break-Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Break-Up "The Break-Up")_ and appeared in _[My Name Is Earl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Name\_Is\_Earl "My Name Is Earl")_ as a reprehensible fast food manager. Favreau also made a guest appearance in Vaughn's _[Wild West Comedy Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild\_West\_Comedy\_Show:\_30\_Days\_&\_30\_Nights\_%E2%80%93\_Hollywood\_to\_the\_Heartland "Wild West Comedy Show: 30 Days & 30 Nights – Hollywood to the Heartland")_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-32)

Also in 2005, Favreau appeared as a guest judge and executive representative of Sony Corporation in week five of the [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") business-focused primetime reality TV show, _[The Apprentice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Apprentice\_(American\_TV\_series)\_season\_4#Week\_5:\_Lost\_in\_Space "The Apprentice (American TV series) season 4")_. He was called upon to judge the efforts of the show's two teams of contestants, who were assigned the task of designing and building a float to publicize his 2005 Sony Pictures movie, _[Zathura: A Space Adventure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zathura:\_A\_Space\_Adventure "Zathura: A Space Adventure")_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-33)

On April 28, 2006, it was announced that Favreau was signed to direct the long-awaited _[Iron Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_(2008\_film) "Iron Man (2008 film)")_ movie.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-34) Released on May 2, 2008, the film was a huge critical[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-35) and commercial[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-36) success, solidifying Favreau's reputation as a director.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-37) In 2022, the film was selected for preservation in the United States [National Film Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Registry "National Film Registry") by the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress") as being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant". It is one of three superhero movies to achieve this honor alongside [Richard Donner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Donner "Richard Donner")'s _[Superman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman\_(1978\_film) "Superman (1978 film)")_ and [Christopher Nolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan "Christopher Nolan")'s _[The Dark Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_Knight "The Dark Knight")_. _Iron Man_ was the first [Marvel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics")-produced movie under their alliance with [Paramount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures"), and Favreau served as the director and an executive producer. During early scenes in _Iron Man,_ Favreau appears as Tony Stark's driver, [Happy Hogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_Hogan_(character) "Happy Hogan (character)"). He wrote two issues of a planned mini-series for [Marvel Knights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Knights "Marvel Knights") titled _Iron Man: Viva Las Vegas_, that debuted in September 2008 before being canceled in November 2008. Favreau also directed and executive produced the film's sequel, _[Iron Man 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_2 "Iron Man 2")_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-38) Favreau said in December 2010 that he would not direct _[Iron Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Man\_3 "Iron Man 3")_ but remain an executive producer.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-39)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Favreau.png/250px-Favreau.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Favreau.png)

Favreau with Robert McCurdy, Cole Dabney, [Jaime Pressly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaime_Pressly "Jaime Pressly") after press junket interview for _[I Love You, Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Love\_You,\_Man "I Love You, Man")_ at [SXSW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SXSW "SXSW") 2009

Favreau was the third director attached to _[John Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John\_Carter\_(film) "John Carter (film)")_, the film adaptation of [Edgar Rice Burroughs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Rice_Burroughs "Edgar Rice Burroughs")' swashbuckling [space hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carter_of_Mars "John Carter of Mars"). While he did not ultimately direct it, he did appear in a cameo in the film, as a bookie.

In 2008, he played Denver, a bully-type bigger brother to Vaughn in _[Four Christmases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four\_Christmases "Four Christmases")._ Favreau co-starred in 2009's _[Couples Retreat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couples\_Retreat "Couples Retreat")_, a comedy chronicling four couples who partake in therapy sessions at a tropical island resort, which he wrote. The film saw him co-star with Vaughn again, while [Kristin Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristin_Davis "Kristin Davis") played his wife.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-40) He voices the character Pre Vizsla, the leader of the Mandalorian Death Watch, in the animated series, _[Star Wars: The Clone Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Clone\_Wars "Star Wars: The Clone Wars")_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-41) In September 2009, he signed up to direct _[Cowboys & Aliens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboys\_&\_Aliens "Cowboys & Aliens")_ based on the [graphic novel of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboys_&_Aliens_(comics) "Cowboys & Aliens (comics)") created by [Scott Mitchell Rosenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Mitchell_Rosenberg "Scott Mitchell Rosenberg").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-42) The [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_film "Science fiction film")[Western film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_film "Western film") was released in 2011, starring [Daniel Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Craig "Daniel Craig") and [Harrison Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford "Harrison Ford"), and is considered to be a financial disappointment, taking $174.8 million in box office receipts on a $163 million budget and received mixed reviews, with critics generally praising its acting while criticizing other aspects.

In 2012, Favreau directed the pilot for the NBC show, _[Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolution\_(TV\_series) "Revolution (TV series)"),_ and served as one of the show's executive producers, alongside [J. J. Abrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._J._Abrams "J. J. Abrams").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-43) In 2013, Favreau directed an episode (Season 9, Episode 16) of NBC's [_The Office_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Office_(American_TV_series) "The Office (American TV series)").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-44) That same year he filmed a pilot for a TV series based on the novel _[About a Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/About\_a\_Boy\_(novel) "About a Boy (novel)")_, but set in San Francisco.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-45) He also directed the _[Destiny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny\_(game) "Destiny (game)")_ trailer "The Law of the Jungle".

In 2014, Favreau wrote, co-produced, directed, and starred in _[Chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chef\_(2014\_film) "Chef (2014 film)")_. Favreau played a chef who, after a public altercation with a food critic, quits his job at a popular Los Angeles restaurant to operate a [food truck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_truck "Food truck") with his young son. It co-stars [Sofía Vergara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sof%C3%ADa_Vergara "Sofía Vergara"), [John Leguizamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Leguizamo "John Leguizamo"), [Scarlett Johansson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarlett_Johansson "Scarlett Johansson"), [Oliver Platt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Platt "Oliver Platt"), [Bobby Cannavale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Cannavale "Bobby Cannavale") and [Dustin Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dustin_Hoffman "Dustin Hoffman"), along with [Robert Downey Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Downey_Jr. "Robert Downey Jr.") in a cameo role. Favreau wrote the script after directing several big-budget films, wanting to go "back to basics" and to create a film about cooking. It was well received by critics, who praised the direction, music, writing, story, and performances grossing $45 million against a production budget of $11 million.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-46)

### 2016–present: Franchise work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2016–present: Franchise work")]

Favreau directed and produced the live-action adaptation of _[The Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jungle\_Book\_(2016\_film) "The Jungle Book (2016 film)")_, for [Walt Disney Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Pictures "Walt Disney Pictures"), which was released on April 15, 2016, to critical and commercial acclaim.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-47) That same year, it was reported that Favreau would direct a [CGI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-generated_imagery "Computer-generated imagery") adaptation of [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company")'s _[The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King\_(2019\_film) "The Lion King (2019 film)")_,[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-LionKing-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-49) marking his first time directing a musical.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-LionKing-48)[Donald Glover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Glover "Donald Glover") voiced Simba,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-50) and [James Earl Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Earl_Jones "James Earl Jones") reprised his role as Mufasa from the [original film.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lion_King "The Lion King")[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-51) The film was released in July 2019. On July 29, _The Lion King_ surpassed _The Jungle Book_ to become Favreau's highest-grossing film as director, while also surpassing the original film.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-52) Simultaneous with his directorial projects, he worked as a consultant on 24 episodes of _[The Orville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Orville "The Orville")_ from 2017 to 2019.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-53)

He returned as [Happy Hogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_Hogan_(character) "Happy Hogan (character)") in the film _[Spider-Man: Homecoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Homecoming "Spider-Man: Homecoming")_ (2017), and co-executive produced _[Avengers: Infinity War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Infinity\_War "Avengers: Infinity War")_ (2018). Favreau filmed a scene for _Avengers: Infinity War_, but was cut, ending up on the Blu-Ray release. In 2017, Favreau directed the pilot episode of [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS")' _[Young Sheldon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Sheldon "Young Sheldon")_.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-54) On March 8, 2018, Lucasfilm announced that Favreau would executive produce and write a live-action _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_ television series, titled _[The Mandalorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian "The Mandalorian")_, for [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-56) The series premiered on November 12, 2019, alongside the streaming service and was co-produced by Favreau's production company [Golem Creations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golem_Creations "Golem Creations"). Jon Favreau also lent his voice to the character of Paz Vizsla, who was portrayed by Tait Fletcher.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-57)

During that same year, Favreau appeared in _[Solo: A Star Wars Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solo:\_A\_Star\_Wars\_Story "Solo: A Star Wars Story")_ voicing Rio Durant, "a very cool and important alien character" and member of Beckett's crew.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-58) In the 2019 film _[Avengers: Endgame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avengers:\_Endgame "Avengers: Endgame")_, Favreau reprised his role as Happy Hogan in a cameo near the end of the film. The film, directed by the [Russo brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo_brothers "Russo brothers"),[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-FavreauPaltrowAvengers4-59) was executive-produced by Favreau.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-60)_Avengers: Endgame_ was released on April 26, 2019. In 2019, Favreau also appeared in the sequel to _[Spider-Man: Homecoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Homecoming "Spider-Man: Homecoming")_, _[Spider-Man: Far From Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Far\_From\_Home "Spider-Man: Far From Home")_.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-61)

In May of the same year, it was also announced that Favreau would co-host and executive produce a cooking show for [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") along with co-host [Roy Choi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Choi "Roy Choi"), called _[The Chef Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chef\_Show "The Chef Show")_. It premiered in June 2019.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-62) In December 2021 and July 2024, Favreau reprised his role as Happy Hogan in _[Spider-Man: No Way Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_No\_Way\_Home "Spider-Man: No Way Home")_ and _[Deadpool & Wolverine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool\_&\_Wolverine "Deadpool & Wolverine")_. In May 2022, Favreau produced the documentary series _[Prehistoric Planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistoric\_Planet\_(2022\_TV\_series) "Prehistoric Planet (2022 TV series)")_ alongside the [BBC Studios Natural History Unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Studios_Natural_History_Unit "BBC Studios Natural History Unit") for [Apple TV+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_TV+ "Apple TV+").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-63)

In January 2024, [Lucasfilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucasfilm "Lucasfilm") announced that a feature film titled _[The Mandalorian and Grogu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian\_and\_Grogu "The Mandalorian and Grogu")_ was in active development, with Favreau directing, writing, and co-producing alongside [Kathleen Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathleen_Kennedy_(producer) "Kathleen Kennedy (producer)") and [Dave Filoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Filoni "Dave Filoni").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-64) The film released on May 22 2026.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-65)

In March 2025, it was reported that Favreau was developing a [live-action animation hybrid series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswald_(2027_TV_series) "Oswald (2027 TV series)") based on _[Oswald the Lucky Rabbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswald\_the\_Lucky\_Rabbit "Oswald the Lucky Rabbit")_ for Disney+ as writer and producer.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-66)
