## Unreleased projects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Unreleased projects")]

In 1997, Favreau was working on a [Miramax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miramax "Miramax") project _The Marshal of Revelation_, an offbeat [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_film "Western film") featuring "a [Hasidic Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasidic_Jew "Hasidic Jew") gunslinger."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-67)

A [motion-captured](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_capture "Motion capture") animated film titled _Neanderthals_[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-68) was in development at [Sony Pictures Animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Pictures_Animation "Sony Pictures Animation") in the mid-2000s that Favreau would have written and produced, but the project was cancelled sometime in 2008[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-69) after four years in development.

In November 2010, it was reported that Favreau would direct a film titled _Magic Kingdom_, based on [The Walt Disney Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company")'s theme park [of the same name.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_Kingdom "Magic Kingdom")[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-70) In July 2012, Favreau reported that he was officially working on the film.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-72) In 2014, he stated that he still had interest in the project, and that he could direct it after finishing filming _[The Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jungle\_Book\_(2016\_film) "The Jungle Book (2016 film)")_ (2016).[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-73)

In October 2012, Favreau was attached to direct the racing film _Battle for Bonneville_ about the story of [Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Arfons "Art Arfons") and [Walt Arfons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Arfons "Walt Arfons"), with [Ryan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Reynolds "Ryan Reynolds") set to star as one of the leads. [New Regency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Regency "New Regency") was in negotiations to acquire the package. The script was written by [Dan Gilroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Gilroy "Dan Gilroy"). Favreau also was additionally developing to direct _[Jersey Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey\_Boys\_(film) "Jersey Boys (film)")_ at the time, and wanted to follow it with _Battle for Bonneville_.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-74)

In November 2012, it was said that Favreau – along with [David Fincher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Fincher "David Fincher"), [Brad Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Bird "Brad Bird"), [Matthew Vaughn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Vaughn "Matthew Vaughn") and [Ben Affleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck "Ben Affleck") – was being considered to direct _[Star Wars: The Force Awakens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Force\_Awakens "Star Wars: The Force Awakens")_, but the choice fell on [J. J. Abrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._J._Abrams "J. J. Abrams").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-75) In June 2015, Favreau stated that although he would not be working on the [_Star Wars_ anthology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars "Star Wars") films, he could work on future _Star Wars_ movies at some point.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-76) Favreau later worked with the franchise on the live action series _[The Mandalorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian "The Mandalorian")_.

In December 2013, [Will Ferrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Ferrell "Will Ferrell") stated that he did not want to make a sequel to _[Elf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf\_(film) "Elf (film)")_.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-77) Despite this, during an interview in January 2016, Favreau stated that a sequel could possibly be made.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-78) The next month however, Ferrell reiterated that it was unlikely that the sequel would happen and that he still did not want to return to the role.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-79)

In April 2016, it was reported that Favreau would return to direct [the sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Jungle_Book_(2016_film)#Future "The Jungle Book (2016 film)") to his critically acclaimed live-action adaptation of _[The Jungle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jungle\_Book\_(1967\_film) "The Jungle Book (1967 film)")_.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-81) Early pre-production of the sequel had begun by June 12, 2018, with [Justin Marks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Marks_(writer) "Justin Marks (writer)"), who wrote the previous film, having written an early draft for the film.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-JungleBook2Unusued-82)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Favreau married Joya Tillem, a physician, on November 24, 2000.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-83) The couple have a son and two daughters.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-84) Tillem is the niece of lawyer/talk show host [Len Tillem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Len_Tillem "Len Tillem").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-85)

Favreau credits the role-playing game _[Dungeons & Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungeons\_&\_Dragons "Dungeons & Dragons")_ with giving him "a really strong background in imagination, storytelling, understanding how to create tone and a sense of balance."[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-86)

## Golem Creations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Favreau&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Golem Creations")]

Golem Creations Ltd. LLC is a television [production company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Production_company "Production company") created by Jon Favreau on August 30, 2018.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-CABR-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-THR_Interview-88) In an interview with _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_, Favreau cited his fascination with the overlap of technology and storytelling and that he gave the company its name because a [golem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golem "Golem") was like technology; it could be used to protect or destroy if control was lost of it.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau#cite_note-THR_Interview-88) The company most recently produced _[The Mandalorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mandalorian "The Mandalorian")_, _[The Book of Boba Fett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Book\_of\_Boba\_Fett "The Book of Boba Fett")_, _[Ahsoka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahsoka\_(TV\_series) "Ahsoka (TV series)")_, and _[Star Wars: Skeleton Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_Skeleton\_Crew "Star Wars: Skeleton Crew")_ television shows, in partnership with [Lucasfilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucasfilm "Lucasfilm"), and the [Apple TV+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_TV+ "Apple TV+") documentary series _[Prehistoric Planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistoric\_Planet "Prehistoric Planet")_.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Dutch Anabaptist martyr (died 1569)

[![Image 4: An etching of a man leaning down to reach another man who has fallen through broken ice. Several bystanders are in the background, as well as a church.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Dirk.willems.rescue.ncs.jpg/250px-Dirk.willems.rescue.ncs.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dirk.willems.rescue.ncs.jpg)

Dirk Willems saves his pursuer in this etching from the 1685 edition of _[Martyrs Mirror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martyrs\_Mirror "Martyrs Mirror")_.

**Dirk Willems** (Dutch pronunciation:[[ˈdɪr(ə)k ˈʋɪləms]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch"); also spelled **Durk Willems**; died 16 May 1569) was a [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_people "Dutch people")[Anabaptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anabaptism "Anabaptism")[martyr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_martyrs "Christian martyrs") most famous for [escaping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prison_escape "Prison escape") from prison but then turning back to rescue his pursuer – who had fallen through thin ice while chasing Willems – only to be recaptured, tortured, and killed for his beliefs.

## Life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dirk_Willems&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life")]

Willems was born in [Asperen, Gelderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asperen "Asperen") (then under the [Duchy of Guelders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duchy_of_Guelders "Duchy of Guelders") in the [Holy Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire "Holy Roman Empire")), in the current [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"). He was subject to a [believers' baptism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believers'_baptism "Believers' baptism"), i.e. "rebaptized" (which made him an "Anabaptist" in the eyes of officials) as a young man in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-:0-1) thus rejecting the [infant baptism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infant_baptism "Infant baptism"), practiced at that time by both [Catholics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") and [established](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Established_church "Established church") Protestants in the Netherlands, which he would have received previously. This action, plus his continued devotion to his new faith and the baptism of several other people in his home, led to his condemnation by the [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") in the Netherlands and subsequent arrest in Asperen in 1569.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-:0-1)

Willems was held in a residential palace turned into a prison, from which he escaped using a rope made out of knotted rags. He climbed out of the prison onto the frozen moat. A guard noticed his escape and gave chase. Willems was able to traverse the thin ice of a frozen pond, the _Hondegat_, because of his lighter weight after subsisting on prison rations. However, the pursuing guard fell through the ice and yelled for help as he struggled in the [icy water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice "Ice").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-Kreider-2) Willems turned back to save the life of his pursuer and thus was recaptured. His former pursuer stated his desire to let Willems go, but the [burgomaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgomaster "Burgomaster") "reminded the pursuer of his oath", causing the pursuer to seize Willems.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-:0-1)

Willems was thereafter held until he was condemned by a group of seven judges, who, quoting Willems' "persisting obstinately in his opinion", ordered that he be [burned at the stake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_by_burning "Death by burning") on 16 May 1569, as well as that all his property be confiscated "for the benefit of [his royal majesty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_II_of_Spain "Philip II of Spain")". Willems was executed in Asperen. With a strong eastward wind blowing, the fire was driven away from the condemned's upper body, thus prolonging his torturous death. It was reported that the wind carried his screams all the way to nearby [Leerdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leerdam "Leerdam"), where he was heard to have exclaimed things such as "O Lord; my God", etc., over seventy times. The [bailiff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailiff "Bailiff") on horseback nearby was so saddened by Willems' suffering that he said to the executioner, "Dispatch the man with a quick death." Though it is not known if the executioner obeyed this request, it is known that Willems eventually died there, "with great steadfastness", and "having commended his soul into the hands of God".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-:0-1)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dirk_Willems&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Today, he is one of the most celebrated martyrs among [Anabaptists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anabaptist "Anabaptist"), which includes [Mennonites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mennonite "Mennonite") and [Amish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amish "Amish"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-3) as well as a [folk hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_hero "Folk hero") among modern residents of Asperen.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-Kreider-2)

## Portrayals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dirk_Willems&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Portrayals")]

[Heinz Gaugel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinz_Gaugel "Heinz Gaugel") included a portrayal of Willems' rescue of his pursuer in his 1992 cyclorama _[Behalt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behalt "Behalt")_, now housed at the [Amish and Mennonite Heritage Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amish_and_Mennonite_Heritage_Center "Amish and Mennonite Heritage Center") in Ohio.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-:4-4)

In 2018, a statue of Dirk Willems was unveiled at the [Mennonite Heritage Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mennonite_Heritage_Village "Mennonite Heritage Village") museum in [Steinbach, Manitoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steinbach,_Manitoba "Steinbach, Manitoba").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-5)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Dutch Anabaptist martyr (died 1569)

[![Image 4: An etching of a man leaning down to reach another man who has fallen through broken ice. Several bystanders are in the background, as well as a church.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Dirk.willems.rescue.ncs.jpg/250px-Dirk.willems.rescue.ncs.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dirk.willems.rescue.ncs.jpg)

Dirk Willems saves his pursuer in this etching from the 1685 edition of _[Martyrs Mirror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martyrs\_Mirror "Martyrs Mirror")_.

**Dirk Willems** (Dutch pronunciation:[[ˈdɪr(ə)k ˈʋɪləms]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch"); also spelled **Durk Willems**; died 16 May 1569) was a [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_people "Dutch people")[Anabaptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anabaptism "Anabaptism")[martyr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_martyrs "Christian martyrs") most famous for [escaping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prison_escape "Prison escape") from prison but then turning back to rescue his pursuer – who had fallen through thin ice while chasing Willems – only to be recaptured, tortured, and killed for his beliefs.

## Life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dirk_Willems&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life")]

Willems was born in [Asperen, Gelderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asperen "Asperen") (then under the [Duchy of Guelders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duchy_of_Guelders "Duchy of Guelders") in the [Holy Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire "Holy Roman Empire")), in the current [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"). He was subject to a [believers' baptism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believers'_baptism "Believers' baptism"), i.e. "rebaptized" (which made him an "Anabaptist" in the eyes of officials) as a young man in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-:0-1) thus rejecting the [infant baptism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infant_baptism "Infant baptism"), practiced at that time by both [Catholics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") and [established](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Established_church "Established church") Protestants in the Netherlands, which he would have received previously. This action, plus his continued devotion to his new faith and the baptism of several other people in his home, led to his condemnation by the [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") in the Netherlands and subsequent arrest in Asperen in 1569.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-:0-1)

Willems was held in a residential palace turned into a prison, from which he escaped using a rope made out of knotted rags. He climbed out of the prison onto the frozen moat. A guard noticed his escape and gave chase. Willems was able to traverse the thin ice of a frozen pond, the _Hondegat_, because of his lighter weight after subsisting on prison rations. However, the pursuing guard fell through the ice and yelled for help as he struggled in the [icy water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice "Ice").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-Kreider-2) Willems turned back to save the life of his pursuer and thus was recaptured. His former pursuer stated his desire to let Willems go, but the [burgomaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgomaster "Burgomaster") "reminded the pursuer of his oath", causing the pursuer to seize Willems.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-:0-1)

Willems was thereafter held until he was condemned by a group of seven judges, who, quoting Willems' "persisting obstinately in his opinion", ordered that he be [burned at the stake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_by_burning "Death by burning") on 16 May 1569, as well as that all his property be confiscated "for the benefit of [his royal majesty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_II_of_Spain "Philip II of Spain")". Willems was executed in Asperen. With a strong eastward wind blowing, the fire was driven away from the condemned's upper body, thus prolonging his torturous death. It was reported that the wind carried his screams all the way to nearby [Leerdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leerdam "Leerdam"), where he was heard to have exclaimed things such as "O Lord; my God", etc., over seventy times. The [bailiff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailiff "Bailiff") on horseback nearby was so saddened by Willems' suffering that he said to the executioner, "Dispatch the man with a quick death." Though it is not known if the executioner obeyed this request, it is known that Willems eventually died there, "with great steadfastness", and "having commended his soul into the hands of God".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-:0-1)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dirk_Willems&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Today, he is one of the most celebrated martyrs among [Anabaptists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anabaptist "Anabaptist"), which includes [Mennonites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mennonite "Mennonite") and [Amish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amish "Amish"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-3) as well as a [folk hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_hero "Folk hero") among modern residents of Asperen.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-Kreider-2)

## Portrayals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dirk_Willems&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Portrayals")]

[Heinz Gaugel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinz_Gaugel "Heinz Gaugel") included a portrayal of Willems' rescue of his pursuer in his 1992 cyclorama _[Behalt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behalt "Behalt")_, now housed at the [Amish and Mennonite Heritage Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amish_and_Mennonite_Heritage_Center "Amish and Mennonite Heritage Center") in Ohio.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-:4-4)

In 2018, a statue of Dirk Willems was unveiled at the [Mennonite Heritage Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mennonite_Heritage_Village "Mennonite Heritage Village") museum in [Steinbach, Manitoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steinbach,_Manitoba "Steinbach, Manitoba").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Willems?redirect=no#cite_note-5)

Read pages for a research assistant and follow useful links recursively. During
extraction, only the supplied page is evidence. The question defines what to look
for; parent reasoning guides navigation but is not this page's evidence.
Extraction uses the original question and current page, not the search query or
parent's hypothesis. Keep facts relevant to any part of the original question.
During navigation, a supplied local relation is a task, not evidence. Follow links
that establish or contradict it. Return when it is settled or has no useful route
here; other unresolved relations belong to the parent. Do not solve the whole
question again inside every branch.

Preserve exact relevant names and rows with their headers, values, units, dates
and scope. Never replace relevant rows with ellipses, examples or instructions to
continue the list. If all rows cannot fit, prioritize rows useful to the question
and explicitly mark omissions. A partial, restricted or truncated list is not the
complete candidate set. Missing fields are unknown. Keep relevant discoveries even
if they answer a different part of the original question.

Follow links likely to fill a candidate's missing condition or reach the required

### 25 actors who produced their own movies

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 4: 25 actors who produced their own movies](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 5](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/3/84/3845bf47-0070-5893-af5d-27cf01275e77/629804f081c22.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Many of the most well-known actors and actresses wear more than one hat behind the scenes. In front of the camera, they might change the original script with ad-libbing or suggesting different lines for their character. Behind the screen, many have been known to take a bigger creative role. Sometimes an actor or actress simply believes in a project and wants to make it happen, other times a film requires an additional investment during production and the studio well has run dry.

It’s not uncommon for a star to help fund a project they work on, though that tends to translate to an executive producer credit, as opposed to a producer credit. The distinction there is that the executive producer need not be quite as “hands-on” with production. A producer—in addition to sourcing the funding for the project—helps with casting and also makes artistic contributions to the set, location arrangements, and the film’s final form. In short, film producers have an enormous influence over everything from the filmmaking process to the culture of the movie set.

There are occasions when an actor is a frequent collaborator with a director, and their role as producer goes hand in hand with that partnership. But it’s rare for an actor to take on the role of a core producer in the nitty-gritty of the production—from pre- to post-production, or frankly, anywhere in between.Still, it does happen—perhaps more often than you might think.

To that end, [Giggster](https://giggster.com/) compiled a list of actors representing a diverse range of age, race, and expression who have all produced at least two of their own movies. To be included, the actor had to have produced more than one of their own films and been billed not merely as executive producer but as producer or producer and executive producer.

### Antonio Banderas

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 7: Antonio Banderas](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 8](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/0/39/039e73bc-c5c3-5875-8ff0-7d37bde17b36/629804f0ce5a1.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

While not a prolific producer, Antonio Banderas has still helped make some movies a reality through his contributions. His first producing credit was 1999’s “The White River Kid,” where he also portrayed a con man working alongside his adoptive brother (Bob Hoskins). He also produced and starred in the animated film “Justin and the Knights of Valour” in 2013 and the science fiction movie “Automata” in 2014.

### Drew Barrymore

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 9: Drew Barrymore](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 10](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/7/1d/71df6f1c-8d08-5fd1-9343-5975e56f98c0/629804f131db1.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Drew Barrymore has been a driving force in producing many of her iconic movies, starting with an executive producer credit on 1999’s rom-com “Never Been Kissed.” Since then, Barrymore has taken a hands-on production approach in such films as “Charlie’s Angels” and its follow-up “Charlie’s Angels: Full Throttle”; “Duplex,” where she starred opposite Ben Stiller for director Danny DeVito; and “Whip It,” the modern roller-derby classic, which she also directed. Perhaps her most surprising (executive) producing credit, however, is “Donnie Darko,” which sees her in a small but pivotal role as the titular character’s English teacher.

### Warren Beatty

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 11: Warren Beatty](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 12](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/e/f0/ef0a4fa8-6f06-5a51-81d8-4f18be4adc1a/629804f185253.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Arguably one of Hollywood’s greatest actors, Warren Beatty is well-known for being an “all-hands” filmmaker. From 1967’s “Bonnie and Clyde,” where he starred alongside Faye Dunaway in the film’s titular roles, through his most recent credit, 2016’s “Rules Don’t Apply,” Beatty has produced—or executive produced, in a few rare cases—every film with which he’s been associated.Moreover, he is an accomplished director, and of course, he has produced each of his directorial efforts too. Several films he directed are contemporary classics, among them “Reds” (for which he won the Best Picture Oscar), “Dick Tracy,” and “Bugsy.”

### Jackie Chan

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 13: Jackie Chan](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 14](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/6/0a/60a5923a-ad8c-5969-9e80-0f3e55259203/629804f1cbd1b.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Fang Shilong, known internationally as Jackie Chan, is considered a figurehead in globalizing kung fu martial arts through film. He has more than 60 producer credits to his name, among them the Hong Kong action flick “The Accidental Spy” and the 2004 remake of “Around the World in 80 Days.” He is the chairman of JCE Movies Limited, which produces films for both China and the U.S.

### Charlie Chaplin

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 15: Charlie Chaplin](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 16](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/8/ed/8ed04160-a7d5-5a92-982b-d0708751211e/629804f44244c.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Given how this silent film icon also directed and wrote many of the movies in which he starred, it should come as no surprise that Charlie Chaplin has an extensive producing résumé. The majority of his producing credits were uncredited during his lifetime, however, he still helped bring such classics as “The Immigrant” and “The Great Dictator” to the cinematic canon.

Not to mention, he was one of the founders of United Artists, along with actors Douglas Fairbanks and Mary Pickford and director D.W. Griffith (which, today, is part of MGM and owned by Amazon Studios).

### Tom Cruise

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 17: Tom Cruise](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 18](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/4/2f/42f2153f-c673-5767-ab83-404a1cdef002/629804f471309.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Much like he does many of his own stunts, Tom Cruise has produced a significant number of the movies he’s starred in. His producing career began with 1996’s “Mission: Impossible,” and he has produced every film in the franchise ever since, including the forthcoming “Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning.”

In 1992, Cruise and his then-agent Paula Wagner founded Cruise/Wagner Productions in order to give him more creative control over his movies. When the shingle went defunct in 2008, Cruise simply carried on alone, by which time he had more than enough bankability in the industry to make the films he wanted. He also produced 2004’s “The Last Samurai,” both films in his Jack Reacher series, as well as the 2022 installment of his popular Top Gun franchise, “Top Gun: Maverick.”

### Danny DeVito

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 19: Danny DeVito](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 20](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/b/53/b53c09f8-3cbf-531b-831a-603370c35a41/629804f4a8072.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Not only has he directed and starred in films such as 1992’s “Hoffa” and 1996’s beloved family film “Matilda,” Danny DeVito has also produced some of the most successful films of the past 30 years. After co-founding Jersey Films in 1992, DeVito went on to produce hits including “Reality Bites,” “Get Shorty” (in which he also starred), and a pair of Steven Soderbergh films, including “Out of Sight” and the Oscar-winning “Erin Brockovich.” Additionally, he’s been the producing force behind the Liam Neeson action thriller, “A Walk Among the Tombstones,” and the 2007 drama, “Freedom Writers,” starring two-time Oscar-winning actress Hilary Swank.

### Tina Fey

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 21: Tina Fey](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 22](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/d/c8/dc82866b-989f-5943-a7c2-d6e6a93a8e42/629804f4f22b2.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Given her status as a comedic icon, it might be surprising that Tina Fey has only produced two of her movies. While a prolific television producer, her first feature producing credit was 2015’s “Sisters,” in which Fey starred alongside former “Saturday Night Live” cast member Amy Poehler, which she followed with “Whiskey Tango Foxtrot,” a dramedy about a journalist covering the war in Afghanistan. However, she is [adapting the “Mean Girls” Broadway musical](https://deadline.com/2021/09/mean-girls-the-musical-arturo-perez-jr-and-samantha-jayne-direct-paramount-players-1234840881/) (based on the 2004 film she herself wrote) into a film, which is currently in development.

Little Stranger



### Jodie Foster

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 23: Jodie Foster](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 24](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/8/61/861e54e1-adbb-562d-8a81-b0e5b56750bb/629804f53dc74.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Like other entries on this list, Oscar-winning actress Jodie Foster is known for producing movies she’s also starred in and occasionally directs. Her first producing credit came with 1985’s “Mesmerized,” which she co-produced alongside Antony I. Ginnane and Christopher J. Kirkham. Nearly 10 years and two Best Actress Oscars later, Foster produced and starred in “Nell,” followed swiftly by her first directorial effort, the 1995 Thanksgiving holiday comedy “Home for the Holidays.”

She also produced and took a supporting role in “The Dangerous Lives of Altar Boys” in 2002. Her latest producing effort was the documentary, “Be Natural: The Untold Story of Alice Guy-Blaché,” which she also narrated.

Egg Pictures



### Tom Hanks

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 25: Tom Hanks](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 26](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/8/6c/86c1fcad-34b6-53ae-9095-02712e3ca20b/629804f57ebe1.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

In 1996, Tom Hanks wrote and co-starred in his directorial debut, “That Thing You Do!” That story of a one-hit-wonder rock ’n’ roll band was the genesis for Hanks’ production shingle, Playtone, which is taken from the record label the fictional band was signed to in the movie. Beginning with the HBO limited series “From the Earth to the Moon,” Hanks and Playtone have been behind numerous successful film and TV series since.

Hanks’ first feature producing credit was 2000’s “Cast Away,” for which he also secured a Best Actor Academy Award nomination. Since then he has pulled double duty in such films as “Charlie Wilson’s War,” “The Great Buck Howard,” and “Larry Crowne,” which he also directed. He is also producing the upcoming dramedy, “A Man Called Otto,” in which he is also starring.

Twentieth Century Fox

![Image 27: Salma Hayek](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

While her producing credits are not as lengthy as other entries on this list, Salma Hayek has helped bring important and engaging stories to the big screen. She co-produced 2002’s “Frida,” the acclaimed biopic in which she also played Frida Kahlo. Other movies that Hayek helped to produce include 2014’s “The Prophet,” an animated drama about the homebound journey of an exiled poet to whom Hayek also lent her voice acting, and the following year’s “Septembers of Shiraz,” in which she co-starred with Oscar winner Adrien Brody.

A powerhouse in the entertainment industry, Queen Latifah has helped produce many movies that she starred in over the years. Her first executive producing credit was 2003’s “Bringing Down the House,” and she very quickly transitioned to producer with “The Cookout” and “Beauty Shop” in the two years after. Her film production has dwindled in recent years as she began appearing more on television, but she has continued to be an active producer on the small screen through her entertainment company Flavor Unit Entertainment.

While having starred in several movies previously, pop star Jennifer Lopez’s first foray into producing was the 2006 film “El Cantante,” in which she starred alongside ex-husband Marc Anthony. Perhaps her most successful producing role was 2019’s “Hustlers,” where she also gave a critically acclaimed performance.She most recently produced, starred in, and performed the entire soundtrack for the 2022 romantic comedy “Marry Me” and has several projects in the pipeline, including the action thriller “The Mother,” which will see her playing an assassin who comes out of hiding to protect the daughter she once gave up.

Given how influential Eddie Murphy has been in the comedy world, it might come as a surprise just how few of his films he produced himself. His first producing credit was 1995’s “Vampire in Brooklyn,” though he had been a credited executive producer on his comedy films of the 1980s as well as his directorial effort, 1989’s “Harlem Nights.” In the last two decades, Murphy has produced and acted in 2007’s “Norbit,” 2019’s “Dolemite Is My Name,” and the 2021 sequel to one of his most successful films of the ’80s, “Coming 2 America.”

Tyler Perry has become a modern-day Hollywood legend, thanks in large part to his prolific production company, Tyler Perry Studios. He has produced the majority of movies he has starred in, most notably every single entry of his Madea franchise. Other notable movies he has produced, starred in, and even directed include “Why Did I Get Married?” and “A Fall from Grace.” He is currently producing “Sister Act 3,” the long-awaited sequel that will see [Whoopi Goldberg reprise her role](https://www.cheatsheet.com/entertainment/tyler-perry-gives-update-sister-act-3-starring-whoopi-goldberg.html/) as the beloved Deloris Wilson.

Oscar-winning actor Brad Pitt has produced a plethora of movies under his company Plan B Entertainment Inc., many of which he also starred in. He produced and starred in 2007’s “The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford,” marking the first time he ever produced a movie in which he also acted. He has been both the face of and behind-the-scenes power for such films as “Moneyball,” “World War Z,” “The Big Short,” and most recently, 2019’s “Ad Astra.”

It took a bit for Aubrey Plaza to begin her producing journey, but it has already resulted in some notable credits and roles. The “Parks and Recreation” star’s first producing credit was 2017’s “The Little Hours,” directed by her husband and frequent collaborator, Jeff Baena. That same year also saw the release of “Ingrid Goes West,” in which Plaza plays a slightly unhinged social media stalker opposite actress Elizabeth Olsen, of Avengers franchise fame. Plaza also produced and starred in the acclaimed “Black Bear” in 2020 as well as 2022’s “Emily the Criminal.”

In addition to founding the Sundance Film Festival, Robert Redford has one of the longest and strongest résumés in Hollywood—and not just as an actor but as a producer and director as well. His Wildwood Enterprises Inc. production company has been behind many of Redford’s films, including “Three Days of the Condor,” “The Company You Keep,” and “Our Souls at Night.” Moreover, Redford is a credited producer on many of the other films he has directed and/or starred in, notable among them are 1994’s Oscar-nominated “Quiz Show,” 1998’s “The Horse Whisperer,” and 2015’s “A Walk in the Woods,” an adaptation of Bill Bryson’s classic account of wanderlust.

She produced (and starred in) 2017’s critically acclaimed, Oscar-winning “I, Tonya” and has since produced the noir “Terminal,” Depression-era thriller “Dreamland,” and perhaps most well-known, “Birds of Prey.” She will also be producing and starring in [the buzzy “Barbie” for director Greta Gerwig](https://www.indiewire.com/2022/05/margot-robbie-greta-gerwig-barbie-plot-cast-details-1234703047/), slated for 2023.

There is no denying that Barbra Streisand is an entertainment icon, having conquered the music and filmmaking industries in more ways than one. Despite only having three film-producing credits to her name, they were movies that she also directed and starred in. 1983’s “Yentl” won her two Golden Globes for both Best Motion Picture–Musical or Comedy and Best Director. She was nominated for the Best Picture Oscar for her producing work on “The Prince of Tides” in 1991. 1996’s “The Mirror Has Two Faces” was met with equal acclaim—co-star and acting legend Lauren Bacall earned an Oscar nomination for the movie—but Streisand has not produced or directed a film since.

Two-time Oscar winner Denzel Washington has made a respectable name for himself as a producer and director, ever since his first foray into producing with 2002’s “Antwone Fisher.” Since then he has worked as both actor and producer on “The Book of Eli” and both films in the Equilizer series and took a threefer on “Fences,” directing Viola Davis to win the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress, the first Oscar triumph of her career.

Starting with 1991’s “A Rage in Harlem,” Forest Whitaker has used his star power to help produce movies by new filmmakers such as 2005’s “American Gun,” the directorial debut of “Behind the Movement” filmmaker Aric Avelino, and “Powder Blue,” Timothy Linh Bui’s critically heralded sophomore effort. Dubbed the “Queen of All Media,” Oprah Winfrey has developed a media empire that includes stints in film production. Her first film producing credit was the ABC television movie “Before Women Had Wings” in 1997, and soon after she stepped boldly into film, producing and starring in Jonathan Demme’s 1998 adaptation of Toni Morrison’s novel “Beloved.” Winfrey also helped produce 2014’s “Selma,” the 2017 TV movie “The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks,” and was the producer behind Denzel Washington’s sophomore directorial effort, 2007’s “The Great Debaters.”

While in recent years she’s become most well-known for her burgeoning book club, “Reese’s Book Club,” Reese Witherspoon is still a very powerful player behind the camera. She served as executive producer on 2003’s “Legally Blonde 2: Red, White & Blonde,” and from there has used her largesse as a producer to get such acclaimed acting vehicles as 2014’s “Wild” and 2006’s “Penelope” off the ground. ### 25 actors who produced their own movies

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 4: 25 actors who produced their own movies](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 5](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/3/84/3845bf47-0070-5893-af5d-27cf01275e77/629804f081c22.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Many of the most well-known actors and actresses wear more than one hat behind the scenes. In front of the camera, they might change the original script with ad-libbing or suggesting different lines for their character. Behind the screen, many have been known to take a bigger creative role. Sometimes an actor or actress simply believes in a project and wants to make it happen, other times a film requires an additional investment during production and the studio well has run dry.

It’s not uncommon for a star to help fund a project they work on, though that tends to translate to an executive producer credit, as opposed to a producer credit. The distinction there is that the executive producer need not be quite as “hands-on” with production. A producer—in addition to sourcing the funding for the project—helps with casting and also makes artistic contributions to the set, location arrangements, and the film’s final form. In short, film producers have an enormous influence over everything from the filmmaking process to the culture of the movie set.

There are occasions when an actor is a frequent collaborator with a director, and their role as producer goes hand in hand with that partnership. But it’s rare for an actor to take on the role of a core producer in the nitty-gritty of the production—from pre- to post-production, or frankly, anywhere in between.Still, it does happen—perhaps more often than you might think.

To that end, [Giggster](https://giggster.com/) compiled a list of actors representing a diverse range of age, race, and expression who have all produced at least two of their own movies. To be included, the actor had to have produced more than one of their own films and been billed not merely as executive producer but as producer or producer and executive producer.

From 1967’s “Bonnie and Clyde,” where he starred alongside Faye Dunaway in the film’s titular roles, through his most recent credit, 2016’s “Rules Don’t Apply,” Beatty has produced—or executive produced, in a few rare cases—every film with which he’s been associated.Moreover, he is an accomplished director, and of course, he has produced each of his directorial efforts too. Several films he directed are contemporary classics, among them “Reds” (for which he won the Best Picture Oscar), “Dick Tracy,” and “Bugsy.”

Updated Jun 1, 2022

Given how this silent film icon also directed and wrote many of the movies in which he starred, it should come as no surprise that Charlie Chaplin has an extensive producing résumé. ### Tom Cruise

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 17: Tom Cruise](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 18](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/4/2f/42f2153f-c673-5767-ab83-404a1cdef002/629804f471309.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Much like he does many of his own stunts, Tom Cruise has produced a significant number of the movies he’s starred in. His producing career began with 1996’s “Mission: Impossible,” and he has produced every film in the franchise ever since, including the forthcoming “Mission: Impossible - Dead Reckoning.”

In 1992, Cruise and his then-agent Paula Wagner founded Cruise/Wagner Productions in order to give him more creative control over his movies. When the shingle went defunct in 2008, Cruise simply carried on alone, by which time he had more than enough bankability in the industry to make the films he wanted. He also produced 2004’s “The Last Samurai,” both films in his Jack Reacher series, as well as the 2022 installment of his popular Top Gun franchise, “Top Gun: Maverick.”

In 1996, Tom Hanks wrote and co-starred in his directorial debut, “That Thing You Do!” That story of a one-hit-wonder rock ’n’ roll band was the genesis for Hanks’ production shingle, Playtone, which is taken from the record label the fictional band was signed to in the movie. Beginning with the HBO limited series “From the Earth to the Moon,” Hanks and Playtone have been behind numerous successful film and TV series since.

Hanks’ first feature producing credit was 2000’s “Cast Away,” for which he also secured a Best Actor Academy Award nomination. Since then he has pulled double duty in such films as “Charlie Wilson’s War,” “The Great Buck Howard,” and “Larry Crowne,” which he also directed. He is also producing the upcoming dramedy, “A Man Called Otto,” in which he is also starring.

Since then, she has pulled double duty for projects like “Tully,” the film adaptation of Gillian Flynn’s novel “Dark Places,” the action smash “Atomic Blonde,” and “Bombshell,” a drama film that looks at how three women in the Fox News empire took on the network’s toxic work environment.

### Denzel Washington

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 49: Denzel Washington](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 50](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/4/06/4068357e-4918-5861-b73d-7e4c3381858a/629804f98d285.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Two-time Oscar winner Denzel Washington has made a respectable name for himself as a producer and director, ever since his first foray into producing with 2002’s “Antwone Fisher.” Since then he has worked as both actor and producer on “The Book of Eli” and both films in the Equilizer series and took a threefer on “Fences,” directing Viola Davis to win the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress, the first Oscar triumph of her career.

### Forest Whitaker

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 51: Forest Whitaker](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 52](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/5/4a/54ad55fd-c2f3-5aa5-ace6-004e388eb059/629804f9c3ffd.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Starting with 1991’s “A Rage in Harlem,” Forest Whitaker has used his star power to help produce movies by new filmmakers such as 2005’s “American Gun,” the directorial debut of “Behind the Movement” filmmaker Aric Avelino, and “Powder Blue,” Timothy Linh Bui’s critically heralded sophomore effort. Whitaker took supporting roles in both films. He also produced the critical and commercially successful “Fruitvale Station,” “Sorry to Bother You,” and “Passing,” the 2021 Rebecca Hall adaptation of the classic Nella Larsen novel.

### Oprah Winfrey

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 53: Oprah Winfrey](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

![Image 54](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/3/5a/35a43130-aec2-57d5-a0ca-22e5ae3cd1e9/629804fa3d4fc.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

Dubbed the “Queen of All Media,” Oprah Winfrey has developed a media empire that includes stints in film production. Her first film producing credit was the ABC television movie “Before Women Had Wings” in 1997, and soon after she stepped boldly into film, producing and starring in Jonathan Demme’s 1998 adaptation of Toni Morrison’s novel “Beloved.” Winfrey also helped produce 2014’s “Selma,” the 2017 TV movie “The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks,” and was the producer behind Denzel Washington’s sophomore directorial effort, 2007’s “The Great Debaters.”

Updated Jun 1, 2022

![Image 56](https://bloximages.chicago2.vip.townnews.com/thesouthern.com/content/tncms/assets/v3/editorial/5/fb/5fbf8945-d466-5172-af1c-b17a36c82bc1/629804fa99c22.preview.jpg?resize=200%2C200)

While in recent years she’s become most well-known for her burgeoning book club, “Reese’s Book Club,” Reese Witherspoon is still a very powerful player behind the camera. She served as executive producer on 2003’s “Legally Blonde 2: Red, White & Blonde,” and from there has used her largesse as a producer to get such acclaimed acting vehicles as 2014’s “Wild” and 2006’s “Penelope” off the ground. Her most recent film producing and starring credit was 2015’s “Hot Pursuit,” but she has not faded away in the slightest; she starred in and produced the series “Big Little Lies,” “Little Fires Everywhere,” and “The Morning Show.”

# Here Are 13 Celebrities Who Produced Major Movies That They Didn’t Appear In

Did everyone else already know that Bradley Cooper was a producer on _Joker_?

Posted on Mar 28, 2024

comment

Comment

*   [](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Here%20Are%2013%20Celebrities%20Who%20Produced%20Major%20Movies%20That%20They%20Didn%E2%80%99t%20Appear%20In%0A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.buzzfeed.com%2Fjosephlongo%2Fcelebs-who-are-successful-film-producers%3Futm_source%3Ddynamic%26utm_campaign%3Dbfsharebluesky)

*    

[![Image 1: Joseph Longo](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2021-06/3/16/user_images/a824550933a9/tomiobaro-v2-2174-1622738336-41_large.jpg?downsize=120:*&output-format=jpg&output-quality=auto) by Joseph Longo BuzzFeed Staff Hello!](https://www.buzzfeed.com/josephlongo)

## Last month, [Emma Stone](https://www.buzzfeed.com/tag/emma-stone) achieved a significant feat with her Oscar win for _[Poor Things](https://www.buzzfeed.com/noradominick/2024-oscars-best-picture-nominees-facts)._ She's now a two-time Academy Award winner, first taking home Best Actress in 2017 for _La La Land_. But this is far from the only major success she's had lately.

![Image 2: Olivia in elegant strapless gown with statement necklace, smiling at the camera](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/19/asset/b0e4be6c644c/sub-buzz-808-1711137221-6.jpg?downsize=700%3A%2A&output-quality=auto&output-format=auto)

 Mike Coppola / Getty Images 

## Behind the scenes, Emma has built an impressive career as a film producer. She also garnered a Best Picture nomination this year as a producer for _Poor Things_. Emma even runs a production company, Fruit Tree, alongside her husband, Dave McCary. And though the company didn't produce _Poor Things_, they've hit the ground running with some notable film releases since [launching](https://deadline.com/2020/08/emma-stone-dave-mccary-plant-fruit-tree-production-banner-with-a24-first-look-tv-deal-1203005063/) in 2020.

![Image 3: Emma Stone in a beaded dress holds an Oscar, standing next to Dave McCary in a tuxedo](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/26/17/asset/c9a67a765d41/sub-buzz-1263-1711475158-1.jpg?downsize=700%3A%2A&output-quality=auto&output-format=auto)

 Steve Granitz / FilmMagic / Getty Images 

## Their recent films include _When You Finish Saving the World_ and _Problemista_, while they've got [_I Saw the TV Glow_](https://www.buzzfeed.com/josephlongo/new-movies-to-watch-march-april-may) and _A Real Pain_ coming later this year.

![Image 5: Two characters in a scene, woman in green blazer with pink hair, man in brown shirt with backpack](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/21/asset/910e1ba004f9/sub-buzz-3259-1711141443-4.jpg)

 A24 / Courtesy Everett Collection 

## Emma is far from the first celeb to make a name for themselves producing movies. So here are 13 stars, including a former president, who've also proved themselves to be savvy film producers:

## 1.Margot Robbie: _Saltburn_ (2023)

![Image 7: Margot in a black corset top and suede waistcoat at an event](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/21/asset/b25feecd14f6/sub-buzz-2505-1704402312-1.jpg)

 Michael Tran / AFP via Getty Images 

## The star is an Oscar-nominated producer through her production company, LuckyChap, which she founded alongside Josey McNamara and her husband, Tom Ackerley. In addition to working on some of Margot's films, like _I, Tonya_, _Terminal_, and _Barbie_, the company was also behind the TV series _Dollface_ and the miniseries _Maid_. They also produced director Emerald Fennell's films _Promising Young Woman_ and _Saltburn._

![Image 9: Barry Keogh in burgundy robe overlooking a park with people and scattered objects in Saltburn](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/20/asset/b494186aa7dd/sub-buzz-2253-1711137616-1.jpg)

 MGM / Courtesy Everett Collection 

As for what Margot first thought of _Saltburn_'s many infamous scenes, she told [Variety](https://variety.com/2024/film/features/margot-robbie-luckychap-barbie-saltburn-shocks-being-original-1235858528/) in January, "It didn't feel that shocking in the script, because Emerald immerses you into a world so quickly. She's so masterful at tone and plot; she gets you into it so quickly — you're just immediately like, 'I'm in this world.' So by the time you get to something like the bathtub scene, she's primed you for it. She's got you. You're, like, picking at a scab; you're like, 'I can't help myself.' Or like popping a pimple: 'I know I shouldn't squeeze, but I'm gonna.'"

## 2.Will Ferrell: _May December_ (2023)

![Image 11: Will in gray suit and red tie standing against a backdrop with Netflix logo](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/20/asset/f2bf74135d1c/sub-buzz-8784-1704399053-1.jpg)

 Valerie Macon / AFP via Getty Images 

## Will and Adam McKay produced numerous films and TV shows together through their production company, Gary Sanchez Productions. This includes hits like _Step Brothers_, _Vice_, _The Menu_, and _Succession_. [Following the end of Gary Sanchez Productions](https://variety.com/2019/film/news/will-ferrell-adam-mckay-cease-production-partnership-1203182411/), Will shifted his producing efforts in recent years to women-centered content alongside producer Jessica Elbaum through sister label Gloria Sanchez Productions. The company is behind films like _Booksmart_, _Hustlers_, and _May December_.

![Image 13: Julianne Moore and Natalie Portman in a dressing room, Natalie holding a notepad, Julianne with makeup, in May December](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/20/asset/6665ff65f148/sub-buzz-5729-1711137683-1.jpg)

 Francois Duhamel / © Netflix / Courtesy Everett Colleection 

Will told [Vanity Fair](https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/may-december-producers-will-ferrell-jessica-elbaum-awards-insider)in January, "It just kind of happened this way" that he's begun producing women-centric content. "If the planet is a school bus, men have been driving it since the beginning of civilization," he continued. "It's women's turn to take over the wheel."

## 3.Barack Obama: _Leave the World Behind_ (2023)

![Image 15: Barack Obama speaking at an event, wearing a suit without a tie, gesturing with his right hand](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/21/asset/af6b6e3cbb0d/sub-buzz-9642-1704402612-1.jpg)

 Spencer Platt / Getty Images 

## Through their production company Higher Ground, Barack and Michelle Obama worked on the film about a dystopian future amid a blackout. The movie is based on Rumaan Alam's 2020 novel of the same name. "He had a lot [of] notes about the characters and the empathy we would have for them," the film's director and writer, Sam Esmail, told [Vanity Fair](https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/09/leave-the-world-behind-movie-first-look) last year of the former president's involvement. "I have to say he is a big movie lover, and he wasn't just giving notes about things that were from his background. He was giving notes as a fan of the book, and he wanted to see a really good film."

![Image 17: Four actors, including Mahershala Ali and Julia Roberts, stand together with serious expressions](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/25/20/asset/945dd8348252/sub-buzz-1053-1711399351-1.jpg)

 JoJo Whilden / © Netflix / Courtesy Everett Collection 

Last year, Higher Ground also produced _Rustin_, the Bayard Rustin biopic starring Colman Domingo.

## 4.Maria Bello: _The Woman King_ (2022)

![Image 19: Maria smiling at a media event wearing a suit and tie](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/21/asset/f2bf74135d1c/sub-buzz-8980-1704402497-1.jpg)

 Matt Winkelmeyer / Getty Images 

## "_The Woman King_ was definitely born of my love of the continent in general," Maria told the [Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lifestyle/lifestyle-news/the-woman-king-producer-maria-bello-kenya-1235199627/) in 2022, referring to Africa. "It's based on women's history, a story I found many years ago about this army of women in the 17th century. I was watching _Braveheart_ and I was like, 'Why isn't there a woman's movie like this?'"

![Image 21: Viola Davis in traditional warrior attire stands confidently in a bustling village setting at night](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/20/asset/b494186aa7dd/sub-buzz-2261-1711137865-2.jpg)

 TriStar Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection 

Maria [pitched](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/viola-davis-gina-prince-bythewood-the-woman-king-1235210487/) the film to Viola Davis, who came aboard as a producer alongside her husband and producing partner, Julius Tennon, through their company, JuVee Productions. Viola also starred in the film.

## 5.Reese Witherspoon: _Where the Crawdads Sing_ (2022)

![Image 23: Reese Witherspoon smiling, wearing a strapless red gown at the SAG Awards](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/28/15/asset/edacc7ee2d7d/sub-buzz-1049-1711640634-4.jpg)

 Frazer Harrison / Getty Images 

## _Where the Crawdads Sing_ is based on Delia Owens's 2018 novel of the same name. Reese's involvement with the book turned movie came after she [selected the novel](https://reesesbookclub.com/article/4eRlfCOXueqPrm6ZnQpzwl) that year as a book for her book club. Then Reese's production company, Hello Sunshine, produced the adaptation.

![Image 25: Woman standing in the woods, looking forward, with a tree trunk behind her](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/25/20/asset/1647495bdca8/sub-buzz-539-1711399879-1.jpg)

 Michele K. Short / © Sony Pictures Entertainment / Courtesy Everett Collection 

"Shortly after, one of my very dearest friends and closest collaborators called me and said, 'So we make it into a movie? And I was like, 'Yessss! That would be amazing!" Reese told[_Entertainment Tonight_](https://www.etonline.com/reese-witherspoon-reflects-on-taking-where-the-crawdads-sing-from-book-club-to-the-big-screen)in 2022. "From there, we just started going, and it's just been a dream come true."

## 6.Denzel Washington: _Ma Rainey's Black Bottom_ (2020)

![Image 27: Denzel in a black suit and tie at an event](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/21/asset/58847356212f/sub-buzz-1459-1704405002-1.jpg)

 Angela Weiss / AFP via Getty Images 

## "I put my two cents in where I could, but in all seriousness, I really tried to stay out of the way," Denzel told [the Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/film/2020/dec/04/he-will-be-remembered-as-a-hero-denzel-washington-and-viola-davis-on-chadwick-boseman) in 2020 about producing the film based on August Wilson's play of the same name.

![Image 29: Viola Davis as Ma Rainey in patterned dress singing with jazz band members playing instruments in vintage room](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/21/asset/9d80fe9d54fb/sub-buzz-1028-1711141285-12.jpg)

 David Lee / © Netflix / Courtesy Everett Collection 

According to [Variety](https://variety.com/2021/awards/news/chadwick-boseman-ma-raineys-black-bottom-denzel-washington-1234936791/), _Ma Rainey's Black Bottom_ is one of the late playwright's 10 plays, known as the Pittsburgh Cycle or the Century Cycle, that Denzel is working to adapt to the screen. Another was _Fences_, which was adapted in 2016. Denzel starred in, directed, and produced that adaptation.

## 7.Bradley Cooper: _Joker_ (2019)

![Image 31: Bradley Cooper stands smiling in a tailored navy suit with a tie, at a Netflix event for "Maestro"](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/21/asset/98fc5e8400eb/sub-buzz-1988-1704402887-1.jpg)

 Axelle/Bauer-Griffin / FilmMagic / Getty Images 

## "We kept this one pretty close to us," Jeff Groth, the film editor on _Joker_, told [IndieWire](https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/bradley-cooper-joker-editing-room-1202205304/) in 2020. "We screened it more personally for people and filmmakers. Bradley Cooper definitely came in a couple of times. He was a producer on the movie, but he definitely watched the movie many times and sat with us. We could call him if we got stuck with something and be like, 'Hey, can you come over and take a look at things?'"

![Image 33: Joaquin Phoenix dressed as the Joker dancing on steps](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/20/asset/9d80fe9d54fb/sub-buzz-1017-1711141154-8.jpg)

 Niko Tavernise / © Warner Bros. / Courtesy Everett Collection 

## 8.Eva Longoria: _John Wick_ (2014)

"It was so great, and I thought, _This could actually be a fantastic movie_." # Here Are 13 Celebrities Who Produced Major Movies That They Didn’t Appear In

Did everyone else already know that Bradley Cooper was a producer on _Joker_?

Posted on Mar 28, 2024

comment

[![Image 1: Joseph Longo](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2021-06/3/16/user_images/a824550933a9/tomiobaro-v2-2174-1622738336-41_large.jpg?downsize=120:*&output-format=jpg&output-quality=auto) by Joseph Longo BuzzFeed Staff Hello!](https://www.buzzfeed.com/josephlongo)

## Last month, [Emma Stone](https://www.buzzfeed.com/tag/emma-stone) achieved a significant feat with her Oscar win for _[Poor Things](https://www.buzzfeed.com/noradominick/2024-oscars-best-picture-nominees-facts)._ She's now a two-time Academy Award winner, first taking home Best Actress in 2017 for _La La Land_. But this is far from the only major success she's had lately.

![Image 2: Olivia in elegant strapless gown with statement necklace, smiling at the camera](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/19/asset/b0e4be6c644c/sub-buzz-808-1711137221-6.jpg?downsize=700%3A%2A&output-quality=auto&output-format=auto)

 Mike Coppola / Getty Images 

## Behind the scenes, Emma has built an impressive career as a film producer. She also garnered a Best Picture nomination this year as a producer for _Poor Things_. Emma even runs a production company, Fruit Tree, alongside her husband, Dave McCary. And though the company didn't produce _Poor Things_, they've hit the ground running with some notable film releases since [launching](https://deadline.com/2020/08/emma-stone-dave-mccary-plant-fruit-tree-production-banner-with-a24-first-look-tv-deal-1203005063/) in 2020.

![Image 3: Emma Stone in a beaded dress holds an Oscar, standing next to Dave McCary in a tuxedo](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/26/17/asset/c9a67a765d41/sub-buzz-1263-1711475158-1.jpg?downsize=700%3A%2A&output-quality=auto&output-format=auto)

 Steve Granitz / FilmMagic / Getty Images 

## Their recent films include _When You Finish Saving the World_ and _Problemista_, while they've got [_I Saw the TV Glow_](https://www.buzzfeed.com/josephlongo/new-movies-to-watch-march-april-may) and _A Real Pain_ coming later this year.

![Image 5: Two characters in a scene, woman in green blazer with pink hair, man in brown shirt with backpack](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/21/asset/910e1ba004f9/sub-buzz-3259-1711141443-4.jpg)

 A24 / Courtesy Everett Collection 

## Emma is far from the first celeb to make a name for themselves producing movies. So here are 13 stars, including a former president, who've also proved themselves to be savvy film producers:

## 1.Margot Robbie: _Saltburn_ (2023)

![Image 7: Margot in a black corset top and suede waistcoat at an event](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/21/asset/b25feecd14f6/sub-buzz-2505-1704402312-1.jpg)

 Michael Tran / AFP via Getty Images 

## The star is an Oscar-nominated producer through her production company, LuckyChap, which she founded alongside Josey McNamara and her husband, Tom Ackerley. In addition to working on some of Margot's films, like _I, Tonya_, _Terminal_, and _Barbie_, the company was also behind the TV series _Dollface_ and the miniseries _Maid_. They also produced director Emerald Fennell's films _Promising Young Woman_ and _Saltburn._

![Image 9: Barry Keogh in burgundy robe overlooking a park with people and scattered objects in Saltburn](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/20/asset/b494186aa7dd/sub-buzz-2253-1711137616-1.jpg)

 MGM / Courtesy Everett Collection 

As for what Margot first thought of _Saltburn_'s many infamous scenes, she told [Variety](https://variety.com/2024/film/features/margot-robbie-luckychap-barbie-saltburn-shocks-being-original-1235858528/) in January, "It didn't feel that shocking in the script, because Emerald immerses you into a world so quickly. She's so masterful at tone and plot; she gets you into it so quickly — you're just immediately like, 'I'm in this world.' So by the time you get to something like the bathtub scene, she's primed you for it. She's got you. You're, like, picking at a scab; you're like, 'I can't help myself.' Or like popping a pimple: 'I know I shouldn't squeeze, but I'm gonna.'"

## 2.Will Ferrell: _May December_ (2023)

![Image 11: Will in gray suit and red tie standing against a backdrop with Netflix logo](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/20/asset/f2bf74135d1c/sub-buzz-8784-1704399053-1.jpg)

 Valerie Macon / AFP via Getty Images 

## Will and Adam McKay produced numerous films and TV shows together through their production company, Gary Sanchez Productions. This includes hits like _Step Brothers_, _Vice_, _The Menu_, and _Succession_. [Following the end of Gary Sanchez Productions](https://variety.com/2019/film/news/will-ferrell-adam-mckay-cease-production-partnership-1203182411/), Will shifted his producing efforts in recent years to women-centered content alongside producer Jessica Elbaum through sister label Gloria Sanchez Productions. The company is behind films like _Booksmart_, _Hustlers_, and _May December_.

![Image 13: Julianne Moore and Natalie Portman in a dressing room, Natalie holding a notepad, Julianne with makeup, in May December](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/20/asset/6665ff65f148/sub-buzz-5729-1711137683-1.jpg)

 Francois Duhamel / © Netflix / Courtesy Everett Colleection 

Will told [Vanity Fair](https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/may-december-producers-will-ferrell-jessica-elbaum-awards-insider)in January, "It just kind of happened this way" that he's begun producing women-centric content. "If the planet is a school bus, men have been driving it since the beginning of civilization," he continued. "It's women's turn to take over the wheel."

## 3.Barack Obama: _Leave the World Behind_ (2023)

![Image 15: Barack Obama speaking at an event, wearing a suit without a tie, gesturing with his right hand](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/21/asset/af6b6e3cbb0d/sub-buzz-9642-1704402612-1.jpg)

 Spencer Platt / Getty Images 

## Through their production company Higher Ground, Barack and Michelle Obama worked on the film about a dystopian future amid a blackout. The movie is based on Rumaan Alam's 2020 novel of the same name. "He had a lot [of] notes about the characters and the empathy we would have for them," the film's director and writer, Sam Esmail, told [Vanity Fair](https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/09/leave-the-world-behind-movie-first-look) last year of the former president's involvement. "I have to say he is a big movie lover, and he wasn't just giving notes about things that were from his background. He was giving notes as a fan of the book, and he wanted to see a really good film."

![Image 17: Four actors, including Mahershala Ali and Julia Roberts, stand together with serious expressions](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/25/20/asset/945dd8348252/sub-buzz-1053-1711399351-1.jpg)

 JoJo Whilden / © Netflix / Courtesy Everett Collection 

Last year, Higher Ground also produced _Rustin_, the Bayard Rustin biopic starring Colman Domingo.

## 4.Maria Bello: _The Woman King_ (2022)

![Image 19: Maria smiling at a media event wearing a suit and tie](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/21/asset/f2bf74135d1c/sub-buzz-8980-1704402497-1.jpg)

 Matt Winkelmeyer / Getty Images 

## "_The Woman King_ was definitely born of my love of the continent in general," Maria told the [Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lifestyle/lifestyle-news/the-woman-king-producer-maria-bello-kenya-1235199627/) in 2022, referring to Africa. "It's based on women's history, a story I found many years ago about this army of women in the 17th century. I was watching _Braveheart_ and I was like, 'Why isn't there a woman's movie like this?'"

![Image 21: Viola Davis in traditional warrior attire stands confidently in a bustling village setting at night](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/20/asset/b494186aa7dd/sub-buzz-2261-1711137865-2.jpg)

 TriStar Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection 

Maria [pitched](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/viola-davis-gina-prince-bythewood-the-woman-king-1235210487/) the film to Viola Davis, who came aboard as a producer alongside her husband and producing partner, Julius Tennon, through their company, JuVee Productions. Viola also starred in the film.

## 5.Reese Witherspoon: _Where the Crawdads Sing_ (2022)

![Image 23: Reese Witherspoon smiling, wearing a strapless red gown at the SAG Awards](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/28/15/asset/edacc7ee2d7d/sub-buzz-1049-1711640634-4.jpg)

 Frazer Harrison / Getty Images 

## _Where the Crawdads Sing_ is based on Delia Owens's 2018 novel of the same name. Reese's involvement with the book turned movie came after she [selected the novel](https://reesesbookclub.com/article/4eRlfCOXueqPrm6ZnQpzwl) that year as a book for her book club. Then Reese's production company, Hello Sunshine, produced the adaptation.

![Image 25: Woman standing in the woods, looking forward, with a tree trunk behind her](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/25/20/asset/1647495bdca8/sub-buzz-539-1711399879-1.jpg)

 Michele K. Short / © Sony Pictures Entertainment / Courtesy Everett Collection 

"Shortly after, one of my very dearest friends and closest collaborators called me and said, 'So we make it into a movie? And I was like, 'Yessss! That would be amazing!" Reese told[_Entertainment Tonight_](https://www.etonline.com/reese-witherspoon-reflects-on-taking-where-the-crawdads-sing-from-book-club-to-the-big-screen)in 2022. "From there, we just started going, and it's just been a dream come true."

## 6.Denzel Washington: _Ma Rainey's Black Bottom_ (2020)

![Image 27: Denzel in a black suit and tie at an event](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/21/asset/58847356212f/sub-buzz-1459-1704405002-1.jpg)

 Angela Weiss / AFP via Getty Images 

## "I put my two cents in where I could, but in all seriousness, I really tried to stay out of the way," Denzel told [the Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/film/2020/dec/04/he-will-be-remembered-as-a-hero-denzel-washington-and-viola-davis-on-chadwick-boseman) in 2020 about producing the film based on August Wilson's play of the same name.

![Image 29: Viola Davis as Ma Rainey in patterned dress singing with jazz band members playing instruments in vintage room](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/21/asset/9d80fe9d54fb/sub-buzz-1028-1711141285-12.jpg)

 David Lee / © Netflix / Courtesy Everett Collection 

According to [Variety](https://variety.com/2021/awards/news/chadwick-boseman-ma-raineys-black-bottom-denzel-washington-1234936791/), _Ma Rainey's Black Bottom_ is one of the late playwright's 10 plays, known as the Pittsburgh Cycle or the Century Cycle, that Denzel is working to adapt to the screen. Another was _Fences_, which was adapted in 2016. Denzel starred in, directed, and produced that adaptation.

## 7.Bradley Cooper: _Joker_ (2019)

![Image 31: Bradley Cooper stands smiling in a tailored navy suit with a tie, at a Netflix event for "Maestro"](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/21/asset/98fc5e8400eb/sub-buzz-1988-1704402887-1.jpg)

 Axelle/Bauer-Griffin / FilmMagic / Getty Images 

## "We kept this one pretty close to us," Jeff Groth, the film editor on _Joker_, told [IndieWire](https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/bradley-cooper-joker-editing-room-1202205304/) in 2020. "We screened it more personally for people and filmmakers. Bradley Cooper definitely came in a couple of times. He was a producer on the movie, but he definitely watched the movie many times and sat with us. We could call him if we got stuck with something and be like, 'Hey, can you come over and take a look at things?'"

![Image 33: Joaquin Phoenix dressed as the Joker dancing on steps](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/20/asset/9d80fe9d54fb/sub-buzz-1017-1711141154-8.jpg)

 Niko Tavernise / © Warner Bros. / Courtesy Everett Collection 

## 8.Eva Longoria: _John Wick_ (2014)

![Image 35: Eva Longoria poses in a pastel blazer over a neutral top at an event](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-01/4/21/asset/2547ef6525a8/sub-buzz-1848-1704405433-9.jpg)

 Alberto Rodriguez / Variety via Getty Images 

## In 2019, Eva told [GQ](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TujB7dvy1Jk) of producing the film, "I saved the movie...I really did. It was fun. Keanu was amazing, and it was an amazing movie."

![Image 37: Keanu Reeves as John Wick walking determinedly in a dimly lit space with damaged cars and debris around](https://img.buzzfeed.com/buzzfeed-static/static/2024-03/22/21/asset/63eca66dd73a/sub-buzz-1774-1711141367-1.jpg)

 David Lee / © Summit Entertainment / Courtesy Everett Collection 

Chad Stahelski and David Leitch [directed the film](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/keanu-reeves-john-wick-directors-743810/). Chad told the[Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/john-wick-filmmaker-chad-stahelski-sequels-oscar-stunt-snubs-firearms-1235343132/)last year of Eva's involvement, "The first _John Wick_ was independent, and someone went to her with it as an investment opportunity. When Dave Leitch and I were filming, we didn't even know about it. We didn't meet her until well after the movie came out. We eventually met her at Chateau Marmont for lunch one day, and she's like, 'Hi, I'm Eva. Isn't this the weirdest thing?' We actually made her a bunch of money, which is awesome, so she felt like she should take us to lunch."

## 9.Pharrell Williams: _Hidden Figures_ (2016)

"I'm appreciative for that wiggle room and to be part of the conversation."

 Angela Weiss / AFP via Getty Images 

## Tom and Rita produced _Mamma Mia_ and the sequel films through Tom's production company, Playtone _,_ which he cofounded with Gary Goetzman _._ According to [Vulture](https://www.vulture.com/2018/01/tom-hanks-was-rejected-from-a-role-in-mamma-mia.html), Tom said on _The Graham Norton Show_ in 2018, "I was a producer of _Mamma Mia_ and I tried out for a role. Nia Vardalos, who starred in and wrote all three films in the series, was running a one-woman play in the late '90s. Rita, a fellow Greek actor, attended and subsequently convinced Tom and Playtone to [turn the play into the first film](https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/movies/2023/09/08/rita-wilson-big-fat-greek-wedding/70794308007/), which remains the [highest-grossing rom-com to date](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/hollywood-flashback-my-big-fat-greek-wedding-shattered-expectations-1235582348/).
