Affleck is a supporter of [Paralyzed Veterans of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paralyzed_Veterans_of_America "Paralyzed Veterans of America").[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-251) He filmed public service announcements for the organization in both 2009 and 2014.[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-252)[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-253) He has also volunteered on behalf of [Operation Gratitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Gratitude "Operation Gratitude").[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-254)[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-255)

Affleck is a member of [Feeding America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feeding_America "Feeding America")'s Entertainment Council.[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-256) He made an appearance at the [Greater Boston Food Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Boston_Food_Bank "Greater Boston Food Bank") in 2007,[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-257) and at a Denver food bank in 2008.[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-258) Affleck spoke at a Feeding America rally in Washington D.C. in 2009,[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-259) and filmed a public service announcement for the charity in 2010.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-260) Affleck and [Ellen DeGeneres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellen_DeGeneres "Ellen DeGeneres") launched Feeding America's Small Change Campaign in 2011.[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-261) Also that year, he and [Howard Graham Buffett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Graham_Buffett "Howard Graham Buffett") co-wrote an article for _The Huffington Post_, highlighting the "growing percentage of the food insecure population that is not eligible for federal nutrition programs".[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-262) During the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), Affleck organized an online celebrity poker tournament to benefit the charity,[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-263) made a personal donation and urged others to support the cause.[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-264)

## Politics

### Political views

Affleck has described himself as "moderately [liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_liberalism_in_the_United_States "Modern liberalism in the United States")."[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-Fox_News-270) He was raised in "a very strong [union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_union "Trade union") household".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-salon.com-29) In 2000, he spoke at a rally at [Harvard University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University") in support of an increased living wage for all workers on campus; his father worked as a janitor at the university.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-harvard-19) He later narrated a documentary, _Occupation_ (2002), about a sit-in organized by the Harvard Living Wage Campaign.[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-271) Affleck and Senator [Ted Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Kennedy "Ted Kennedy") held a press conference on Capitol Hill in 2004, pushing for an increase in the [minimum wage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_wage_in_the_United_States "Minimum wage in the United States").[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-272) He spoke at a 2007 press conference at Boston's City Hall in support of [SEIU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_Employees_International_Union "Service Employees International Union")'s unionization efforts for the city's low-paid hospital workers.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-273) During the [Writers' Strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Writers_Guild_of_America_strike "2007–08 Writers Guild of America strike") in 2008, Affleck voiced support for the picketers.[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-274)

Affleck is [pro-choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_abortion-rights_movement "United States abortion-rights movement"). In a 2000 interview, he stated that he believes "very strongly in a woman's right to choose".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-salon.com-29) In 2012, he supported the [Draw the Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Reproductive_Rights "Center for Reproductive Rights") campaign, describing reproductive rights as "fundamental".[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-275)

Affleck was a longtime supporter of legalizing [gay marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_marriage "Gay marriage"), saying in 2004 that he hoped to look back on the marriage debate "with some degree of embarrassment for how antiquated it was".[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-276) Also that year, he remarked that it was "outrageous and offensive" to suggest members of the [transgender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") community were not entitled to equal rights.[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-277) He appeared alongside his gay cousin in a 2005 [Parents and Friends of Lesbians and Gays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parents_and_Friends_of_Lesbians_and_Gays "Parents and Friends of Lesbians and Gays") print advertising campaign.[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-278)
