**Benjamin Géza Affleck**[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-3) (born August 15, 1972) is an American actor and filmmaker. [His accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Ben_Affleck "List of awards and nominations received by Ben Affleck") include two [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"), two [BAFTA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Awards "BAFTA Awards"), and three [Golden Globes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globes "Golden Globes"). Affleck began his career as a child when he starred in the [PBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBS "PBS") educational series _[The Voyage of the Mimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Voyage\_of\_the\_Mimi "The Voyage of the Mimi")_ (1984–1988). He later appeared in the independent comedy _[Dazed and Confused](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dazed\_and\_Confused\_(film) "Dazed and Confused (film)")_ (1993) and several [Kevin Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Smith "Kevin Smith") comedies, including _[Mallrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats "Mallrats")_ (1995), _[Chasing Amy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chasing\_Amy "Chasing Amy")_ (1997), and _[Dogma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dogma\_(film) "Dogma (film)")_ (1999).

Affleck gained wider recognition when he and [Matt Damon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Damon "Matt Damon") won the [Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay") for writing _[Good Will Hunting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good\_Will\_Hunting "Good Will Hunting")_ (1997), which they also starred in. He established himself as a leading man in studio films, including the disaster film _[Armageddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armageddon\_(1998\_film) "Armageddon (1998 film)")_ (1998), the action crime thriller _[Reindeer Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reindeer\_Games "Reindeer Games")_ (2000), the war drama _[Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl\_Harbor\_(film) "Pearl Harbor (film)")_ (2001), and the thriller _[The Sum of All Fears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sum\_of\_All\_Fears\_(film) "The Sum of All Fears (film)")_ (2002). After a career downturn, Affleck made a comeback by portraying [George Reeves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Reeves "George Reeves") in the biopic _[Hollywoodland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywoodland "Hollywoodland")_ (2006), winning the [Volpi Cup for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volpi_Cup_for_Best_Actor "Volpi Cup for Best Actor").

His directorial debut, _[Gone Baby Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone\_Baby\_Gone "Gone Baby Gone")_ (2007), which he also co-wrote, was well received. He then directed and starred in the crime drama _[The Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Town\_(2010\_film) "The Town (2010 film)")_ (2010) and the political thriller _[Argo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argo\_(2012\_film) "Argo (2012 film)")_ (2012), both of which were critical and commercial successes. For the latter, Affleck won the [BAFTA Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Director "BAFTA Award for Best Director"), and the [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Film "BAFTA Award for Best Film") and [Academy Award for Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). Affleck then starred in the psychological thriller _[Gone Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone\_Girl\_(film) "Gone Girl (film)")_ (2014) and played the superhero [Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Wayne_(DC_Extended_Universe) "Bruce Wayne (DC Extended Universe)") in the [DC Extended Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Extended_Universe "DC Extended Universe") (2016–2023). He starred in the thriller _[The Accountant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Accountant\_(2016\_film) "The Accountant (2016 film)")_ (2016) and the sports drama _[The Way Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Way\_Back\_(2020\_film) "The Way Back (2020 film)")_ (2020). Affleck had supporting roles in the dramas _[The Last Duel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Duel\_(2021\_film) "The Last Duel (2021 film)")_ (2021), _[The Tender Bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tender\_Bar\_(film) "The Tender Bar (film)")_ (2021) and _[Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air\_(2023\_American\_film) "Air (2023 American film)")_ (2023), the third of which he also directed.

Affleck is the co-founder of the [Eastern Congo Initiative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Congo_Initiative "Eastern Congo Initiative"), a [grantmaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grantmaking "Grantmaking") and advocacy-based nonprofit organization. He is a supporter of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"). Affleck and Damon are co-owners of the production company [Artists Equity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artists_Equity "Artists Equity") and were also co-owners of [Pearl Street Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Street_Films "Pearl Street Films").

## Early life

Affleck was born Benjamin Géza Affleck-Boldt on August 15, 1972, in [Berkeley, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkeley,_California "Berkeley, California").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-fullname-4)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-5) His family moved to Massachusetts when he was three,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-viewaskew1-6) living in [Falmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falmouth,_Massachusetts "Falmouth, Massachusetts"), where his brother [Casey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Affleck "Casey Affleck") was born, before settling in [Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_Massachusetts "Cambridge, Massachusetts").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-Morris_full-7) His mother, Christopher Anne "Chris" Boldt,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-8)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-9) was a [Harvard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University")-educated elementary school teacher.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-auto-10)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-:0-11) His father, Timothy Byers Affleck,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-nytimes2000-12)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-People2026TimothyAffleck-13) was an aspiring playwright[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-nytimes2000-12) who was "mostly unemployed".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-14) Ben’s father worked sporadically as a carpenter,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-highbeam1-15) auto mechanic,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-viewaskew1-6)[bookie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bookmaker "Bookmaker"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-kinja1-16) electrician,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-washingtonpost1-17) bartender,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-bostonmagazine2006-18) and janitor at Harvard.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-harvard-19) In the mid-1960s, he had been an actor and stage manager with the [Theater Company of Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theater_Company_of_Boston "Theater Company of Boston").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-20)

During Affleck's childhood, his father had a self-described "severe, chronic problem with alcoholism",[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-people1-21) and Affleck has recalled him drinking "all day ... every day".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-22) His father was "very difficult",[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-23) and Affleck felt a sense of "relief" at the age of 11 when his parents divorced,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-24)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-mosaic-25) and his father exited the family home.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-people1-21)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-nytimes2000-12) His father continued to drink heavily[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-auto-10) and eventually became homeless, spending two years living on the streets of Cambridge.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-kinja1-16)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-26) When Affleck was 16, his father entered a rehabilitation facility in [Indio, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indio,_California "Indio, California"). He lived at the facility for 12 years to maintain his sobriety[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-wtf-27) and worked there as an addiction counselor.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-auto-10)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-28)

Affleck was raised in a politically active, liberal household.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-kinja1-16)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-salon.com-29) He and his brother, Casey, were surrounded by people who worked in the arts;[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-30) the boys regularly attended theater performances with their mother[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-31) and were encouraged to make their own [home movies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_movies "Home movies").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-32)[David Wheeler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Wheeler_(stage_director) "David Wheeler (stage director)"), a family friend, later remembered Affleck as a "very bright and intensely curious" child.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-people2-33) The brothers auditioned for roles in local commercials and film productions because of their mother's friendship with a Cambridge-area casting director,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-bostonmagazine2006-18) and Affleck first acted professionally at the age of seven.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-people2-33) His mother saved his wages in a college trust fund[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-nytimes2000-12) and hoped her son would ultimately become a teacher, worrying that acting was an insecure and "frivolous" profession.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-Los_Angeles_Times-34) When Affleck was 13, he filmed a children's television program in Mexico. He learned to speak Spanish during a year spent traveling around the country with his mother and brother.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-35)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-36)

As a [Cambridge Rindge and Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge_Rindge_and_Latin_School "Cambridge Rindge and Latin School") high school student, Affleck acted in theater productions and was inspired by drama teacher Gerry Speca.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-37)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-cbsnews1-38) He became close friends with fellow student [Matt Damon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Damon "Matt Damon"), whom he had known since the age of eight.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-interviewmagazine1-39) Although Damon was two years older, the pair had "identical interests" and both wanted to pursue acting careers.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-interviewmagazine1-39) They traveled to New York together for acting auditions[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-Parade-40) and saved money for train and airline tickets in a joint bank account.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-41) While Affleck had high [SAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAT "SAT") scores,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-nytimes2000-12) he was largely an unfocused student with poor attendance.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-auto-10)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-42) He spent a few months studying Spanish at the [University of Vermont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Vermont "University of Vermont"), chosen because of its proximity to his then-girlfriend,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-washingtonpost1-17) but he left after fracturing his hip while playing basketball.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-Parade-40) At 18, Affleck moved to Los Angeles,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-Los_Angeles_Times-34) studying Middle Eastern affairs at [Occidental College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occidental_College "Occidental College") for a year and a half.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-43)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-44)

## Career

### 1981–1997: Child acting and _Good Will Hunting_

Affleck acted professionally throughout his childhood but, in his own words, "not in the sense that I had a mom that wanted to take me to Hollywood or a family that wanted to make money from me ... I kind of chanced into something."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceA-45) He first appeared, at the age of seven, in an independent film, _[The Dark End of the Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_End\_of\_the\_Street\_(1981\_film) "The Dark End of the Street (1981 film)")_ (1981), directed by a family friend.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-46) His biggest success as a child actor was as the star of the [PBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBS "PBS") children's series _[The Voyage of the Mimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Voyage\_of\_the\_Mimi "The Voyage of the Mimi")_ (1984) and _[The Second Voyage of the Mimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Second\_Voyage\_of\_the\_Mimi "The Second Voyage of the Mimi")_ (1988), produced for sixth-grade science classes. Affleck worked "sporadically" on _Mimi_ from the age of eight to fifteen in both Massachusetts and Mexico.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceA-45) As a teenager, he appeared in the [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")[after school special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_school_special "After school special")_Wanted: A Perfect Man_ (1986),[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-47) the television film _Hands of a Stranger_ (1987),[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceA-45) and a 1989 [Burger King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burger_King "Burger King") commercial.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-cbsnews1-38)

After high school, Affleck moved briefly to New York in search of acting work.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceA-45) Later, while studying at Occidental College in Los Angeles, Affleck directed [student films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Killed_My_Lesbian_Wife,_Hung_Her_on_a_Meat_Hook,_and_Now_I_Have_a_Three-Picture_Deal_at_Disney "I Killed My Lesbian Wife, Hung Her on a Meat Hook, and Now I Have a Three-Picture Deal at Disney").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-kinja1-16)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-48) As an actor, he had a series of "knock-around parts, one to the next".[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceA-45) He played [Patrick Duffy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Duffy "Patrick Duffy")'s son in the television film _[Daddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daddy\_(1991\_film) "Daddy (1991 film)")_ (1991), made an uncredited appearance as a basketball player in the _[Buffy the Vampire Slayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffy\_the\_Vampire\_Slayer\_(film) "Buffy the Vampire Slayer (film)")_ film (1992), and had a supporting role as a prep school student in _[School Ties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School\_Ties "School Ties")_ (1992).[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-49) He played a high school quarterback in the [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") television series _[Against the Grain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Against\_the\_Grain\_(TV\_series) "Against the Grain (TV series)")_ (1993), and a steroid-abusing high school football player in _[\_Body to Die For: The Aaron Henry Story\_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifestories:\_Families\_in\_Crisis "Lifestories: Families in Crisis")_ (1994). Affleck's most notable role during this period was as a high school bully in [Richard Linklater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Linklater "Richard Linklater")'s cult classic _[Dazed and Confused](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dazed\_and\_Confused\_(film) "Dazed and Confused (film)")_ (1993).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-50) Linklater wanted a likable actor for the villainous role, and, while Affleck was "big and imposing", he was "so smart and full of life ... I just liked him."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-51)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-52) Affleck later said Linklater was instrumental in demystifying the filmmaking process for him.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-kinja1-16)

Affleck's first starring film role was as an aimless art student in the college drama _[Glory Daze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glory\_Daze\_(film) "Glory Daze (film)")_ (1995), with Stephen Holden of _The New York Times_ remarking that his "affably mopey performance finds just the right balance between obnoxious and sad sack".[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-53) He then played a bully in filmmaker [Kevin Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Smith "Kevin Smith")'s comedy _[Mallrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mallrats "Mallrats")_ (1995) and became friends with Smith during the filming. Affleck had begun to worry that he would be relegated to a career of "throwing people into their lockers",[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceA-45) but Smith wrote him a lead role in the romantic comedy _[Chasing Amy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chasing\_Amy "Chasing Amy")_ (1997).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-viewaskew1-6)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceA-45) The film was Affleck's breakthrough.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceA-45)[Janet Maslin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Maslin "Janet Maslin") of _The New York Times_ praised Affleck's "wonderful ease" playing the role, combining "suave good looks with cool comic timing".[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-54) Owen Gleiberman of _Entertainment Weekly_ described it as a "wholesome and quick-witted" performance.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-55) When Affleck starred as a recently returned Korean War veteran in the coming-of-age drama _[Going All the Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Going\_All\_the\_Way "Going All the Way")_ (1997), Todd McCarthy of _Variety_ found him "excellent",[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-56) while Janet Maslin of _The New York Times_ noted that his "flair for comic self-doubt made a strong impression."[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-57)

[![Image 7: Bill Clinton, Ben Affleck, and Matt Damon sit on two sofas while looking towards a television screen](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/CampDavid.jpg/250px-CampDavid.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CampDavid.jpg)

Affleck and Matt Damon attend a [Camp David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_David "Camp David") screening of _Good Will Hunting_ with President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") in January 1998.

The success of 1997's _[Good Will Hunting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good\_Will\_Hunting "Good Will Hunting")_, which Affleck co-wrote and acted in, marked a turning point in his career. The screenplay originated in 1992 when Damon wrote a 40-page script for a playwriting class at Harvard University.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-bostonmag-history-58) He asked Affleck to act out the scenes with him in front of the class and, when Damon later moved into Affleck's Los Angeles apartment, they began working on the script in earnest.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-interviewmagazine1-39) The film, which they wrote mainly during improvisation sessions, was set partly in their hometown of Cambridge and drew from their own experiences.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-bostonmag-history-58)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-59) The screenplay was borne of their desire to create "an acting reel" for themselves.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-keegan-60) They sold the screenplay to [Castle Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castle_Rock_Entertainment "Castle Rock Entertainment") in 1994 when Affleck was 22 years old. During the development process, they received notes from industry figures, including [Rob Reiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Reiner "Rob Reiner") and [William Goldman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Goldman "William Goldman").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-61) Following a lengthy dispute with Castle Rock about a suitable director, Affleck and Damon persuaded [Miramax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miramax "Miramax") to purchase the screenplay.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-highbeam1-15) The two friends moved back to Boston for a year before the film finally went into production, directed by [Gus Van Sant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Van_Sant "Gus Van Sant"), and co-starring Damon, Affleck, [Minnie Driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnie_Driver "Minnie Driver"), and [Robin Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Williams "Robin Williams").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-bostonmag-history-58)

On its release, Janet Maslin of _The New York Times_ praised the "smart and touching screenplay",[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-62) while Emanuel Levy of _Variety_ found it "funny, nonchalant, moving and angry".[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-63) Jay Carr of _The Boston Globe_ wrote that Affleck brought "a beautifully nuanced tenderness" to his role as the working-class friend of Damon's mathematical prodigy character.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-64) Affleck and Damon eventually won the [Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Writing_Original_Screenplay "Academy Award for Writing Original Screenplay").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-kinja1-16) Affleck has described this period of his life as "dreamlike": "It was like one of those scenes in an old movie when a newspaper comes spinning out of the black on to the screen. You know, '$100 Million Box Office! Awards!'"[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-Parade-40) He remains the youngest writer (at age 25) ever to win an Oscar for screenwriting.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-bostonmag-history-58)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-65)

### 1998–2002: Leading man status

[![Image 8: Ben Affleck, Michael Bay and Liv Tyler posing on the red carpet](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Bay_Affleck_Tyler_at_JFK_Space_Center_Armageddon_premiere_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Bay_Affleck_Tyler_at_JFK_Space_Center_Armageddon_premiere_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bay_Affleck_Tyler_at_JFK_Space_Center_Armageddon_premiere_(cropped).jpg)

Affleck with [Michael Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay "Michael Bay") and [Liv Tyler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liv_Tyler "Liv Tyler") at the _[Armageddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armageddon\_(1998\_film) "Armageddon (1998 film)")_ premiere in June 1998

_[Armageddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armageddon\_(1998\_film) "Armageddon (1998 film)")_, released in 1998, established Affleck as a viable leading man for Hollywood studio films. _Good Will Hunting_ had not yet been released during the casting process and, after Affleck's [screen test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_test "Screen test"), director [Michael Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay "Michael Bay") dismissed him as “a [geek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geek "Geek")". Producer [Jerry Bruckheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Bruckheimer "Jerry Bruckheimer") convinced Bay that Affleck would be a star,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-Los_Angeles_Times-34) but he was required to lose weight, become tanned, and get his teeth capped before filming began.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-66) The film, where he starred opposite [Bruce Willis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Willis "Bruce Willis") as a blue-collar driller tasked by [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") with stopping an asteroid from colliding with Earth, was a box office success.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-67) Daphne Merkin of _The New Yorker_ remarked: "Affleck demonstrates a sexy [Paul Newmanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Newman "Paul Newman") charm and is clearly bound for stardom."[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-68)

Later in 1998, Affleck had a supporting role as an arrogant English actor in the period romantic comedy _[Shakespeare in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespeare\_in\_Love "Shakespeare in Love")_, starring his then-girlfriend [Gwyneth Paltrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwyneth_Paltrow "Gwyneth Paltrow"). Lael Loewenstein of _Variety_ remarked that Affleck "does some of his very best work, suggesting that comedy may be his true calling,"[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-69) while Janet Maslin of _The New York Times_ found him "very funny".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-70)_Shakespeare in Love_ won seven [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"), including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"), while the cast won the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Cast_in_a_Motion_Picture "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture"). Affleck then appeared as a small-town sheriff in the supernatural horror film _[Phantoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phantoms\_(film) "Phantoms (film)")_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceA-45) Stephen Holden of _The New York Times_ wondered why actors like Affleck and [Peter O'Toole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_O'Toole "Peter O'Toole") had agreed to appear in the "junky" film: "Affleck's thudding performance suggests he is reading his dialogue for the first time, directly from cue cards."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-71)

Affleck and Damon had an on-screen reunion in Kevin Smith's religious satire _[Dogma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dogma\_(film) "Dogma (film)")_, which premiered at the [1999 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_Cannes_Film_Festival "1999 Cannes Film Festival"). Janet Maslin of _The New York Times_ remarked that the pair, playing fallen angels, "bring great, understandable enthusiasm to Mr. Smith's smart talk and wild imaginings".[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-72) Affleck starred opposite [Sandra Bullock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Bullock "Sandra Bullock") in the romantic comedy _[Forces of Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forces\_of\_Nature\_(1999\_film) "Forces of Nature (1999 film)")_ (1999), playing a groom whose attempts to get to his wedding are complicated by his free-spirited traveling companion. [Joe Leydon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Leydon "Joe Leydon") of _Variety_ praised "his winning ability to play against his good looks in a self-effacing comic turn."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-73) Affleck then appeared opposite [Courtney Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Courtney_Love "Courtney Love") in the little-seen ensemble comedy _[200 Cigarettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/200\_Cigarettes "200 Cigarettes")_ (1999).[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-74)

Interested in a directorial career, Affleck shadowed [John Frankenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Frankenheimer "John Frankenheimer") throughout pre-production of the action thriller _[Reindeer Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reindeer\_Games "Reindeer Games")_ (2000).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-Los_Angeles_Times-34)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceB-75) Frankenheimer, directing his last feature film, described Affleck as having "a very winning, likable quality about him. I've been doing this for a long time and he's really one of the nicest."[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-76) He starred opposite [Charlize Theron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron "Charlize Theron") as a hardened criminal, with Elvis Mitchell of _The New York Times_ enjoying the unexpected casting choice: "Affleck often suggests one of the [Kennedys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_family "Kennedy family") playing [Clark Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clark_Kent "Clark Kent") ... He looks as if he has never missed a party or a night's sleep. He's game, though, and his slight dislocation works to the advantage of _Reindeer Games_."[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-77) He then had a supporting role as a ruthless stockbroker in the crime drama _[Boiler Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boiler\_Room\_(film) "Boiler Room (film)")_ (2000).[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceB-75)[A.O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.O._Scott "A.O. Scott") of _The New York Times_ felt Affleck had merely "traced over" [Alec Baldwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alec_Baldwin "Alec Baldwin")'s performance in _[Glengarry Glen Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glengarry\_Glen\_Ross "Glengarry Glen Ross")_,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-78) while Peter Rainer of _New York Magazine_ said he "does a series of riffs on Baldwin's aria, and each one is funnier and crueler than the next".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-79) He provided the voice of Joseph in the animated _[Joseph: King of Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph:\_King\_of\_Dreams "Joseph: King of Dreams")_.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-80) In his last film role of 2000, Affleck starred opposite his girlfriend Paltrow in the romantic drama _[Bounce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bounce\_(film) "Bounce (film)")_. Stephen Holden of _The New York Times_ praised the "understated intensity and exquisite detail" of his performance: "His portrait of a young, sarcastically self-defined 'people person' who isn't half as confident as he would like to appear is close to definitive."[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-81)

Affleck reunited with director Michael Bay for the critically derided war drama _[Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl\_Harbor\_(film) "Pearl Harbor (film)")_ (2001).[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-82) Todd McCarthy of _Variety_ wrote "the blandly handsome Affleck couldn't convince that he'd ever so much as been turned down for a date, much less lost the love of his life to his best friend".[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-83) Affleck then parodied _Good Will Hunting_ with Damon and Van Sant in Kevin Smith's _[Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay\_and\_Silent\_Bob\_Strike\_Back "Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back")_ (2001),[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-84) made a cameo in the comedy _[Daddy and Them](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daddy\_and\_Them "Daddy and Them")_ (2001),[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-85) and had a supporting role in the little-seen _[The Third Wheel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Third\_Wheel\_(film) "The Third Wheel (film)")_ (2002).[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-people2-33) He portrayed the [CIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIA "CIA") analyst [Jack Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Ryan_(Tom_Clancy) "Jack Ryan (Tom Clancy)") in the thriller _[The Sum of All Fears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sum\_of\_All\_Fears\_(film) "The Sum of All Fears (film)")_ (2002). Stephen Holden of _The New York Times_ felt he was miscast in a role previously played by both [Harrison Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford "Harrison Ford") and Alec Baldwin: "Although Mr. Affleck can be appealing when playing earnest young men groping toward maturity, he simply lacks the gravitas for the role."[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-86) Affleck had an "amazing experience" making the thriller _[Changing Lanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changing\_Lanes "Changing Lanes")_ (2002),[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceA-45) and later cited [Roger Michell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Michell "Roger Michell") as someone he learned from as a director.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceB-75)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-87) Robert Koehler of _Variety_ described it as one of his "most thoroughly wrought" performances: "The journey into a moral fog compels him to play more inwardly and thoughtfully than he ever has before."[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-88)

Affleck became more involved with television and film production in the early 2000s. He and Damon had set up [Pearl Street Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Street_Films "Pearl Street Films") in 1998,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-89) named after the street that ran between their childhood homes.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-lauraholson-90) Their next production company [LivePlanet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LivePlanet "LivePlanet"), co-founded in 2000 with [Sean Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Bailey "Sean Bailey") and [Chris Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Moore_(film_producer) "Chris Moore (film producer)"), sought to integrate the Internet into mainstream television and film production.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-lauraholson-90)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-Laura_M._Holson-91) LivePlanet's biggest success was the documentary series _[Project Greenlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project\_Greenlight "Project Greenlight")_, aired on [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") and later [Bravo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bravo_(U.S._TV_network) "Bravo (U.S. TV network)"), which focused on first-time filmmakers being given the chance to direct a feature film. _Project Greenlight_ was nominated for the [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Reality Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Reality_Program "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Reality Program") in 2002, 2004, and 2005.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-92)_[Push, Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push,\_Nevada "Push, Nevada")_ (2002), created, written, and produced by Affleck and Bailey,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-93) was an [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") mystery drama series that placed a viewer-participation game within the frame of the show.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-94)[Caryn James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caryn_James "Caryn James") of _The New York Times_ praised the show's "nerve, imagination, and clever writing",[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-95) but Robert Bianco of _USA Today_ described it as a "knock-off" of _[Twin Peaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin\_Peaks "Twin Peaks")_.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-96) The show was canceled by ABC after seven episodes due to low ratings.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-97) Over time, LivePlanet's focus shifted from multimedia projects to more traditional film production.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-Laura_M._Holson-91) Affleck and his partners signed a film production deal with [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") in 2002; it expired in 2007.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-98)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-99)

### 2003–2005: Career downturn and tabloid notoriety

While Affleck had been a tabloid figure for much of his career,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-people2-33) he was the subject of increased media attention in 2003 because of his relationship with Jennifer Lopez. By the end of the year, Affleck had become, in the words of _GQ_, the "world's most over-exposed actor".[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-100) His tabloid fame coincided with a series of poorly received films.

[![Image 9: Ben Affleck, with a trim goatee and moustache, is surrounded by hands reaching out to him.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Benafflecknavy1.jpg/250px-Benafflecknavy1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Benafflecknavy1.jpg)

Affleck visiting US Marines in [Manama, Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manama,_Bahrain "Manama, Bahrain") in 2003

The first of these was _[Daredevil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daredevil\_(film) "Daredevil (film)")_ (2003), in which Affleck starred as the [blind superhero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daredevil_(Marvel_Comics_character) "Daredevil (Marvel Comics character)"). Affleck was a longtime comic book fan, and, in 1999, had written a foreword for Kevin Smith's _[Guardian Devil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guardian\_Devil "Guardian Devil")_ about his love for the character of Daredevil.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-101) The film was a commercial success,[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-earnings-102) but received a mixed response from critics. Elvis Mitchell of _The New York Times_ said Affleck was "lost" in the role: "Affleck is shriveled by the one-dimensional role ... Only his scenes with [Jon Favreau have] a playful side that allows Mr. Affleck to show his generosity as an actor."[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-103) In 2014, Affleck described _Daredevil_ as the only film he regretted making.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-kinja1-16) He next appeared as a low-ranking mobster in the romantic comedy _[Gigli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigli\_(film) "Gigli (film)")_ (2003), co-starring Lopez. The film was almost uniformly panned,[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-104)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-105) with [Manohla Dargis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manohla_Dargis "Manohla Dargis") of the _Los Angeles Times_ remarking that "Affleck doesn't have the chops or the charm to maneuver around (or past) bad material."[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-106) Rex Reed of _[The Observer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observer.com "Observer.com")_ criticized the co-stars, writing that the film reminds the world how "pathetically incompetent they both are in the only two things that matter in career longevity—craft and talent."[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-107) Yet Affleck has repeatedly defended director [Martin Brest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Brest "Martin Brest") since the film's release, describing him as "one of the really great directors."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-ReferenceB-75)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-82) In his last film role of 2003, Affleck starred as a [reverse engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reverse_engineering "Reverse engineering") in the sci-fi thriller _[Paycheck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paycheck\_(film) "Paycheck (film)")_ (2003). Peter Bradshaw of _The Guardian_ remarked on Affleck's "self-deprecating charm" and wondered why he could not find better scripts.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-108) Manohla Dargis of the _Los Angeles Times_ found it "almost unfair" to critique Affleck, given that he “had such a rough year.”[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-109)

Affleck's poor critical notices continued in 2004 when he starred as a bereaved husband in the romantic comedy _[Jersey Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey\_Girl\_(2004\_film) "Jersey Girl (2004 film)")_, directed by longtime collaborator Smith. Stephen Holden of _The New York Times_ described Affleck as an actor "whose talent has curdled as his tabloid notoriety has spread."[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-110) Later that year, he starred opposite [James Gandolfini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Gandolfini "James Gandolfini") in the holiday comedy _[Surviving Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surviving\_Christmas "Surviving Christmas")_. Holden noted in _The New York Times_ that the film "found a clever way to use Ben Affleck's disagreeable qualities. The actor's shark-like grin, cocky petulance and bullying frat-boy swagger befit his character."[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-111) At this point, the quality of scripts offered to Affleck "was just getting worse and worse", the negative press coverage "really started to affect" him,[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-112) and he decided to take a career break.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-113) The _Los Angeles Times_ published a piece on the downfall of Affleck's career in late 2004. The article noted that, unlike film critics and tabloid journalists, "few industry professionals seem to be gloating over Affleck's travails.”[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-114)

### 2006–2015: Emergence as a director

Affleck began a career comeback in 2006 with his acclaimed performance as [Superman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman "Superman") actor [George Reeves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Reeves "George Reeves") in the noir biopic _[Hollywoodland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywoodland "Hollywoodland")_. [Peter Travers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Travers "Peter Travers") of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ praised "an award-caliber performance ... This is feeling, nuanced work from an actor some of us had prematurely written off."[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-stone-115) Geoffrey Macnab of _The Guardian_ said he "beautifully" captured "the character's curious mix of charm, vulnerability and fatalism".[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-116) He was awarded the [Volpi Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volpi_Cup "Volpi Cup") at the [Venice Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Film_Festival "Venice Film Festival") and was nominated for a [Golden Globe for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture "Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-117) Also in 2006, he made a cameo in Smith's _[Clerks II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clerks\_II "Clerks II")_,[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-118) starred in the little-seen _[Man About Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man\_About\_Town\_(2006\_film) "Man About Town (2006 film)")_ and had a minor role in the crime drama _[Smokin' Aces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smokin'\_Aces "Smokin' Aces")_.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-119)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-120)

In 2007, Affleck made his feature film directorial debut with _[Gone Baby Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone\_Baby\_Gone "Gone Baby Gone")_, a crime drama set in a working-class Boston neighborhood, starring his brother Casey as a private investigator searching for a young abductee. Affleck co‑wrote the screenplay, based on the [book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone,_Baby,_Gone_(novel) "Gone, Baby, Gone (novel)") by [Dennis Lehane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Lehane "Dennis Lehane"), with childhood friend Aaron Stockard, having first mentioned his intention to adapt the story in 2003.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-121)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-122) It opened to enthusiastic reviews.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-123) Manohla Dargis of _The New York Times_ praised the film's "sensitivity to real struggle,"[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-124) while Stephen Farber of _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ described it as "thoughtful, deeply poignant, [and] splendidly executed."[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-125)

While Affleck intended to "keep a primary emphasis on directing" going forward in his career,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-126) he acted in three films in 2009. In the ensemble romantic comedy _[He's Just Not That Into You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/He's\_Just\_Not\_That\_Into\_You\_(film) "He's Just Not That Into You (film)")_, the chemistry between Affleck and [Jennifer Aniston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Aniston "Jennifer Aniston") was praised.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-127)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-128) Affleck played a congressman in the political thriller _[State of Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State\_of\_Play\_(film) "State of Play (film)")_. Wesley Morris of _The Boston Globe_ found him "very good in the film's silliest role,"[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-129) but David Edelstein of _New York Magazine_ remarked of Affleck: "He might be smart and thoughtful in life [but] as an actor his wheels turn too slowly."[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-130) He had a supporting role as a bartender in the little-seen comedy film _[Extract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extract\_(film) "Extract (film)")_.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-131) Peter Travers of _Rolling Stone_ described his performance as "a goofball delight",[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-132) while Manohla Dargis of _The New York Times_ declared it "a real performance".[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-133) In 2010, Affleck starred in _[The Company Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Company\_Men "The Company Men")_ as a mid-level sales executive who is made redundant during the [2008 financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis "2008 financial crisis").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-134) David Denby of _The New Yorker_ declared that Affleck "gives his best performance yet",[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-135) while Richard Corliss of _Time_ found he "nails Bobby's plunge from hubris to humiliation".[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-136)

[![Image 10: Ben Affleck, wearing a tracksuit top, smiles](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/The_town_affleck.jpg/250px-The_town_affleck.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_town_affleck.jpg)

Affleck on the set of _[The Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Town\_(2010\_film) "The Town (2010 film)")_ in 2010

Following the modest commercial success of _Gone Baby Gone_, [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") developed a close working relationship with Affleck and offered him his choice of the studio's scripts.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-auto-10) He decided to direct the crime drama _[The Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Town\_(2010\_film) "The Town (2010 film)")_ (2010), an adaptation of [Chuck Hogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Hogan "Chuck Hogan")'s novel _Prince of Thieves_. He also re-wrote the screenplay and starred in the film as a bank robber. The film became a surprise box office hit, and gained further critical acclaim for Affleck.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-137)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-138) A.O. Scott of _The New York Times_ praised his "skill and self-confidence as a serious director,"[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-139) while Roger Ebert of the _Chicago Sun-Times_ noted: "Affleck has the stuff of a real director. Everything is here. It's an effective thriller, he works closely with actors, he has a feel for pacing."[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-140) Also in 2010, Affleck and Damon's production company, Pearl Street Films, signed a [first-look producing deal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_look_deal "First look deal") at Warner Bros.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-141)

Affleck soon began work on his next directorial project, _[Argo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argo\_(2012\_film) "Argo (2012 film)")_ (2012), for Warner Bros. Written by [Chris Terrio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Terrio "Chris Terrio") and starring Affleck as a CIA operative, the film tells the story of the CIA plan to save six U.S. diplomats during the 1979 [Iran hostage crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_hostage_crisis "Iran hostage crisis") by faking a production for a large-scale science fiction film. Anthony Lane of _The New Yorker_ said the film offered "further proof that we were wrong about Ben Affleck".[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-142) Peter Travers of _Rolling Stone_ remarked: "Affleck takes the next step in what looks like a major directing career ... He directs the hell out of it, nailing the quickening pace, the wayward humor, the nerve-frying suspense."[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-143) A major critical and commercial success,[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-144)_Argo_ won the [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"), [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Drama"), and [BAFTA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Film "BAFTA Award for Best Film") for Best Picture.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-argo-145) The cast won the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Cast_in_a_Motion_Picture "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture"). Affleck himself won the [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Directors Guild of America Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America_Award_for_Outstanding_Directing_%E2%80%93_Feature_Film "Directors Guild of America Award for Outstanding Directing – Feature Film"), and [BAFTA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Direction "BAFTA Award for Best Direction") for Best Director, becoming the first director to win these awards without a nomination for the [Academy Award for Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director").[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-146)

The following year, Affleck played a romantic lead in [Terrence Malick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrence_Malick "Terrence Malick")'s experimental drama _[To the Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To\_the\_Wonder "To the Wonder")_. Malick, a close friend of Affleck's godfather, first met Affleck in the 1990s to offer advice about the plot of _Good Will Hunting_.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-147) Peter Bradshaw of _The Guardian_ enjoyed "a performance of dignity and sensitivity,"[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-148) while _The New Yorker_'s Richard Brody described Affleck as "a solid and muscular performer" who "conveys a sense of thoughtful and willful individuality".[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-149) Affleck's performance as a poker boss was considered a highlight of the poorly reviewed thriller _[Runner Runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runner\_Runner\_(film) "Runner Runner (film)")_ (2013).[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-150)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-151) Betsy Sharkey of the _Los Angeles Times_ remarked that it was "one killer of a character, and Affleck plays him like a [Bach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Sebastian_Bach "Johann Sebastian Bach") concerto– every note perfectly played."[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-152)

He then pushed back production on his own directorial project to star as a husband accused of murder in [David Fincher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Fincher "David Fincher")'s psychological thriller _[Gone Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone\_Girl\_(film) "Gone Girl (film)")_ (2014).[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-153) Fincher cast him partly because he understood what it felt like to be misrepresented by tabloid media: "What many people don't know is that he's crazy smart, but since he doesn't want that to get awkward, he downplays it. I think he learned how to skate on charm."[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-154) David Edelstein of _New York Magazine_ noted that Fincher's controlled style of directing had a "remarkable" effect on Affleck's acting: "I never thought I'd write these words, but he carries the movie. He's terrific."[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-155) Justin Chang of _Variety_ found Affleck "perfectly cast": "It's a tricky turn, requiring a measure of careful underplaying and emotional aloofness, and he nails it completely."[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-156) In 2015, Affleck and Damon's _Project Greenlight_ was resurrected by HBO for one season.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-157)

### 2016–2019: Batman and continued directing

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/Ben_Affleck_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg/250px-Ben_Affleck_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ben_Affleck_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg)

Affleck at the 2016 [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con")

Given Affleck's growing reputation as a filmmaker, his decision to star as [Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Wayne_(DC_Extended_Universe) "Bruce Wayne (DC Extended Universe)") in the 2016 superhero film _[Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman\_v\_Superman:\_Dawn\_of\_Justice "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice")_ was regarded by Dave Itzkoff of _The New York Times_ as "a somewhat bewildering choice".[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-158) Affleck reprised his role as Batman later that year, making a brief cameo appearance in _[Suicide Squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide\_Squad\_(2016\_film) "Suicide Squad (2016 film)")_ (2016).[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-159) He starred as an [autistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autism "Autism") accountant in the action thriller _[The Accountant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Accountant\_(2016\_film) "The Accountant (2016 film)")_ (2016), which was an unexpected commercial success.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-accountanthit-160) Peter Debruge of _Variety_ felt Affleck's "boy-next-door" demeanor– "so normal and non-actorly that most of his performances feel like watching one of your buddies up on screen"– was "a terrific fit" for the role.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-161) Stephen Holden of _The New York Times_ wondered why Affleck, "looking appropriately dead-eyed and miserable," committed himself to the film.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-162)

_[Live by Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_by\_Night\_(film) "Live by Night (film)")_, which Affleck wrote, directed, co-produced, and starred in, was released in late 2016.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-163) Adapted from [Dennis Lehane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Lehane "Dennis Lehane")'s [novel of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_by_Night "Live by Night"), the [Prohibition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States "Prohibition in the United States")-era gangster drama received largely unenthusiastic reviews and failed to recoup its $65 million production budget.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-164) David Sims of _The Atlantic_ described it as "a fascinating mess of a movie" and criticized Affleck's "stiff, uncomfortable" performance. He noted that one of the last action scenes "is so wonderfully staged, its action crisp and easy to follow, that it reminds you what skill Affleck has with the camera".[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-165) In October 2016, Affleck and Damon made a one-off stage appearance for a live reading of the _Good Will Hunting_ screenplay at New York's [Skirball Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skirball_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts "Skirball Center for the Performing Arts").[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-166) The superhero film _[Justice League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice\_League\_(film) "Justice League (film)")_, in which Affleck returned as Batman, was released in 2017.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-DCEU2017-167) He later described it as a "difficult" on-set experience.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-168)[Zack Snyder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zack_Snyder "Zack Snyder") stepped down during filming due to the death of his daughter,[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-169) the replacement director [Joss Whedon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Whedon "Joss Whedon")'s treatment of actors was the subject of complaints,[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-170) and Affleck himself was struggling with addiction issues.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-171) The film drew mixed opinions from critics; Todd McCarthy of _The Hollywood Reporter_ wrote that Affleck "looks like he'd rather be almost anywhere else but here."[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-172)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-173)

Amidst an alcoholism relapse, Affleck did not work in 2017.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-tf-174) He stepped down as director, writer and, ultimately, as the star of _[The Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Batman\_(film) "The Batman (film)")_,[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-175) saying he "couldn't crack it"[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-176) and no longer felt "passionate" about the story.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-177)[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-barnesnyt-178) Filming of the drug-trafficking thriller _[Triple Frontier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple\_Frontier\_(film) "Triple Frontier (film)")_ was postponed by six months in order to accommodate his treatment for "health issues".[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-179)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-tf-174) Upon _Triple Frontier_'s release in 2019, Rodrigo Perez of _The Playlist_ remarked that director [J.C. Chandor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J.C._Chandor "J.C. Chandor") "gets a lot of mileage out of the Sad Affleck narrative and perhaps both director and actor lean into the idea."[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-180) Later in 2019, Affleck made a cameo appearance in _[Jay and Silent Bob Reboot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay\_and\_Silent\_Bob\_Reboot "Jay and Silent Bob Reboot")_, having had little contact with Kevin Smith since the making of _Clerks II_ in 2006.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-181)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-182) Affleck played a supporting role as a diplomat in [Dee Rees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dee_Rees "Dee Rees")'s political thriller _[The Last Thing He Wanted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Thing\_He\_Wanted\_(film) "The Last Thing He Wanted (film)")_ (2020). The [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") movie, filmed in mid-2018, received negative reviews from critics,[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-183)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-184) with Tomris Laffly of _Variety_ describing Affleck's performance as "oddly removed".[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-185)

Affleck's starring role as a recovering alcoholic in the sports drama _[The Way Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Way\_Back\_(2020\_film) "The Way Back (2020 film)")_ (2020) was widely praised.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-186) The themes of the movie were "close to home" for Affleck.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-news.com.au-187) He relapsed during pre-production in 2018[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-news.com.au-187) and the movie was shot in the days after he left rehab; Affleck agreed to put his salary in escrow and was accompanied to set by a sober coach.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-188) Richard Lawson of _Vanity Fair_ said it was hard to avoid the movie's "meta angle": "Affleck handles his self-conscious task with a generous humility—giving a performance built not out of histrionics or big actor moments, but instead from the messy details of a man in a plateaued distress".[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-189) David Sims of _The Atlantic_ praised the "subtlety", "vulnerability" and "lumbering physicality" of his performance, describing it as "the rawest and most natural" work of his career.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-190) Due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), cinemas closed in the second week of the movie's release and Warner Bros. made it available to view-on-demand earlier than scheduled.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-191) He received a Best Actor nomination at the [2021 Critics' Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/26th_Critics'_Choice_Awards "26th Critics' Choice Awards").[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-192) Also in 2021, Snyder's [director's cut of _Justice League_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zack_Snyder's_Justice_League "Zack Snyder's Justice League") featured a newly filmed scene with Affleck.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-193)

### 2020–present: Supporting roles and Artists Equity

Affleck had supporting roles in two 2021 releases.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-194) He played [Peter II, Count of Alençon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_II,_Count_of_Alen%C3%A7on "Peter II, Count of Alençon"), a hedonistic aristocrat in [Ridley Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridley_Scott "Ridley Scott")'s medieval drama _[The Last Duel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Duel\_(2021\_film) "The Last Duel (2021 film)")_; he also co-wrote the movie's screenplay with Damon and [Nicole Holofcener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Holofcener "Nicole Holofcener").[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-195)[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-196) Bilge Ebiri of _New York Magazine_ was impressed by Affleck's "imperious" performance as the "wonderfully skeezy Pierre, a marvelously out-there creation who shouldn't work at all and yet becomes an engine of uneasy delights."[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-197) Brian Truitt of _USA Today_ said he "steals the movie": "He seems to have written the most entertaining character in the movie for himself, but we'll allow it."[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-198) Later that year, Affleck appeared as a substitute father figure in [George Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clooney "George Clooney")'s coming-of-age drama _[The Tender Bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tender\_Bar\_(film) "The Tender Bar (film)")_.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-199) The film premiered at the London Film Festival, with Clooney remarking that he cast Affleck because he is "very intelligent, and he can also come off as the big goomba."[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-200) Pete Hammond of _Deadline_ described it as "a part he was born to play", writing that he "beautifully and knowingly" delivered "an unforgettable portrait of the uncle you wish you had."[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-201) Kevin Maher of _The Times_ said he played the role with "extraordinary subtly and depth": "He dominates his every scene, with deftly delivered quips, comedy reaction shots or sheer hang-dog charisma alone."[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-202) For the role, Affleck was nominated for the [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture "Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture") and [Screen Actors Guild Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Male_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Supporting Role") for Best Supporting Actor.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-203)[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-204)

In 2022, Affleck and [Ana de Armas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ana_de_Armas "Ana de Armas") starred in [Adrian Lyne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrian_Lyne "Adrian Lyne")'s thriller _[Deep Water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep\_Water\_(2022\_film) "Deep Water (2022 film)")_, an adaptation of [Patricia Highsmith's novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_Water_(Highsmith_novel) "Deep Water (Highsmith novel)").[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-205) It was released on streaming service Hulu and received largely negative reviews.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-206) Justin Chang of the _Los Angeles Times_ said Affleck "excels at playing the emasculated dreamboat, the golden boy gone to seed."[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-207) Adam Nayman of _The Ringer_ said the film "serves as an example of his formidable skill set within a very specific range": "What used to seem like the callow cockiness of a handsome front-runner has hardened—and deepened—into a kind of grizzled charisma, the gravitas of a frat boy facing down his own expiration date."[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-208) He also made a cameo appearance in Smith's _[Clerks III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clerks\_III "Clerks III")_.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-209)[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-210)

Affleck's fifth directorial project, _[Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air\_(2023\_American\_film) "Air (2023 American film)")_, about [Nike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nike,_Inc. "Nike, Inc.")'s creation of the [Air Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Jordan "Air Jordan"), premiered in 2023 and was well-reviewed.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-211) The movie starred [Matt Damon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Damon "Matt Damon") and [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), with Affleck playing a supporting role as [Phil Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Knight "Phil Knight").[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-212)[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-213)[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-214) It marked the first release from Affleck and Damon's independent production company [Artists Equity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artists_Equity "Artists Equity"), which aims to share profits with all stakeholders. Affleck serves as the company's CEO and intends to work exclusively for Artists Equity as a filmmaker.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-215)[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-216) In a review of _Air_ for _The Ringer_, Adam Nayman wrote that Affleck, while not a "masterful" filmmaker, "has a gift for pacing and working with actors ... He and Damon spend most of the time pumping each other up, and the chemistry between them is undeniable." David Sims of _The Atlantic_ said _Air_ was "a great return to Affleck's original impulses as a director: It's a fun, well-made film for grown-ups that gives its actors room to flesh out their characters."[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-217) Also in 2023, Affleck starred as a detective in [Robert Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Rodriguez "Robert Rodriguez")'s action thriller _[Hypnotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypnotic\_(2023\_film) "Hypnotic (2023 film)")_[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-218) and made his final appearance as Batman in the film _[The Flash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Flash\_(film) "The Flash (film)")_, appearing in a cameo.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-219)

In 2025, Affleck starred in the action thriller _[The Accountant 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Accountant\_2 "The Accountant 2")_. In January 2026, he alongside Damon starred in the crime thriller _[The Rip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rip\_(film) "The Rip (film)")_.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-220) He currently has another film in post-production; Ben directed and starred opposite [Gillian Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gillian_Anderson "Gillian Anderson") in the kidnapping thriller _[Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animals\_(2026\_film) "Animals (2026 film)")_, and is scheduled to release on Netflix on an unknown date.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-221)

In March 2026, [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix,_Inc. "Netflix, Inc.") acquired Affleck's AI-focused post-production startup, InterPositive, for an estimated $600 million, at which time he joined the company as a senior advisor to oversee the technology's integration.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-222)[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-223)

## Philanthropy

### Eastern Congo Initiative

Main article: [Eastern Congo Initiative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Congo_Initiative "Eastern Congo Initiative")

[![Image 12: Ben Affleck, holding a pen and sitting behind a microphone, looks ahead while offering testimony](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Ben_Affleck_testifying_to_Congress_on_the_Democratic_Republic_of_Congo..jpg/250px-Ben_Affleck_testifying_to_Congress_on_the_Democratic_Republic_of_Congo..jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ben_Affleck_testifying_to_Congress_on_the_Democratic_Republic_of_Congo..jpg)

Affleck in 2011, testifying before the [House Subcommittee on Africa, Global Health and Human Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Foreign_Affairs_Subcommittee_on_Africa,_Global_Health,_Global_Human_Rights_and_International_Organizations "United States House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Africa, Global Health, Global Human Rights and International Organizations")

After traveling in the region between 2007 and early 2010, Affleck and [Whitney Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitney_Williams "Whitney Williams") co-founded the nonprofit organization [Eastern Congo Initiative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Congo_Initiative "Eastern Congo Initiative") in 2010.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-224)[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-225) ECI acts as a grant maker for [Congolese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo")-led, community-based charities.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-amanpour.blogs.cnn.com-226) It offers training and resources to cooperatives of Congolese farmers while leveraging partnerships with companies including [Theo Chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theo_Chocolate "Theo Chocolate") and [Starbucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starbucks "Starbucks").[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-227)[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-228) ECI also aims to raise public awareness and drive policy change in the United States.[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-229)

Affleck has written op-eds about issues facing eastern Congo for the _Washington Post_,[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-230)[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-231)_Politico_,[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-232) the _Huffington Post_,[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-233)_Time_,[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-234)_The New York Times_[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-235) and the _Los Angeles Times_.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-236) He has appeared as a discussion panelist at many events, including at the [Center for Strategic and International Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Strategic_and_International_Studies "Center for Strategic and International Studies"),[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Affleck#cite_note-237) the [Global Philanthropy Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Philanthropy_Forum "Global Philanthropy
