William Bradley Pitt (born December 18, 1963) is an American actor and film producer. In a film career spanning more than thirty-five years, Pitt has received numerous accolades, including two Academy Awards, two British Academy Film Awards, two Golden Globe Awards, two Primetime Emmy Awards, and one Volpi Cup. His films as a leading actor have grossed over $7.5 billion worldwide.[2][3]

Pitt first gained recognition as a cowboy hitchhiker in the Ridley Scott road film Thelma & Louise (1991). Pitt emerged as a star taking on leading roles in films such as the drama A River Runs Through It (1992), the western Legends of the Fall (1994), the horror film Interview with the Vampire (1994), the crime thriller Seven (1995), the cult film Fight Club (1999), and the crime comedy Snatch (2000). He cemented his leading man status by starring in blockbusters, such as the Ocean's film trilogy (2001–2007), Troy (2004) and Mr. & Mrs. Smith (2005).[4] His other major successes include Inglourious Basterds (2009), World War Z (2013), Bullet Train (2022) and F1 (2025).

Pitt earned Academy Award nominations for his performances in the science fiction drama 12 Monkeys (1995), the fantasy romance The Curious Case of Benjamin Button (2008) and the sports drama Moneyball (2011). For his portrayal of a stuntman in Quentin Tarantino's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood (2019), he won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor. He also starred in acclaimed films such as Babel (2006), The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford (2007), Burn After Reading (2008), The Tree of Life (2011), Fury (2014), The Big Short (2015), Ad Astra (2019) and Babylon (2022).

In 2001, Pitt co-founded the production company Plan B Entertainment.[5] As a producer, he won the Academy Award for Best Picture for 12 Years a Slave (2013) and was nominated for Moneyball (2011) and The Big Short (2015). An influential figure in popular culture, Pitt appeared on Forbes' annual Celebrity 100 list from 2006 to 2008, and the Time 100 list in 2007. Regarded as a sex symbol, Pitt was named People's Sexiest Man Alive in 1995 and 2000. Pitt's relationships have been subject to widespread media attention, particularly his marriages to actresses Jennifer Aniston and Angelina Jolie.

Early life

William Bradley Pitt was born on December 18, 1963, in Shawnee, Oklahoma,[6] to William Alvin Pitt, the proprietor of a trucking company, and Jane Etta (née Hillhouse; 1940–2025),[7] a school counselor.[8] The family soon moved to Springfield, Missouri, where Pitt lived with his younger siblings, Doug Pitt (born 1966) and Julie Neal (née Pitt; born 1969).[9] Born into a conservative Christian household,[10][11] he was raised as Southern Baptist and later "oscillate[d] between agnosticism and atheism".[12] He later returned to a belief "that we're all connected".[13][14]

Pitt attended Kickapoo High School, where he was a member of the golf, swimming, and tennis teams.[15] He participated in the school's Key and Forensics clubs, in school debates, and in musicals.[16] Pitt enrolled at the University of Missouri in 1982, majoring in journalism with a focus on advertising.[17] As graduation approached, Pitt did not feel ready to settle down. He loved films, and since films were not made in Missouri, he decided to go to where they were made.[18][19] Two weeks before completing the coursework for a degree, Pitt left the university and moved to Los Angeles, where he took acting lessons and worked odd jobs.[18] He has named Gary Oldman, Sean Penn, and Mickey Rourke as his early acting heroes.[20]

Career
Early work (1987–1993)

While struggling to establish himself in Los Angeles, Pitt took lessons from acting coach Roy London.[16][21] His acting career began in 1987, with uncredited roles in the films No Way Out, No Man's Land and Less than Zero.[16][22] In May of the same year, he made his television debut in a two-episode role on the NBC soap opera Another World.[23] That November, he had guest appearances on the CBS sitcom Trial and Error[24][25] and the ABC sitcom Growing Pains.[26] He appeared in four episodes of the CBS primetime series Dallas between December 1987 and February 1988 as Randy, the boyfriend of Charlotte (played by Shalane McCall).[27] Later in 1988, Pitt made a guest appearance on the Fox police drama 21 Jump Street[28] and appeared in a Pringles commercial directed by Lawrence Bridges.[29] The same year, he had his first leading film role in the Yugoslavian–American co-production The Dark Side of the Sun, as a young American taken by his family to the Adriatic to find a remedy for a skin condition. The film was shelved at the outbreak of the Croatian War of Independence, and was not released until 1997.[16] Pitt made two film appearances in 1989: the first in a supporting role in the comedy Happy Together, and the second in a major role in the horror film Cutting Class, which was the first of Pitt's films to reach theaters.[26] That year, he made guest appearances on the television series Head of the Class, Freddy's Nightmares, Thirtysomething, and Growing Pains.[30]

Pitt appeared as Billy Canton, a drug addict who takes advantage of a young runaway (played by Juliette Lewis) in the 1990 NBC television film Too Young to Die?, the story of an abused teenager sentenced to death for a murder. Ken Tucker of Entertainment Weekly described Pitt as a "magnificent slimeball" in his role as the "hoody" and "really scary" boyfriend of Lewis' character.[31] The same year, Pitt co-starred in six episodes of the short-lived Fox drama Glory Days and had a supporting role in the HBO television film The Image.[32] His next appearance came in the 1991 film Across the Tracks, in which he portrays Joe Maloney, a high school runner.[33] The same year he featured in a Levi's jeans commercial.[34]

Pitt attracted wider recognition in his supporting role in Ridley Scott's 1991 film Thelma & Louise.[32] He plays J.D., a small-time criminal who befriends Thelma (Geena Davis). His love scene with Davis has been cited as the event that defined Pitt as a sex symbol.[26][35] Pitt subsequently starred in Johnny Suede (1991) a low-budget film about an aspiring rock star,[36] and the live-action/animated fantasy film Cool World (1992),[26] both of which fared poorly at the box office and with critics.[37][38]

Pitt appeared as Paul Maclean in the 1992 biographical film A River Runs Through It, directed by Robert Redford.[39] Although Pitt thought his portrayal of Maclean was one of his weakest performances,[9] the Los Angeles Times described it as a career-making performance. Jeff Giles of Rotten Tomatoes said Pitt's portrayal proved he could be more than a "cowboy-hatted hunk."[40][41] In 1993, Pitt reunited with Juliette Lewis for the road film Kalifornia, playing the serial killer husband of her character.[42] His performance was described by Peter Travers of Rolling Stone as "outstanding, all boyish charm and then a snort that exudes pure menace."[42] Pitt also garnered attention for a brief appearance in the cult hit True Romance as a stoner named Floyd.[43] He finished the year by winning a ShoWest Award for Male Star of Tomorrow.[44]

Breakthrough (1994–1998)
Pitt with Losang Thonden in Argentina on the set of Seven Years in Tibet in 1997

In 1994, Pitt portrayed the vampire Louis de Pointe du Lac in the horror film Interview with the Vampire: The Vampire Chronicles, based on Anne Rice's 1976 novel Interview with the Vampire.[45] Pitt was part of an ensemble cast that included Tom Cruise, Kirsten Dunst, Christian Slater, and Antonio Banderas.[45] Despite winning two MTV Movie Awards at the 1995 ceremony,[46] his performance was poorly received by critics.[citation needed] Matt Zoller Seitz of the Dallas Observer felt Pitt was dull in the role because he failed to display the self-awareness and inner torment necessary for the character.[47]

Pitt next starred in Legends of the Fall (1994), based on the novel Legends of the Fall by Jim Harrison and set in the American West during the first four decades of the twentieth century.[48] He portrays Tristan Ludlow, son of Colonel William Ludlow (Anthony Hopkins).[49] For his performance, Pitt received his first Golden Globe Award nomination, in the Best Actor category.[50] Janet Maslin of The New York Times wrote, "Pitt's diffident mix of acting and attitude works to such heartthrob perfection it's a shame the film's superficiality gets in his way."[51] Although the film received mixed reviews,[52] the Deseret News predicted that Legends of the Fall would solidify Pitt's reputation as a lead actor.[53]

In 1995, Pitt starred alongside Morgan Freeman, Gwyneth Paltrow, and Kevin Spacey in the crime thriller Seven, playing a detective on the trail of a serial killer who preys on people he considers guilty of the Seven Deadly Sins.[54] Pitt said the role would expand his acting horizons,[55] expressing an intention to move on from playing the "pretty boy" to playing someone with flaws."[56] Variety wrote that Pitt did a "determined, energetic, creditable job" in his role, and that his performance "was screen acting at its best".[57] Following the box-office success of Seven, Pitt played the psychotic anarchist Jeffrey Goines in Terry Gilliam's 1995 science fiction film 12 Monkeys.[37] The film received predominantly positive reviews, with Pitt praised in particular. Janet Maslin of The New York Times called Twelve Monkeys "fierce and disturbing" and remarked on Pitt's "startlingly frenzied performance", concluding that he "electrifies Jeffrey with a weird magnetism that becomes important later in the film."[58] He won a Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor for the film[50] and received his first Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor.[59]

The following year, he appeared in the legal drama Sleepers (1996), based on Lorenzo Carcaterra's novel of the same name.[60] The film received mixed reviews.[61] In the 1997 film The Devil's Own Pitt starred, opposite Harrison Ford, as Irish Republican Army terrorist Rory Devany,[62] a role for which he was required to learn an Irish accent.[63] Critical opinion was divided on his accent; "Pitt finds the right tone of moral ambiguity, but at times his Irish brogue is too convincing – it's hard to understand what he's saying", wrote the San Francisco Chronicle.[64] The Charleston Gazette opined that it had favored Pitt's accent over the movie.[65] The Devil's Own grossed $140 million worldwide.[37]

Later that year, he led as Austrian mountaineer Heinrich Harrer in the Jean-Jacques Annaud film Seven Years in Tibet.[66] Pitt trained for months for the role, which demanded significant mountain climbing and trekking practice, including rock climbing in California and the European Alps with his co-star David Thewlis.[67] Pitt had the lead role in 1998's fantasy romance film Meet Joe Black. He portrayed a personification of death inhabiting the body of a young man to learn what it is like to be human.[68] The film received mixed reviews, and many were critical of Pitt's performance. According to Mick LaSalle of the San Francisco Chronicle, Pitt was unable to "make an audience believe that he knows all the mysteries of death and eternity."[69] Roger Ebert remarked, "Pitt is a fine actor, but this performance is a miscalculation."[70]

Rise to prominence (1999–2003)

In 1999, Pitt portrayed Tyler Durden in Fight Club,[71][8] a film adaptation of Chuck Palahniuk's novel of the same name, directed by David Fincher.[72] Pitt prepared for the part with lessons in boxing, taekwondo, and grappling.[73] To look the part, Pitt consented to the removal of pieces of his front teeth which were restored when filming ended.[74] While promoting Fight Club, Pitt said that the film explored not taking one's aggressions out on someone else but to "have an experience, take a punch more and see how you come out on the other end."[75] Fight Club premiered at the 1999 Venice International Film Festival.[76] Despite divided critical opinion on the film as a whole,[77][78] Pitt's performance was widely praised. Paul Clinton of CNN noted the risky yet successful nature of the film,[79] while Variety remarked upon Pitt's ability to be "cool, charismatic and more dynamically physical, perhaps than [...] his breakthrough role in Thelma and Louise".[80] In spite of a worse-than-expected box office performance, Fight Club became a cult classic after its DVD release in 2000.[81]

Pitt in 2001

Pitt was cast as an Irish Traveller boxer with a barely intelligible accent in Guy Ritchie's 2000 gangster film Snatch.[82] Several reviewers were critical of Snatch; however, most praised Pitt.[83] Mick LaSalle of the San Francisco Chronicle said Pitt was "ideally cast as an Irishman whose accent is so thick even Brits can't understand him", going on to say that, before Snatch, Pitt had been "shackled by roles that called for brooding introspection, but recently he has found his calling in black comic outrageousness and flashy extroversion;"[84] while Amy Taubin of The Village Voice claimed that "Pitt gets maximum comic mileage out of a one-joke role".[85]

The following year Pitt starred opposite Julia Roberts in the romantic comedy The Mexican,[86] a film that garnered a range of reviews[87] but enjoyed box office success.[37] Pitt's next role, in 2001's $143 million-grossing Cold War thriller Spy Game,[37] was as Tom Bishop, an operative of the CIA's Special Activities Division, mentored by Robert Redford's character.[88] Mark Holcomb of Salon.com enjoyed the film, although he noted that neither Pitt nor Redford provided "much of an emotional connection for the audience".[89]

On November 22, 2001, Pitt made a guest appearance in the eighth season of the television series Friends, playing a man with a grudge against Rachel Green, played by Jennifer Aniston (to whom Pitt was married at the time).[90] For this performance, he was nominated for an Emmy Award.[91] In December 2001, Pitt played Rusty Ryan in the heist film Ocean's Eleven, a remake of the 1960 Rat Pack original. He joined an ensemble cast including George Clooney, Matt Damon, Andy García, and Julia Roberts.[92] Well received by critics, Ocean's Eleven was highly successful at the box office, earning $450 million worldwide.[37]

Pitt appeared in two episodes of MTV's reality series Jackass in February 2002, first running through the streets of Los Angeles with several cast members in gorilla suits,[93] and in a subsequent episode participating in his own staged abduction.[94] In the same year, Pitt had a cameo role in George Clooney's directorial debut Confessions of a Dangerous Mind.[95] He took on his first voice-acting roles in 2003, speaking as the titular character of the DreamWorks animated film Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas[96] and playing Boomhauer's brother, Patch, in an episode of the animated television series King of the Hill.[97]

Worldwide recognition (2004–2008)

Pitt had two major film roles in 2004, starring as Achilles in Troy, and reprising his role, Rusty Ryan, in the sequel Ocean's Twelve. He spent six months sword training before the filming of Troy, based on the Iliad.[98] An on-set injury to his Achilles tendon delayed production on the picture for several weeks.[99] Stephen Hunter of The Washington Post stated that Pitt excelled at such a demanding role.[100] Troy was the first film produced by Plan B Entertainment, a film production company he had founded two years earlier with Jennifer Aniston and Brad Grey, CEO of Paramount Pictures.[101] Ocean's Twelve earned $362 million worldwide,[37] and Pitt and Clooney's dynamic was described by CNN's Paul Clinton as "the best male chemistry since Paul Newman and Robert Redford."[102] In 2005, Pitt starred as John Smith in the Doug Liman-directed action comedy Mr. & Mrs. Smith, in which a bored married couple discover that each is an assassin for a competing agency. The feature received reasonable reviews but was generally lauded for the chemistry between Pitt and Angelina Jolie, who played his character's wife Jane Smith. The Star Tribune noted that "while the story feels haphazard, the movie gets by on gregarious charm, galloping energy and the stars' thermonuclear screen chemistry".[103] Mr. & Mrs. Smith earned $478 million worldwide, making it one of the biggest hits of 2005.[104]

Pitt at the premiere of Burn After Reading in 2008

For his next film, Pitt starred opposite Cate Blanchett in Alejandro González Iñárritu's multi-narrative drama Babel (2006).[105] Pitt's performance was critically well-received, and the Seattle Post-Intelligencer said that he was credible and gave the film visibility.[106] Pitt later said he regarded taking the part as one of the best decisions of his career.[107] The film was screened at a special presentation at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival[108] and was later featured at the 2006 Toronto International Film Festival.[109] Babel received seven Academy Award and Golden Globe nominations, winning the Golden Globe, and earned Pitt a Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture nomination.[50] That same year, Pitt's company Plan B Entertainment produced The Departed, which won the Academy Award for Best Picture. Pitt was credited on-screen as a producer; however, only Graham King was ruled eligible for the Oscar win.[110]

Reprising his role as Rusty Ryan in a third picture, Pitt starred in 2007's Ocean's Thirteen.[111] While less lucrative than the first two films, this sequel earned $311 million at the international box office.[37] Pitt's next film role was as American outlaw Jesse James in the 2007 Western drama The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford, adapted from Ron Hansen's 1983 novel of the same name.[112] Directed by Andrew Dominik and produced by Pitt's company Plan B Entertainment, the film premiered at the 2007 Venice Film Festival,[113] with Pitt playing a "scary and charismatic" role, according to Lewis Beale of Film Journal International,[114] and earning Pitt the Volpi Cup award for Best Actor at the 64th Venice International Film Festival.[115] He eventually collected the award one year later at the 2008 festival.[116] As of January 2019, it was his own favorite of his films.[117]

Pitt's next appearance was in the 2008 black comedy Burn After Reading, his first collaboration with the Coen brothers. The film received a positive reception from critics, with The Guardian calling it "a tightly wound, slickly plotted spy comedy",[118] noting that Pitt's performance was one of the funniest.[118] He was later cast as Benjamin Button, the lead in David Fincher's 2008 film The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, a loosely adapted version of a 1921 short story by F. Scott Fitzgerald. The story follows a man who is born an octogenarian and ages in reverse,[119] with Pitt's "sensitive" performance making Benjamin Button a "timeless masterpiece", according to Michael Sragow of The Baltimore Sun.[120] The performance earned Pitt his first Screen Actors Guild Award nomination,[121] as well as a fourth Golden Globe and second Academy Award nomination.[50] The film received 13 Academy Award nominations and grossed $329 million at the box office worldwide.[37]

Artistic resurgence and production success (2009–2018)
Pitt at the 2012 Cannes Film Festival

Pitt's next leading role came in 2009 with the Quentin Tarantino-directed war film Inglourious Basterds, which premiered at the 2009 Cannes Film Festival.[122] Pitt played Lieutenant Aldo Raine, "The Apache", an American resistance fighter battling Nazis in German-occupied France.[123] The film was a box office hit, taking $311 million worldwide,[37] and garnered generally favorable reviews.[124] The film received multiple awards and nominations, including eight Academy Award nominations and seven MTV Movie Award nominations, including Best Male Performance for Pitt.[125][126] He next voiced the superhero Metro Man in the 2010 animated feature Megamind.[127] Pitt produced and appeared in Terrence Malick's experimental drama The Tree of Life, co-starring Sean Penn, which won the Palme d'Or at the 2011 Cannes Film Festival.[128] In a performance that attracted strong praise, he portrayed Oakland Athletics general manager Billy Beane in the drama Moneyball, which is based on the 2003 book of the same name written by Michael Lewis.[129] Moneyball received six Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture and Best Actor for Pitt.[130]

His next role was as mob hitman Jackie Cogan in Andrew Dominik's Killing Them Softly (2012), based on the novel Cogan's Trade by George V. Higgins.[131] In 2013, Pitt starred in World War Z, a thriller about a zombie apocalypse, based on Max Brooks's novel of the same name. Pitt also produced the film.[132] World War Z grossed $540 million at the box office worldwide,[37] becoming Pitt's then highest grossing picture, until it was overtaken by F1 in 2025.[133] Next in 2013, he produced, and played a small role in, 12 Years a Slave, a historical drama based on the autobiography of Solomon Northup.[134] The film received critical acclaim[135] and was nominated for nine Academy Awards and won three, including Best Picture.[136] Also in 2013, Pitt had a supporting role in Ridley Scott's The Counselor.[137] Plan B Entertainment landed its first television series on the 2013–2014 schedule, as their joint venture with ABC Studios, the sci-fi/fantasy drama Resurrection, was picked up by ABC.[138]

Pitt at the Japan premiere of War Machine in 2017

Pitt starred in Fury, a World War II film directed and written by David Ayer, and co-starring Shia LaBeouf, Logan Lerman, Jon Bernthal, Michael Peña, and Jason Isaacs.[139][140][141] The film was released on October 17, 2014.[139] By the end of its run, Fury proved to be a commercial and critical success; it grossed $211 million worldwide[37] and received highly positive reviews from critics.[142]

In 2015, Pitt starred opposite his wife, Jolie, in her third directorial effort, By the Sea, a romantic drama about a marriage in crisis, based on her screenplay. The film was their first collaboration since 2005's Mr. & Mrs. Smith. Pitt's next role came with the biographical comedy-drama The Big Short, which he also produced and also co-starred alongside Christian Bale, Steve Carell, and Ryan Gosling. The film was a commercial and critical success. It went on to gross over $102 million worldwide[143] and received positive reviews from critics.[144][145] The film was nominated for five Academy Awards, including Best Picture, earning Pitt his third Academy Award nomination as producer. In 2016, Pitt starred in Robert Zemeckis's romantic thriller Allied, in which he plays an assassin who falls in love with a French spy (played by Marion Cotillard) during a mission to kill a German official in World War II.[146][147] In 2017, he starred in the Netflix satirical war comedy War Machine,[148] which he also produced.[149] Pitt played a recurring role as a weatherman on the late-night talk show The Jim Jefferies Show throughout 2017.[150]

A 2017 sequel to World War Z was announced in 2016,[151] then briefly delayed, then its director confirmed to be David Fincher, and finally shelved because of budget problems.[152][153]

Established legacy (2019–present)

Pitt starred as veteran stunt double Cliff Booth opposite Leonardo DiCaprio, in Quentin Tarantino's 2019 film Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, reuniting with DiCaprio after The Departed, which Pitt produced and DiCaprio starred in.[154] For his performance in the film, he won the Academy Award, Golden Globe Award, BAFTA, Screen Actors Guild Award, and Critics' Choice Award.[155][156] This is the second Oscar for Pitt, his first that he received for acting.[156] In 2019, he also starred in James Gray's deep space epic Ad Astra, in which he played Roy McBride, a space engineer searching the galaxy for his father.[157] Pitt's performance was praised as one of his career-best turn,[158][159] delivering a performance "that weaponizes passivity into a lethal form of self-defense".[160] In 2020, Pitt portrayed Dr. Anthony Fauci in the cold open on Saturday Night Live, earning him a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series nomination.[161][162]

In 2021, Pitt entered the recording business by creating a company with French record producer Damien Quintard. Set in Pitt's Chateau Miraval in South of France, Miraval Studios re-opened in 2022 after two decades of inactivity. The previous version of the studio was one of the most iconic studios in the world, producing the records for Pink Floyd, the Cranberries, AC/DC, Sade and Muse, among others.[163] In 2022, Pitt starred in Bullet Train, directed by David Leitch,[164] and reunited with his Once Upon a Time in Hollywood co-star Margot Robbie in Babylon, directed by Damien Chazelle.[165] He reteamed with George Clooney in Wolfs, a comedy-thriller written and directed by Jon Watts, which was released in September 2024.[166] In 2025, Pitt produced and starred in the Formula One racing film F1, directed by Joseph Kosinski,[167] for which he earned $30 million.[168] F1 quickly became Apple's biggest hit at the box office,[169] and Pitt's highest-grossing film.[170]

Acting credits and accolades
See also: Brad Pitt filmography and List of awards and nominations received by Brad Pitt

Over his career, Pitt has received numerous awards including two Academy Awards (as a producer and actor), two BAFTA Awards, two Golden Globe Awards, two Primetime Emmy Awards, and two Screen Actors Guild Awards.

Pitt has been recognized by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences for the following performances:

68th Academy Awards (1995): Best Supporting Actor, nomination, 12 Monkeys
81st Academy Awards (2008): Best Actor, nomination, The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
84th Academy Awards (2011): Best Actor, nomination, Moneyball
92nd Academy Awards (2019): Best Supporting Actor, win, Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
Philanthropy and activism

Pitt visited the University of Missouri campus in October 2004 to encourage students to vote in the 2004 U.S. presidential election,[171] in which he supported John Kerry.[171][172] Later in October, he publicly supported the principle of public funding for embryonic stem-cell research. "We have to make sure that we open up these avenues so that our best and our brightest can go find these cures that they believe they will find", he said.[173] In support of this he endorsed Proposition 71, a California ballot initiative intended to provide state government funding for stem-cell research.[174]

Pitt at the "Global Summit to End Sexual Violence in Conflict" in 2014

Pitt supports One Campaign, an organization aimed at combating AIDS and poverty in the developing world.[175][176] He narrated the 2005 PBS public television series Rx for Survival: A Global Health Challenge, which discusses current global health issues.[177] The following year Pitt and Jolie flew to Haiti, where they visited a school supported by Yéle Haïti, a charity founded by Haitian-born hip hop musician Wyclef Jean.[178] In May 2007, Pitt and Jolie donated $1 million to three organizations in Chad and Sudan dedicated to those affected by the crisis in the Darfur region.[179] Along with Clooney, Damon, Don Cheadle, David Pressman, and Jerry Weintraub, Pitt is one of the founders of Not On Our Watch, an organization that focuses global attention on stopping "mass atrocities".[180]

Pitt has a sustained interest in architecture,[181] even taking time away from film to study computer-aided design at the Los Angeles offices of renowned architect Frank Gehry.[182] He narrated e2 design, a PBS television series focused on worldwide efforts to build environmentally friendly structures through sustainable architecture and design.[183] In 2000, he co-authored an architectural book on the Blacker House with the architects Thomas A. Heinz and Randell Makinson.[184] In 2006, he founded the Make It Right Foundation, organizing housing professionals in New Orleans to finance and construct 150 sustainable, affordable new houses in New Orleans's Ninth Ward following the devastation caused by Hurricane Katrina.[185][186]

The project involves 13 architectural firms and the environmental organization Global Green USA, with several of the firms donating their services.[187][188] Pitt and philanthropist Steve Bing have each committed $5 million in donations.[189] The first six homes were completed in October 2008,[190] and in September 2009 Pitt received an award in recognition of the project from the U.S. Green Building Council, a non-profit trade organization that promotes sustainability in how buildings are designed, built and operated.[191][192] Pitt met with U.S. President Barack Obama and Speaker of the House of Representatives Nancy Pelosi in March 2009 to promote his concept of green housing as a national model and to discuss federal funding possibilities.[193]

In September 2006, Pitt and Jolie established a charitable organization, the Jolie-Pitt Foundation, to aid humanitarian causes around the world.[194] The foundation made initial donations of $1 million each to Global Action for Children and Doctors Without Borders,[195] followed by an October 2006 donation of $100,000 to the Daniel Pearl Foundation, an organization created in memory of the late American journalist Daniel Pearl.[196] According to federal filings, Pitt and Jolie invested $8.5 million into the foundation in 2006; it gave away $2.4 million in 2006[197] and $3.4 million in 2007.[198] In June 2009, the Jolie-Pitt Foundation donated $1 million to a U.N. refugee agency to help Pakistanis displaced by fighting between troops and Taliban militants.[199] In January 2010, the foundation donated $1 million to Doctors Without Borders for emergency medical assistance to help victims of the Haiti earthquake.[200][201]

Pitt is a supporter of same-sex marriage.[202] In an October 2006 interview with Esquire, Pitt said that he would marry Jolie when everyone in America is legally able to marry.[203] In September 2008, he donated $100,000 to the campaign against California's 2008 ballot proposition Proposition 8, an initiative to overturn the state Supreme Court decision that had legalized same-sex marriage.[204] In March 2012, Pitt was featured in a performance of Dustin Lance Black's play, 8 – a staged reenactment of the federal trial that overturned California's Prop 8 ban on same-sex marriage – as Judge Vaughn Walker.[205] In September 2012, Pitt reaffirmed his support for Obama, saying, "I am an Obama supporter and I'm backing his U.S. election campaign."[206] In October 2020, he narrated an advertisement for Joe Biden's 2020 presidential campaign.[207]

Personal life
Relationships and marriages
Pitt with his then-partner Angelina Jolie at the 2007 Cannes Film Festival

From the late 1980s to early 1990s, Pitt was romantically involved with several of his co-stars, including Shalane McCall (Dallas),[208] Robin Givens (Head of the Class),[209] Jill Schoelen (Cutting Class),[209] Geena Davis (Thelma & Louise),[210] and Juliette Lewis (Too Young to Die? and Kalifornia).[40] McCall and Lewis were 15 and 17, respectively, when Pitt started dating them.[211][212] Subsequently, Pitt had a much-publicized romance with, and engagement to, his Seven co-star, Gwyneth Paltrow, whom he dated from 1994 to 1997.[209]

Pitt met actress Jennifer Aniston in 1998; they married in a private wedding ceremony in Malibu on July 29, 2000.[213] In January 2005, Pitt and Aniston announced they had decided to separate. Two months later, Aniston filed for divorce, citing irreconcilable differences.[214] Pitt and Aniston's divorce was finalized by the Los Angeles Superior Court on October 2, 2005.[214] Despite media reports that Pitt and Aniston had an acrimonious relationship, Pitt said in a February 2009 interview that he and Aniston "check in with each other", adding that they were both big parts of each other's lives.[215]

During Pitt's divorce proceedings, his involvement with his Mr. & Mrs. Smith co-star Angelina Jolie attracted media attention. Jolie and Pitt stated that they fell in love on the set[216][217] and that there was no infidelity.[216] In April 2005, one month after Aniston filed for divorce, a set of paparazzi photographs emerged showing Pitt, Jolie, and her son Maddox at a beach in Kenya; the press interpreted the pictures as evidence of a relationship between Pitt and Jolie. Throughout 2005, the two were seen together with increasing frequency, and the entertainment media dubbed the couple "Brangelina".[218] During the ensuing media circus, shirts with the text "Team Jolie" and "Team Aniston" became a fashion trend.[219][220] On January 11, 2006, Jolie confirmed to People that she was pregnant with Pitt's child, thereby publicly acknowledging their relationship for the first time.[221] Pitt and Jolie announced their engagement in April 2012 after seven years together.[222] They were legally married on August 14, 2014, and had their wedding in a private ceremony at the Château Miraval, France, on August 23, 2014.[223] On September 19, 2016, Jolie filed for divorce from Pitt, citing irreconcilable differences.[224] On April 12, 2019, the divorce became legal.[225][1] After Pitt sued Jolie for selling her share of a winery they owned to a third party, she filed a countersuit, in which she alleged that he physically and verbally abused her and their children in an outburst while on a plane in September 2016.[226]

In 2022, he began dating Ines de Ramon (b. 1992), a jewelry executive and the ex-wife of actor Paul Wesley.[227]

Children

In July 2005, Pitt accompanied Jolie to Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, where she adopted her second child, a girl named Zahara.[228][229] On December 3, 2005, Pitt was in the process of becoming the adoptive father of Jolie's daughter, and Jolie's first adopted child, a boy named Maddox.[230] On January 19, 2006, a California judge granted Jolie's request to change the children's surnames from "Jolie" to "Jolie-Pitt".[231] The adoptions were finalized soon after.[232]

Jolie gave birth to their daughter Shiloh in Swakopmund, Namibia, on May 27, 2006. Pitt confirmed that she would qualify for a Namibian passport.[233] The couple sold the first pictures of their daughter through the distributor Getty Images; the North American rights were purchased by People for over $4.1 million, while Hello! obtained the British rights for approximately $3.5 million. The proceeds from the sale were donated to charities serving African children.[234] Madame Tussauds in New York unveiled a wax figure of the two-month-old; it marked the first time an infant had been honoured with a statue in the museum.[235]

On March 15, 2007, Jolie adopted a 3-year-old boy, Pax, from an orphanage in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.[236] Pitt adopted the boy in the United States on February 21, 2008.[237] At the Cannes Film Festival in May 2008, Jolie confirmed that she was expecting twins.[238] She gave birth to son and daughter, Knox and Vivienne, on July 12, 2008, in Nice, France.[239] The rights for the first images of the twins were jointly sold to People and Hello! for $14 million—the most expensive celebrity pictures ever taken.[240][241] The couple donated the proceeds to the Jolie-Pitt Foundation.[240][242]

Since Jolie filed for divorce from Pitt on September 19, 2016, they have been embroiled in a custody battle over their children. Jolie had full custody until May 2021 when Pitt was granted joint custody, over four and a half years after proceedings began.[243] However, in July, Los Angeles superior court judge John W. Ouderkirk was removed from the case due to concerns over his impartiality as he did not sufficiently disclose business relationships with Pitt's lawyers. This resulted in the custody arrangement reverting to a previous November 2018 agreement where Jolie has primary physical custody while Pitt has "custodial time" with their minor children.[244][245]

In 2024, Pitt's then 18-year-old second-eldest daughter with Jolie changed her name legally from Shiloh Nouvel Jolie-Pitt to Shiloh Nouvel Jolie.[246] In 2026, Maddox Chivan Jolie, Zahara Marley Jolie and Vivienne Marcheline Jolie filed paperwork to legally drop Pitt from their last names.[247][248][249]

Religion

Pitt was raised in a conservative Christian household in Springfield, Missouri, and brought up in the Southern Baptist tradition. He attended church regularly during his childhood but later became critical of organized religion and its doctrines.[250]

He distanced himself from institutional religion in adulthood, and described his beliefs as evolving. He identified at various times as agnostic and atheist, once stating that he was "probably 20 percent atheist and 80 percent agnostic," reflecting skepticism toward traditional religious claims.[251][252] He stated in later interviews that his earlier atheism was not a fixed position and that his views had continued to change over time. He described his spirituality as personal and experiential rather than tied to any organized religious system.[253]

He has shown interest in spiritual and philosophical traditions associated with Buddhism. His role in the film Seven Years in Tibet (1997) contributed to public discussion of Tibetan Buddhism in Western popular culture, with commentary noting the film's emphasis on Buddhist themes and imagery.[254] He appeared on the cover of an October 1997 issue of Time magazine in a religion-themed issue that referenced Buddhism in connection with his work and public image.[255] He visited a Tokyo Buddhist temple in 2022, and participated in a prayer ritual during the promotion of his film Bullet Train.[256]

Abuse allegation

In September 2016, the FBI and the Los Angeles Department of Children and Family Services investigated Pitt for child abuse following an incident on a plane, where Pitt was accused by an anonymous person of being "verbally abusive" and "physical" towards one of his children.[257] Pitt was not criminally charged for the incident by the Los Angeles County Department of Children and Family Services, or by the FBI.[258]

In 2022, Jolie filed a countersuit against Pitt during a legal battle over their formerly co-owned vineyard. Jolie's lawyers stated that during negotiations, Pitt had asked Jolie to sign "a nondisclosure agreement prohibiting her from speaking outside of court about his abuse of her and their children."[226] Her complaint stated that he grabbed and shook her during the plane ride, strangled one of their children, and struck another in the face, among other allegations.[226]

Alcohol and drug use

In September 2016, Pitt got sober and began attending Alcoholics Anonymous meetings.[259] In December 2019, he wrote an article for Interview in which he talked with his Legends of the Fall and Meet Joe Black costar and fellow recovering alcoholic Anthony Hopkins about their experiences with addiction and recovery.[260] Pitt credits fellow actor Bradley Cooper with helping him in his sobriety.[261] In an interview with Esquire in August 2026, Pitt said that he had been sober for seven years before beginning to drink again "in a more restrained manner."[262]

Pitt has admitted to using cannabis in the late 1990s as a way to deal with his increasing fame.[263][264] According to Pitt: "I was hiding out from the celebrity thing; I was smoking way too much dope; I was sitting on the couch and just turning into a doughnut."[263][264][265] He reduced his cannabis use and focused on his work after a trip to Morocco, where he witnessed extreme poverty and suffering.[263][264]

Face blindness

In 2022, Pitt said that he had struggled for years to recognize people's faces due to prosopagnosia (face blindness),[266] for which he has not been formally diagnosed.[266][267] In a 2013 interview, he said that his inability to recognize people's faces had become so severe that he often wanted to stay home.[268]

Artwork

Pitt has an interest in art, learned pottery,[269] and has created sculptures. Nine of his sculptures were exhibited together with works by musician Nick Cave and artist Thomas Houseago at the Sara Hildén Art Museum in Tampere, Finland, in 2022 and 2023.[270][271]

Business ventures

In 2022, Pitt co-founded the skincare products company Beau Domaine.[272]

Public image
Pitt at the 2007 Palm Springs International Film Festival

Pitt has been frequently cited as one of the most attractive actors of all time and has been described as a sex symbol by many sources, including Empire, who named him one of the 25 sexiest stars in film history in 1995.[16][273][274] The same year, he was named People's Sexiest Man Alive, an accolade he received again in 2000.[273][275] Pitt appeared on Forbes' annual Celebrity 100 list of the 100 most powerful celebrities from 2006 to 2008 placing at numbers 20, 5 and 10, respectively.[276][277][278] In 2007, he appeared on the Time 100 list, a compilation of the 100 most influential people in the world, as selected annually by Time magazine.[279] The magazine credited Pitt for using "his star power to get people to look at places and stories that cameras don't usually catch".[279] He was again included on the Time 100 in 2009, this time in the "Builders and Titans" list.[280] As of 2025, Pitt's films have grossed over $7.5 billion worldwide, according to The Numbers.[281]

Beginning in 2005, Pitt's relationship with Angelina Jolie became one of the world's most reported celebrity stories. After Jolie was confirmed to be pregnant in early 2006, the intense media hype surrounding the couple reached what Reuters, in a story titled "The Brangelina fever," called "the point of insanity".[282] To avoid media attention, the couple flew to Namibia for the birth of their daughter, which was described by a paparazzi blog as "the most anticipated baby since Jesus Christ."[283] Similarly, intense media interest greeted the announcement of Jolie's second pregnancy two years later; for the two weeks Jolie spent in a seaside hospital in Nice, reporters and photographers camped outside on the promenade to report on the birth.[284]

In a 2006 global industry survey by ACNielsen in 42 international markets, Pitt, together with Jolie, were found to be the favorite celebrity endorsers for brands and products worldwide.[285] Pitt has appeared in several television commercials. For the U.S. market, he starred in a Heineken commercial aired during the 2005 Super Bowl; it was directed by David Fincher, who had directed Pitt in Seven and Fight Club.[286] Other commercial appearances came in television spots including Acura Integra, in which he was featured opposite Russian model Tatiana Sorokko,[287] as well as SoftBank, and Edwin Jeans.[288] On June 2, 2015, the minor planet 29132 Bradpitt was named in his honor.[289]

Pitt does not use social media and has no accounts on any social media platform.[290][291]

## Brief Life History of Jane Etta

When Jane Etta Hillhouse was born on 13 August 1940, in Memphis, Shelby, Tennessee, United States, her father, Hal Knox Hillhouse, was 29 and her mother, Clara Maurine Bell, was 30. She married William Alvin Pitt on 11 August 1962, in Joplin, Jasper, Missouri, United States. She lived in United States in 1949 and Joplin, Jasper, Missouri, United States in 1950. She died on 5 August 2025, in Springfield, Greene, Missouri, United States, at the age of 84, and was buried in Springfield, Greene, Missouri, United States.

## Name Meaning

Hillhouse 

Jane 

Etta 

English: topographic name from Middle English or early modern English _hill_ + _house_ ‘house on the hill’. In Yorkshire the surname may arise from the name of a farm in Fartown, Pudsey (Yorkshire).

More

Scottish (Ayrshire and Lanarkshire) and English: habitational name from any of several minor places in Ayrshire and elsewhere in Scotland, probably named with Middle English, Older Scots _hill_ + _house_ ‘house on the hill’.

More

History: Rev. James Hillhouse, the first minister of Montville, CT, came to North America from County Londonderry, Ireland, _c._ 1720. His grandson James Hillhouse was a Federalist congressman from CT and treasurer of Yale College from 1782 to 1832.

## Name Meaning

Hillhouse 

Jane 

Etta 

English: topographic name from Middle English or early modern English _hill_ + _house_ ‘house on the hill’. In Yorkshire the surname may arise from the name of a farm in Fartown, Pudsey (Yorkshire).

More

Scottish (Ayrshire and Lanarkshire) and English: habitational name from any of several minor places in Ayrshire and elsewhere in Scotland, probably named with Middle English, Older Scots _hill_ + _house_ ‘house on the hill’.

More

History: Rev. James Hillhouse, the first minister of Montville, CT, came to North America from County Londonderry, Ireland, _c._ 1720. His grandson James Hillhouse was a Federalist congressman from CT and treasurer of Yale College from 1782 to 1832.

## Biography

**Jane Etta (Hillhouse) Pitt** was born about 1940 in Joplin, Jasper, Missouri, United States, daughter of [Hal Knox Hillhouse](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99 "Hillhouse-99") (1911–1976) and [Clara Maurine (Bell) Hillhouse](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Bell-9355 "Bell-9355") (1910–2003).

Jane (21) married **[William Alvin Pitt](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Pitt-677 "Pitt-677")** (20) (born on 24 March 1941 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, Oklahoma; son of [Alvin Monroe Pitt](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Pitt-678 "Pitt-678") and [Betty Jeanne (Brown) Russell](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Brown-179857 "Brown-179857")) in 1962.

Jane passed away about 5 August 2025, aged about 85. She was buried in database and images ([https://www.findagrave.com/memorial](https://www.findagrave.com/memorial "https://www.findagrave.com/memorial").[[1]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-98#_note-Death_1)

## Biography

**Jane Etta (Hillhouse) Pitt** was born about 1940 in Joplin, Jasper, Missouri, United States, daughter of [Hal Knox Hillhouse](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99 "Hillhouse-99") (1911–1976) and [Clara Maurine (Bell) Hillhouse](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Bell-9355 "Bell-9355") (1910–2003).

Jane (21) married **[William Alvin Pitt](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Pitt-677 "Pitt-677")** (20) (born on 24 March 1941 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, Oklahoma; son of [Alvin Monroe Pitt](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Pitt-678 "Pitt-678") and [Betty Jeanne (Brown) Russell](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Brown-179857 "Brown-179857")) in 1962.

Jane passed away about 5 August 2025, aged about 85. She was buried in database and images ([https://www.findagrave.com/memorial](https://www.findagrave.com/memorial "https://www.findagrave.com/memorial").[[1]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-98#_note-Death_1)

He was born on 13 Mar 1911 in Mount Vernon, Lawrence County, Missouri, USA [[1]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-obit) and his parents were Etta Colman (Williams) and Emery A. Hillhouse (1882-1965).

Hal Knox Hillhouse married on 15?25 Feb 1935 in Madeira, California, USA to Clara Maurine Bell (1910-2003).

Following a long illness, he died on 15 Nov 1976 [[2]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-0)[[3]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-1) at Freeman Hospital in Joplin, Newton County, Missouri, USA [[1]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-obit) and was buried at Zion Cemetery in Mount Vernon, Lawrence County, Missouri, USA. [[4]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-2)

Hal was the maternal grandfather of actor Brad Pitt. [[5]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-3)

## Biography

He was born on 13 Mar 1911 in Mount Vernon, Lawrence County, Missouri, USA [[1]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-obit) and his parents were Etta Colman (Williams) and Emery A. Hillhouse (1882-1965).

Hal Knox Hillhouse married on 15?25 Feb 1935 in Madeira, California, USA to Clara Maurine Bell (1910-2003).

Following a long illness, he died on 15 Nov 1976 [[2]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-0)[[3]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-1) at Freeman Hospital in Joplin, Newton County, Missouri, USA [[1]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-obit) and was buried at Zion Cemetery in Mount Vernon, Lawrence County, Missouri, USA. [[4]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-2)

Hal was the maternal grandfather of actor Brad Pitt. [[5]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Hillhouse-99#_note-3)

## Biography

**William Bradley Pitt is an American actor and film producer.**

Brad Pitt was born 18 December 1963 in Shawnee, Oklahoma, to William Alvin Pitt and Jane Etta Hillhouse. William ran a trucking business at the time and the family soon moved to Springfield, Missouri, a place Brad has described as "Mark Twain country" and "Jesse Jame country". In high school, Brad was active in various groups and clubs including Keys and Forensics, the school debate team and the golf, swimming and tennis teams. He also performed in musicals. In 1982 he enrolled in the University of Missouri to study journalism and advertising. As graduation loomed, Brad decided he wasn't ready to settle down. He loved films and since films were not made in Missouri he decided to go where they were made and two weeks before earning his degree, Brad packed it up and headed off to Los Angeles where he worked odd jobs and took acting classes.

Brad landed many roles and had some good success but a major turning point for him came in 1994 when he starred as _Louis de Pointe du Lac_ in _Interview with a Vampire_. His performance in this role was not well received by critics. Later that year he also starred in _Legends of the Fall_ and received mixed reviews. In 1995, Pitt starred in _Seven_ where his performance was finally well received, even called screen acting at its best.

Brad has gone on to receive a Golden Globe Award, a Screen Actors Guild Award, five Academy Award nominations and one Academy Award win for a production by his film company Plan B Entertainment.

Brad has had a few high profile relationships including a five year marriage to [Jennifer Aniston](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Aniston-2 "Aniston-2"). He married Angeline Jolie in 2014, and the couple have six children, some naturally and some through adoption. Brad and Angelina were both very involved in social issues in the United States as well as internationally. They divorced in 2019.

## Biography

**William Bradley Pitt is an American actor and film producer.**

Brad Pitt was born 18 December 1963 in Shawnee, Oklahoma, to William Alvin Pitt and Jane Etta Hillhouse. William ran a trucking business at the time and the family soon moved to Springfield, Missouri, a place Brad has described as "Mark Twain country" and "Jesse Jame country". In high school, Brad was active in various groups and clubs including Keys and Forensics, the school debate team and the golf, swimming and tennis teams. He also performed in musicals. In 1982 he enrolled in the University of Missouri to study journalism and advertising. As graduation loomed, Brad decided he wasn't ready to settle down. He loved films and since films were not made in Missouri he decided to go where they were made and two weeks before earning his degree, Brad packed it up and headed off to Los Angeles where he worked odd jobs and took acting classes.

Brad landed many roles and had some good success but a major turning point for him came in 1994 when he starred as _Louis de Pointe du Lac_ in _Interview with a Vampire_. His performance in this role was not well received by critics. Later that year he also starred in _Legends of the Fall_ and received mixed reviews. In 1995, Pitt starred in _Seven_ where his performance was finally well received, even called screen acting at its best.

Brad has gone on to receive a Golden Globe Award, a Screen Actors Guild Award, five Academy Award nominations and one Academy Award win for a production by his film company Plan B Entertainment.

Brad has had a few high profile relationships including a five year marriage to [Jennifer Aniston](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Aniston-2 "Aniston-2"). He married Angeline Jolie in 2014, and the couple have six children, some naturally and some through adoption. Brad and Angelina were both very involved in social issues in the United States as well as internationally. They divorced in 2019.

# Top-20 directors 1960-1970

[Created by 9-1](https://www.imdb.com/user/p.iq7wb4exqmbw3g4farfd5h7axu/?ref_=ls_usr_ov)Updated 15y ago

12,858 visits

List order

*   
![Image 2: Ingmar Bergman](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTc4MjQwMzY0N15BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwNTI1NTM1MQ@@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000005/?ref_=ls_i_1)  

 #### [1. Ingmar Bergman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000005/?ref_=ls_t_1) 

    *   Writer
    *   Director
    *   Actor

[Wild Strawberries (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050986/?ref_=ls_knf_1)

Ernst Ingmar Bergman was born July 14, 1918, the son of a priest. The film and T.V. series, [The Best Intentions (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0104350/?ls) is biographical and shows the early marriage of his parents. The film [Sunday's Children (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0105511/?ls) depicts a bicycle journey with his father. In the miniseries [Private Confessions (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115164/?ls) is the trilogy closed. Here, as in 'Den Goda Viljan' [Pernilla August](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000278/?ls) play his mother. Note that all three movies are not always full true biographical stories. He began his career early with a puppet theatre which he, his sister and their friends played with. But he was the manager. Strictly professional he begun writing in 1941. He had written a play called 'Kaspers död' (A.K.A. 'Kaspers Death') which was produced the same year. It became his entrance into the movie business as Stina Bergman (not a close relative), from the company S.F. (Swedish Filmindustry), had seen the play and thought that there must be some dramatic talent in young Ingmar. His first job was to save other more famous writers' poor scripts. Under one of that script-saving works he remembered that he had written a novel about his last year as a student. He took the novel, did the save-poor-script job first, then wrote a screenplay on his own novel. When he went back to S.F., he delivered two scripts rather than one. The script was [Torment (1944)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0036914/?ls) and was the fist Bergman screenplay that was put into film (by [Alf Sjöberg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0803549/?ls)). It was also in that movie Bergman did his first professional film-director job. Because Alf Sjöberg was busy, Bergman got the order to shoot the last sequence of the film. Ingmar Bergman is the father of [Daniel Bergman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0074757/?ls), director, and [Mats Bergman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0074835/?ls), actor at the Swedish Royal Dramatic Theater. Ingmar Bergman was also C.E.O. of the same theatre between 1963-1966, where he hired almost every professional actor in Sweden. In 1976 he had a famous tax problem. Bergman had trusted other people to advise him on his finances, but it turned out to be very bad advice. Bergman had to leave the country immediately, and so he went to Germany. A few years later he returned to Sweden and made his last theatrical film [Fanny and Alexander (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0083922/?ls). In later life he retired from movie directing, but still wrote scripts for film and T.V. and directed plays at the Swedish Royal Dramatic Theatre for many years. He died peacefully in his sleep on July 30, 2007.

*   
![Image 3: Sergio Leone in Once Upon a Time in America (1984)](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTk4Njk5MzY3MV5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwMTEyMzE0NA@@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001466/?ref_=ls_i_2)  

 #### [2. Sergio Leone](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001466/?ref_=ls_t_2) 

    *   Second Unit Director or Assistant Director
    *   Writer
    *   Director

[Once Upon a Time in America (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087843/?ref_=ls_knf_2)

[Sergio Leone](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001466/?ls) was virtually born into the cinema - he was the son of [Roberto Roberti](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0730743/?ls) (A.K.A. Vincenzo Leone), one of Italy's cinema pioneers, and actress [Bice Valerian](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1295438/?ls). Leone entered films in his late teens, working as an assistant director to both Italian directors and U.S. directors working in Italy (usually making Biblical and Roman epics, much in vogue at the time). Towards the end of the 1950s he started writing screenplays, and began directing after taking over [The Last Days of Pompeii (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054422/?ls) in mid-shoot after its original director fell ill. His first solo feature, [The Colossus of Rhodes (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054756/?ls), was a routine Roman epic, but his second feature, [A Fistful of Dollars (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058461/?ls), a shameless remake of [Akira Kurosawa](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000041/?ls)'s [Yojimbo (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055630/?ls), caused a revolution. It was the first Spaghetti Western, and shot T.V. cowboy [Clint Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000142/?ls) to stardom (Leone wanted [Henry Fonda](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000020/?ls) or [Charles Bronson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000314/?ls) but couldn't afford them). The two sequels, [For a Few Dollars More (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059578/?ls) and [The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060196/?ls), were shot on much higher budgets and were even more successful, though his masterpiece, [Once Upon a Time in the West (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064116/?ls), in which Leone finally worked with Fonda and Bronson, was mutilated by Paramount Pictures and flopped at the U.S. box office. He directed [Duck, You Sucker! (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067140/?ls) reluctantly (as producer he hired [Peter Bogdanovich](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000953/?ls) to direct but he left before shooting began), and turned down offers to direct [The Godfather (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068646/?ls) in favor of his dream project, which became [Once Upon a Time in America (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087843/?ls). He died in 1989 after preparing an even more expensive Soviet co-production on the World War II siege of Leningrad.

![Image 4: Alfred Hitchcock in Psycho (1960)](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjNjZDM0NGUtZmE0Yy00MTI3LThkNTYtODVlZTUzM2M4Yjk5XkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000033/?ref_=ls_i_3)  

 #### [3. Alfred Hitchcock](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000033/?ref_=ls_t_3) 

    *   Director
    *   Producer
    *   Writer

[Psycho (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054215/?ref_=ls_knf_3)

Alfred Joseph Hitchcock was born in Leytonstone, Essex, England. He was the son of Emma Jane (Whelan; 1863 - 1942) and East End greengrocer William Hitchcock (1862 - 1914). His parents were both of half English and half Irish ancestry. He had two older siblings, William Hitchcock (born 1890) and Eileen Hitchcock (born 1892). Raised as a strict Catholic and attending Saint Ignatius College, a school run by Jesuits, Hitch had very much of a regular upbringing. His first job outside of the family business was in 1915 as an estimator for the Henley Telegraph and Cable Company. His interest in movies began at around this time, frequently visiting the cinema and reading US trade journals.  
  
Hitchcock entering the film industry in 1919 as a title card designer. It was there that he met [Alma Reville](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0720904/?ls), though they never really spoke to each other. It was only after the director for [Always Tell Your Wife (1923)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0818899/?ls) fell ill and Hitchcock was named director to complete the film that he and Reville began to collaborate. Hitchcock had his first real crack at directing a film, start to finish, in 1923 when he was hired to direct the film [Number 13 (1922)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0013444/?ls), though the production wasn't completed due to the studio's closure (he later remade it as a sound film). Hitchcock didn't give up then. He directed [The Pleasure Garden (1925)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0016230/?ls), a British/German production, which was very popular. Hitchcock made his first trademark film in 1927, [The Lodger: A Story of the London Fog (1927)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0017075/?ls) . In the same year, on the 2nd of December, Hitchcock married Alma Reville. They had one child, [Patricia Hitchcock](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0386877/?ls) who was born on July 7th, 1928. His success followed when he made a number of films in Britain such as [The Lady Vanishes (1938)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0030341/?ls) and [Jamaica Inn (1939)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0031505/?ls), some of which also gained him fame in the USA.  
  
In 1940, the Hitchcock family moved to Hollywood, where the producer [David O. Selznick](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006388/?ls) had hired him to direct an adaptation of 'Daphne du Maurier''s [Rebecca (1940)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0032976/?ls). After [Saboteur (1942)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0035279/?ls), as his fame as a director grew, film companies began to refer to his films as 'Alfred Hitchcock's', for example Alfred Hitcock's [Psycho (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054215/?ls), Alfred Hitchcock's [Family Plot (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074512/?ls), Alfred Hitchcock's [Frenzy (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068611/?ls).  
  
Hitchcock was a master of pure cinema who almost never failed to reconcile aesthetics with the demands of the box-office.  
  
During the making of [Frenzy (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068611/?ls), Hitchcock's wife Alma suffered a paralyzing stroke which made her unable to walk very well. On March 7, 1979, Hitchcock was awarded the AFI Life Achievement Award, where he said: "I beg permission to mention by name only four people who have given me the most affection, appreciation, and encouragement, and constant collaboration. The first of the four is a film editor, the second is a scriptwriter, the third is the mother of my daughter Pat, and the fourth is as fine a cook as ever performed miracles in a domestic kitchen and their names are Alma Reville." By this time, he was ill with angina and his kidneys had already started to fail. He had started to write a screenplay with [Ernest Lehman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0499626/?ls) called The Short Night but he fired Lehman and hired young writer David Freeman to rewrite the script. Due to Hitchcock's failing health the film was never made, but Freeman published the script after Hitchcock's death. In late 1979, Hitchcock was knighted, making him Sir Alfred Hitchcock. On the 29th April 1980, 9:17AM, he died peacefully in his sleep due to renal failure. His funeral was held in the Church of Good Shepherd in Beverly Hills. Father Thomas Sullivan led the service with over 600 people attended the service, among them were [Mel Brooks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000316/?ls) (director of [High Anxiety (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0076141/?ls), a comedy tribute to Hitchcock and his films), [Louis Jourdan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0431139/?ls), [Karl Malden](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001500/?ls), [Tippi Hedren](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001335/?ls), [Janet Leigh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001463/?ls) and [François Truffaut](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000076/?ls).

 #### [4. Robert Wise](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0936404/?ref_=ls_t_4) 

    *   Director
    *   Producer
    *   Editor

[West Side Story (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055614/?ref_=ls_knf_4)

Robert Earl Wise was born on September 10, 1914 in Winchester, Indiana, the youngest of three sons of Olive R. (Longenecker) and Earl Waldo Wise, a meat packer. His parents were both of Pennsylvania Dutch (German) descent. At age nineteen, the avid moviegoer came into the film business through an odd job at RKO Radio Pictures. A head sound effects editor at the studio recognized Wise's talent, and made Wise his protégé. Around 1941, [Orson Welles](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000080/?ls) was in need of an editor for [Citizen Kane (1941)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0033467/?ls), and Wise did a splendid job. Welles really liked his work and ideas. Wise started as a director with some B-movies, and his career went on quickly, and he made many classic movies. His last theatrical film, [Rooftops (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098222/?ls), proved that he was a filmmaker still in full command of his craft in his 80s. The carefully composed images, tight editing, and unflagging pace make one wish that Wise had not stayed away from the camera for very long. Robert Wise died of heart failure on September, 14, 2005, just four days after his 91st birthday.

 #### [5. Billy Wilder](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000697/?ref_=ls_t_5) 

    *   Writer
    *   Director
    *   Producer

[The Apartment (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053604/?ref_=ls_knf_5)

Originally planning to become a lawyer, Billy Wilder abandoned that career in favor of working as a reporter for a Viennese newspaper, using this experience to move to Berlin, where he worked for the city's largest tabloid. He broke into films as a screenwriter in 1929 and wrote scripts for many German films until [Adolf Hitler](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0386944/?ls) came to power in 1933. Wilder immediately realized his Jewish ancestry would cause problems, so he emigrated to Paris, then the US. Although he spoke no English when he arrived in Hollywood, Wilder was a fast learner and thanks to contacts such as [Peter Lorre](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000048/?ls) (with whom he shared an apartment), he was able to break into American films. His partnership with [Charles Brackett](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0102818/?ls) started in 1938 and the team was responsible for writing some of Hollywood's classic comedies, including [Ninotchka (1939)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0031725/?ls) and [Ball of Fire (1941)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0033373/?ls). The partnership expanded into a producer-director one in 1942, with Brackett producing and the two turned out such classics as [Five Graves to Cairo (1943)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0035884/?ls), [The Lost Weekend (1945)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0037884/?ls) (Oscars for Best Picture, Director and Screenplay) and [Sunset Boulevard (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043014/?ls) (Oscars for Best Screenplay), after which the partnership dissolved. (Wilder had already made one film, [Double Indemnity (1944)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0036775/?ls) without Brackett, as the latter had refused to work on a film he felt dealt with such disreputable characters.) Wilder's subsequent self-produced films would become more caustic and cynical, notably [Ace in the Hole (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043338/?ls), though he also produced such sublime comedies as [Some Like It Hot (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053291/?ls) and [The Apartment (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053604/?ls) (which won him Best Picture and Director Oscars). He retired in 1981.

![Image 7: Luis Buñuel](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTAxNDAyNjE4OTBeQTJeQWpwZ15BbWU3MDc2NDM3MTg@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000320/?ref_=ls_i_6)  

 #### [6. Luis Buñuel](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000320/?ref_=ls_t_6) 

    *   Writer
    *   Director
    *   Actor

[The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068361/?ref_=ls_knf_6)

The father of cinematic Surrealism and one of the most original directors in the history of the film medium, Luis Buñuel was given a strict Jesuit education (which sowed the seeds of his obsession with both religion and subversive behavior), and subsequently moved to Madrid to study at the university there, where his close friends included [Salvador Dalí](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0198557/?ls) and [Federico García Lorca](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0305030/?ls).  
  
After moving to Paris, Buñuel did a variety of film-related odd jobs in Paris, including working as an assistant to director [Jean Epstein](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0258477/?ls). With financial assistance from his mother and creative assistance from Dalí, he made his first film, the 17-minute [Un chien andalou (1929)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0020530/?ls), in 1929, and immediately catapulted himself into film history thanks to its shocking imagery (much of which - like the sliced eyeball at the beginning - still packs a punch even today). It made a deep impression on the Surrealist Group, who welcomed Buñuel into their ranks.  
  
The following year, sponsored by wealthy art patrons, he made his first feature, the scabrous witty and violent [L'Age d'Or (1930)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0021577/?ls), which mercilessly attacked the church and the middle classes, themes that would preoccupy Buñuel for the rest of his career. That career, though, seemed almost over by the mid-1930s, as he found work increasingly hard to come by and after the Spanish Civil War he emigrated to the US where he worked for the Museum of Modern Art and as a film dubber for Warner Bros.  
  
Moving to Mexico in the late 1940s, he teamed up with producer [Óscar Dancigers](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0199190/?ls) and after a couple of unmemorable efforts shot back to international attention with the lacerating study of Mexican street urchins in [The Young and the Damned (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042804/?ls), winning him the Best Director award at the Cannes Film Festival.  
  
But despite this new-found acclaim, Buñuel spent much of the next decade working on a variety of ultra-low-budget films, few of which made much impact outside Spanish-speaking countries (though many of them are well worth seeking out). But in 1961, General Franco, anxious to be seen to be supporting Spanish culture invited Buñuel back to his native country - and Bunuel promptly bit the hand that fed him by making [Viridiana (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055601/?ls), which was banned in Spain on the grounds of blasphemy, though it won the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival.  
  
This inaugurated Buñuel's last great period when, in collaboration with producer [Serge Silberman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0797889/?ls) and writer [Jean-Claude Carrière](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0140643/?ls) he made seven extraordinary late masterpieces, starting with [Diary of a Chambermaid (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058249/?ls). Although far glossier and more expensive, and often featuring major stars such as [Jeanne Moreau](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0603402/?ls) and [Catherine Deneuve](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000366/?ls), the films showed that even in old age Buñuel had lost none of his youthful vigour.  
  
After saying that every one of his films from [Belle de Jour (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061395/?ls) onwards would be his last, he finally kept his promise with [That Obscure Object of Desire (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0075824/?ls), after which he wrote a memorable (if factually dubious) autobiography, in which he said he'd be happy to burn all the prints of all his films 
    *   a classic Surrealist gesture if ever there was one.

 #### [7. François Truffaut](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000076/?ref_=ls_t_7) 

    *   Writer
    *   Director
    *   Producer

[Day for Night (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0070460/?ref_=ls_knf_7)

French director François Truffaut began to assiduously go to the movies at age seven. He was also a great reader but not a good pupil. He left school at 14 and started working. In 1947, aged 15, he founded a film club and met [André Bazin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0063336/?ls), a French critic, who became his protector. Bazin helped the delinquent Truffaut and also when he was put in jail because he deserted the army. In 1953 Truffaut published his first movie critiques in "Les Cahiers du Cinema." In this magazine Truffaut, and some of his friends as passionate as he was, became defenders of what they call the "author policy". In 1954, as a test, Truffaut directed his first short film. Two years afterwords he assisted [Roberto Rossellini](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0744023/?ls) with some later abandoned projects.  
  
The year 1957 was an important one for him: he married [Madeleine Morgenstern](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1280512/?ls), the daughter of an important film distributor, and founded his own production company, Les Films du Carrosse; named after [Jean Renoir](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0719756/?ls)'s [The Golden Coach (1952)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044487/?ls). He also directed [Les mistons (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050714/?ls), considered the real first step of his cinematographic work. His other big year was 1959: the huge success of his first full-length film, [The 400 Blows (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053198/?ls), was the beginning of the New Wave, a new way of making movies in France. This was also the year his first daughter, [Laura Truffaut](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0874150/?ls), was born.  
  
From 1959 until his death, François Truffaut's life and films are mixed up. Let's only note he had two other daughters [Eva Truffaut](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0874147/?ls) (b. 1961) and Josephine (b. 1982, with French actress [Fanny Ardant](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000272/?ls)). Truffaut was the most popular and successful French film director ever. His main themes were passion, women, childhood and faithfulness.
