# This is Hawkins.

## About Us

*   Culture Culture Culture
*   History History History
*   Safety Safety Safety
*   Leadership Leadership Leadership
*   Awards Awards Awards
*   Community Community Community

## GETTING THE JOB DONE

## — NO MATTER WHAT.

Since 1960, Hawkins has reliably delivered construction projects by holding true to our core values and high standards.

![Image 3](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2F2026-03%2Ficon-17.png&w=2048&q=75)

### Thorough Planning

We think through the smallest details to eliminate surprises before construction begins.

![Image 5](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2F2026-03%2Ficon-3.png&w=2048&q=75)

### Honest Communication

Direct, honest communication builds confidence and lasting relationships.

![Image 7](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2F2026-03%2Ficon-21.png&w=2048&q=75)

### Financial Stewardship

We look out for our clients' best financial interests and eliminate unnecessary waste.

![Image 9](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2F2026-03%2Ficon-16.png&w=2048&q=75)

### Personal Accountability

We measure performance, own our results, and pursue continuous improvement.

![Image 11](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2F2026-03%2Ficon-10.png&w=2048&q=75)

### One Team

Everyone at Hawkins works toward a common goal: project success.

![Image 13](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2F2026-03%2Ficon-23_0.png&w=2048&q=75)

### Disciplined Execution

We make progress every day through disciplined planning and decisive action.

![Image 15](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2F2026-03%2Ficon-20.png&w=2048&q=75)

### Proven Quality

We stand behind our work and deliver results that meet the highest standards.

![Image 17](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2F2026-03%2Ficon-11.png&w=2048&q=75)

### Lasting Legacy

We manage for long-term strength, building a company that lasts for generations.

![Image 19: construction workers on the job](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F16x9_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Fweb_careers_noego_2000x1125_ashlandwt_251102_2451_0.jpg%3Fh%3D854a7be2%26itok%3DIXXiQBjx&w=3840&q=75)

Trust You Can Measure.

## Safety Is the Standard

Safety is not a talking point here. It is how we operate every day. From planning through execution, Hawkins teams anticipate risk, protect one another, and deliver work the right way.

[Our Safety Approach](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/about/safety)

![Image 21: Man with construction truck](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F16x9_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Fweb_about_history_2000x1125_i-80interstate_251005_2027.jpg%3Fh%3D854a7be2%26itok%3DSJoxvR4W&w=3840&q=75)

All in the Family.

## Company History

Hawkins has never grown by accident. Each generation expanded the company through structured preparation, stronger technical capability, and the discipline to preserve the values that built it.

Today, Hawkins remains privately held and fourth-generation led. We answer to our name, not shareholders. That independence allows us to reinvest in our people, equipment, and safety while protecting the long-term stability that defines us.

## Hawkins Over Time.

![Image 23: UNL Archives Early stadium construction 1923](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F1x1_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Funiversity-of-nebraska-archives-stands-early-during-construction-in-1923_0.jpg%3Fh%3D854a7be2%26itok%3DKVRDFOSL&w=3840&q=75)

The Early Years

## 1885–1959

Hawkins’ story began with Parsons Construction in 1885. Earl and Kenneth Hawkins joined the company in the early 1900s and became co-owners by 1933, laying the foundation for Hawkins Construction. The company contributed to projects including Boys Town, a World War II ordnance plant, and Omaha’s Memorial Park while continuing to grow with a new headquarters in 1952.

![Image 25: Memorial Park Dedication with President Truman](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F1x1_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Fowh-archives-memorial-park-dedication-with-truman-2_0.jpg%3Fh%3D854a7be2%26itok%3DmCgXDwJq&w=3840&q=75)

New Generation

## 1960–1979

Hawkins Construction Company was incorporated in 1960. Under Fred Hawkins, the company expanded through major infrastructure projects, including the Missouri River wastewater treatment plant and OPPD North Omaha Power Station. Throughout the 1970s, Hawkins contributed to major civic, commercial, and defense projects across Omaha.

![Image 27: Hawkins headquarters 1961](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F1x1_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Fhawkins-headquarters-1961-2004-bw_0_0.jpg%3Fh%3D854a7be2%26itok%3D-_toZ6BI&w=3840&q=75)

Growing Hawkins

## 1980-1994

The third generation took the helm in 1980 with leadership shared by Kim and Fred Jr. In 1983, Hawkins made major investments to build expertise in heavy-highway construction. As Hawkins grew, Kim and Fred adopted new operational practices to improve safety and efficiency.

![Image 29: Offutt Airborne Command Post ](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F1x1_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Foffutt-airborne-command-post-facility_0.jpg%3Fh%3D854a7be2%26itok%3D14aZUHN3&w=3840&q=75)

Growing Hawkins

## 1995–2006

Major projects built included I-80 expansion from Omaha to Lincoln, the Durham Research Towers at UNMC, the West Dodge Expressway, Eppley Airport airfield paving programs, and First National’s technology park. Continued growth led to a new headquarters in 2002.

![Image 31: Hawkins construction logo and truck](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F1x1_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Fshop-hawk-side-dump.JPG%3Fh%3D790be497%26itok%3Dv0wYJvjF&w=3840&q=75)

Expansion

## 2006–2020

Hawkins grew its regional impact with major infrastructure projects like the Council Bluffs Interstate program, Offutt Runway replacement and Lincoln South Beltway. Hawkins greatly expanded Water/Wastewater expertise, becoming the primary plant constructor for Omaha’s CSO program and regional critical projects.

![Image 33: i-80 work ](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F1x1_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Fweb_safety_emr_current_2000x1125_i-80interstate_251005_1447_0.jpg%3Fh%3D854a7be2%26itok%3Dq_Q7rkPe&w=3840&q=75)

Modern Hawkins

## 2021–Now

Fourth generation Chris Hawkins assumed top leadership in 2021. The Company continues to grow in a multi-state region while expanding lines of business in material supply and infrastructure management.

![Image 23: UNL Archives Early stadium construction 1923](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F1x1_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Funiversity-of-nebraska-archives-stands-early-during-construction-in-1923_0.jpg%3Fh%3D854a7be2%26itok%3DKVRDFOSL&w=3840&q=75)

The Early Years

## 1885–1959

Hawkins’ story began with Parsons Construction in 1885. Earl and Kenneth Hawkins joined the company in the early 1900s and became co-owners by 1933, laying the foundation for Hawkins Construction. The company contributed to projects including Boys Town, a World War II ordnance plant, and Omaha’s Memorial Park while continuing to grow with a new headquarters in 1952.

![Image 25: Memorial Park Dedication with President Truman](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F1x1_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Fowh-archives-memorial-park-dedication-with-truman-2_0.jpg%3Fh%3D854a7be2%26itok%3DmCgXDwJq&w=3840&q=75)

New Generation

## 1960–1979

Hawkins Construction Company was incorporated in 1960. Under Fred Hawkins, the company expanded through major infrastructure projects, including the Missouri River wastewater treatment plant and OPPD North Omaha Power Station. Throughout the 1970s, Hawkins contributed to major civic, commercial, and defense projects across Omaha.

![Image 27: Hawkins headquarters 1961](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F1x1_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Fhawkins-headquarters-1961-2004-bw_0_0.jpg%3Fh%3D854a7be2%26itok%3D-_toZ6BI&w=3840&q=75)

Growing Hawkins

## 1980-1994

The third generation took the helm in 1980 with leadership shared by Kim and Fred Jr. In 1983, Hawkins made major investments to build expertise in heavy-highway construction. As Hawkins grew, Kim and Fred adopted new operational practices to improve safety and efficiency.

![Image 29: Offutt Airborne Command Post ](https://www.hawkinsconstruction.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdrupal.hawkinsconstruction.com%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2Fstyles%2F1x1_large%2Fpublic%2F_images%2Fgeneral%2Foffutt-airborne-command-post-facility_0.jpg%3Fh%3D854a7be2%26itok%3D14aZUHN3&w=3840&q=75)

Growing Hawkins

## 1995–2006

Major projects built included I-80 expansion from Omaha to Lincoln, the Durham Research Towers at UNMC, the West Dodge Expressway, Eppley Airport airfield paving programs, and First National’s technology park. Continued growth led to a new headquarters in 2002.

Brad Pitt is an American actor and film producer. His acting career began at age 23 in 1987 with roles in the hit Fox television series _[21 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_Jump\_Street "21 Jump Street")_. He subsequently appeared in episodes for television shows during the late 1980s and played his first major role in _[The Dark Side of the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_Side\_of\_the\_Sun\_(film) "The Dark Side of the Sun (film)")_ (1988) the slasher film _[Cutting Class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutting\_Class "Cutting Class")_ (1989).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-1) He gained recognition in _[Thelma & Louise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thelma\_&\_Louise "Thelma & Louise")_ (1991), _[A River Runs Through It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_River\_Runs\_Through\_It\_(film) "A River Runs Through It (film)")_ (1992), _[Cool World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cool\_World "Cool World")_ (1992) and _[Kalifornia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalifornia "Kalifornia")_ (1993).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-Thelma-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-3)

He later took on the role of [vampire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vampire "Vampire")[Louis de Pointe du Lac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_de_Pointe_du_Lac "Louis de Pointe du Lac") in the horror drama _[Interview with the Vampire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interview\_with\_the\_Vampire\_(film) "Interview with the Vampire (film)")_ (1994) and for his performance in the epic drama _[Legends of the Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legends\_of\_the\_Fall "Legends of the Fall")_ (1994), he earned his first [Golden Globe Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Drama") nomination.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-Achath2011-4)

Pitt starred in the [David Fincher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Fincher "David Fincher")-directed, commercially successful thriller _[Seven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven\_(1995\_film) "Seven (1995 film)")_ (1995), in which he played a detective on the trail of a [serial killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serial_killer "Serial killer") who murders people he believes are guilty of the [seven deadly sins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_deadly_sins "Seven deadly sins").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-WinterHughes2007-5) His performance as a psychotic mental patient in the science fiction film _[12 Monkeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12\_Monkeys "12 Monkeys")_ won him the [Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture "Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture") and an Academy Award nomination in [the same category](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-7) He followed it with the role of [Heinrich Harrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinrich_Harrer "Heinrich Harrer") in the biopic _[Seven Years in Tibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven\_Years\_in\_Tibet\_(1997\_film) "Seven Years in Tibet (1997 film)")_ (1997) and as [Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personifications_of_death "Personifications of death") in _[Meet Joe Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet\_Joe\_Black "Meet Joe Black")_ (1998).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-8) Pitt reteamed with Fincher to star in the apocalyptic film _[Fight Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fight\_Club "Fight Club")_ (1999) as anti-consumerist cult leader [Tyler Durden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyler_Durden "Tyler Durden"), a role that required him to learn [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing "Boxing"), [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo "Taekwondo"), and [grappling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grappling "Grappling").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-9) A critical and commercial disappointment at the time of release, the film has since developed a [cult status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-11) Pitt portrayed [Rusty Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rusty_Ryan_(character) "Rusty Ryan (character)") in the commercially successful heist film series _[Ocean's Trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean's\_Trilogy "Ocean's Trilogy")_ (2001–07).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-12) In 2002, he earned a [Primetime Emmy Award nomination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Guest_Actor_in_a_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series") for his guest appearance in the sitcom _[Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends\_(TV\_series) "Friends (TV series)")_ alongside his then-wife [Jennifer Aniston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Aniston "Jennifer Aniston").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-13) Also that year, Pitt started a production company, [Plan B Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plan_B_Entertainment "Plan B Entertainment"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-14) whose first release was the epic war film _[Troy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troy\_(film) "Troy (film)")_ (2004), starring Pitt. He played an assassin opposite [Angelina Jolie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelina_Jolie "Angelina Jolie") in the commercially successful action comedy _[Mr. & Mrs. Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_&\_Mrs.\_Smith\_(2005\_film) "Mr. & Mrs. Smith (2005 film)")_ (2005).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-15)

In 2006, Pitt produced the crime drama _[The Departed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Departed "The Departed")_ and starred alongside [Cate Blanchett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cate_Blanchett "Cate Blanchett") in the [multi-narrative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiperspectivity "Multiperspectivity") drama _[Babel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babel\_(2006\_film) "Babel (2006 film)")_; the former won the [Academy Award for Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). Pitt's portrayal of the eponymous man who ages in reverse in the drama _[The Curious Case of Benjamin Button](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Curious\_Case\_of\_Benjamin\_Button\_(film) "The Curious Case of Benjamin Button (film)")_ (2008) earned him an [Academy Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor") nomination.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-16) He starred in the successful war film _[Inglourious Basterds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglourious\_Basterds "Inglourious Basterds")_ (2009),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-17) and produced the superhero film _[Kick-Ass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick-Ass\_(film) "Kick-Ass (film)")_ (2010) and [its sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick-Ass_2_(film) "Kick-Ass 2 (film)") in 2013. In 2011, he earned critical acclaim for producing and starring in two films—the experimental drama _[The Tree of Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tree\_of\_Life\_(film) "The Tree of Life (film)")_ and the biopic sports drama _[Moneyball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moneyball\_(film) "Moneyball (film)")_—both of which were nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-18) He also garnered a Best Actor nomination for the latter. His biggest commercial success as a leading actor for many years was the apocalyptic film _[World War Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World\_War\_Z\_(film) "World War Z (film)")_ (2013), which grossed $540 million worldwide.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-19) That was only eclipsed by the [Apple Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Studios "Apple Studios") produced film _[F1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F1\_(film) "F1 (film)")_ in 2025. Pitt produced the period drama _[12 Years a Slave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12\_Years\_a\_Slave\_(film) "12 Years a Slave (film)")_ (2013), for which he won the Academy Award for Best Picture.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-20) In 2014, he starred in the war film _[Fury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fury\_(2014\_film) "Fury (2014 film)")_ which received positive reviews from critics and proved to be successful at the box office.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-21) For playing a stunt double to [Leonardo DiCaprio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_DiCaprio "Leonardo DiCaprio")'s character in [Quentin Tarantino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quentin_Tarantino "Quentin Tarantino")'s film _[Once Upon a Time in Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Once\_Upon\_a\_Time\_in\_Hollywood "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood")_ (2019), he won an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor"), a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture "Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture"), and a [BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-22)

Brad Pitt is an American actor and film producer. His acting career began at age 23 in 1987 with roles in the hit Fox television series _[21 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_Jump\_Street "21 Jump Street")_. He subsequently appeared in episodes for television shows during the late 1980s and played his first major role in _[The Dark Side of the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_Side\_of\_the\_Sun\_(film) "The Dark Side of the Sun (film)")_ (1988) the slasher film _[Cutting Class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutting\_Class "Cutting Class")_ (1989).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-1) He gained recognition in _[Thelma & Louise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thelma\_&\_Louise "Thelma & Louise")_ (1991), _[A River Runs Through It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_River\_Runs\_Through\_It\_(film) "A River Runs Through It (film)")_ (1992), _[Cool World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cool\_World "Cool World")_ (1992) and _[Kalifornia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalifornia "Kalifornia")_ (1993).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-Thelma-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-3)

He later took on the role of [vampire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vampire "Vampire")[Louis de Pointe du Lac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_de_Pointe_du_Lac "Louis de Pointe du Lac") in the horror drama _[Interview with the Vampire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interview\_with\_the\_Vampire\_(film) "Interview with the Vampire (film)")_ (1994) and for his performance in the epic drama _[Legends of the Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legends\_of\_the\_Fall "Legends of the Fall")_ (1994), he earned his first [Golden Globe Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Drama") nomination.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-Achath2011-4)

Pitt starred in the [David Fincher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Fincher "David Fincher")-directed, commercially successful thriller _[Seven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven\_(1995\_film) "Seven (1995 film)")_ (1995), in which he played a detective on the trail of a [serial killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serial_killer "Serial killer") who murders people he believes are guilty of the [seven deadly sins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_deadly_sins "Seven deadly sins").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-WinterHughes2007-5) His performance as a psychotic mental patient in the science fiction film _[12 Monkeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12\_Monkeys "12 Monkeys")_ won him the [Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture "Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture") and an Academy Award nomination in [the same category](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-7) He followed it with the role of [Heinrich Harrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinrich_Harrer "Heinrich Harrer") in the biopic _[Seven Years in Tibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven\_Years\_in\_Tibet\_(1997\_film) "Seven Years in Tibet (1997 film)")_ (1997) and as [Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personifications_of_death "Personifications of death") in _[Meet Joe Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet\_Joe\_Black "Meet Joe Black")_ (1998).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-8) Pitt reteamed with Fincher to star in the apocalyptic film _[Fight Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fight\_Club "Fight Club")_ (1999) as anti-consumerist cult leader [Tyler Durden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyler_Durden "Tyler Durden"), a role that required him to learn [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing "Boxing"), [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo "Taekwondo"), and [grappling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grappling "Grappling").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-9) A critical and commercial disappointment at the time of release, the film has since developed a [cult status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-11) Pitt portrayed [Rusty Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rusty_Ryan_(character) "Rusty Ryan (character)") in the commercially successful heist film series _[Ocean's Trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean's\_Trilogy "Ocean's Trilogy")_ (2001–07).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-12) In 2002, he earned a [Primetime Emmy Award nomination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Guest_Actor_in_a_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series") for his guest appearance in the sitcom _[Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends\_(TV\_series) "Friends (TV series)")_ alongside his then-wife [Jennifer Aniston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Aniston "Jennifer Aniston").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-13) Also that year, Pitt started a production company, [Plan B Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plan_B_Entertainment "Plan B Entertainment"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-14) whose first release was the epic war film _[Troy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troy\_(film) "Troy (film)")_ (2004), starring Pitt. He played an assassin opposite [Angelina Jolie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelina_Jolie "Angelina Jolie") in the commercially successful action comedy _[Mr. & Mrs. Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_&\_Mrs.\_Smith\_(2005\_film) "Mr. & Mrs. Smith (2005 film)")_ (2005).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-15)

In 2006, Pitt produced the crime drama _[The Departed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Departed "The Departed")_ and starred alongside [Cate Blanchett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cate_Blanchett "Cate Blanchett") in the [multi-narrative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiperspectivity "Multiperspectivity") drama _[Babel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babel\_(2006\_film) "Babel (2006 film)")_; the former won the [Academy Award for Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). Pitt's portrayal of the eponymous man who ages in reverse in the drama _[The Curious Case of Benjamin Button](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Curious\_Case\_of\_Benjamin\_Button\_(film) "The Curious Case of Benjamin Button (film)")_ (2008) earned him an [Academy Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor") nomination.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-16) He starred in the successful war film _[Inglourious Basterds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglourious\_Basterds "Inglourious Basterds")_ (2009),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-17) and produced the superhero film _[Kick-Ass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick-Ass\_(film) "Kick-Ass (film)")_ (2010) and [its sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick-Ass_2_(film) "Kick-Ass 2 (film)") in 2013. In 2011, he earned critical acclaim for producing and starring in two films—the experimental drama _[The Tree of Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tree\_of\_Life\_(film) "The Tree of Life (film)")_ and the biopic sports drama _[Moneyball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moneyball\_(film) "Moneyball (film)")_—both of which were nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-18) He also garnered a Best Actor nomination for the latter. His biggest commercial success as a leading actor for many years was the apocalyptic film _[World War Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World\_War\_Z\_(film) "World War Z (film)")_ (2013), which grossed $540 million worldwide.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-19) That was only eclipsed by the [Apple Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Studios "Apple Studios") produced film _[F1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F1\_(film) "F1 (film)")_ in 2025. Pitt produced the period drama _[12 Years a Slave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12\_Years\_a\_Slave\_(film) "12 Years a Slave (film)")_ (2013), for which he won the Academy Award for Best Picture.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-20) In 2014, he starred in the war film _[Fury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fury\_(2014\_film) "Fury (2014 film)")_ which received positive reviews from critics and proved to be successful at the box office.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-21) For playing a stunt double to [Leonardo DiCaprio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_DiCaprio "Leonardo DiCaprio")'s character in [Quentin Tarantino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quentin_Tarantino "Quentin Tarantino")'s film _[Once Upon a Time in Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Once\_Upon\_a\_Time\_in\_Hollywood "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood")_ (2019), he won an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor"), a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture "Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture"), and a [BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt_filmography#cite_note-22)

An actor, comedian and writer, Seth Rogen has come a long way from doing stand-up comedy as a teen.  
  
Rogen was born in Vancouver, British Columbia, to Sandy (Belogus), a social worker, and Mark Rogen, who worked for non-profits. His father is American-born and his mother is Canadian. He is of Russian Jewish descent. He attended Vancouver Talmud Torah Elementary School and Point Grey Secondary School (although he dropped out of high school to move to Los Angeles) and was known for the stand-up comedy he performed at Camp Miriam, a Habonim Dror camp. At sixteen, Rogen placed second in the 1998 Vancouver Amateur Comedy Contest.  
  
Soon after that he landed his first role in [Judd Apatow](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0031976/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s short-lived but well regarded TV series [Freaks and Geeks (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0193676/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), taking on the role of Ken Miller. Though the show only lasted one season, it was the launching pad for many careers, including Rogen, Apatow, [James Franco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0290556/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and [Jason Segel](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0781981/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). This early work sharpened Rogen's keen improvisational skills, which he's used on many projects since.  
  
Following [Freaks and Geeks (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0193676/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), he participated in a few unsuccessful television projects, and then joined the American television version of [Da Ali G Show (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0241088/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as a writer during its second and last season, along with his childhood friend and writing partner [Evan Goldberg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1698571/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). The writing team received an Emmy nomination. As a huge fan of the first season, Rogen was thrilled to get the chance to work with [Sacha Baron Cohen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0056187/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
Continuing his work with Apatow, he joined the cast of Apatow's debut film [The 40-Year-Old Virgin (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0405422/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and is credited as co-producer. After that he took the lead in [Knocked Up (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0478311/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), Apatow's second movie and a huge success. He's since been a frequent collaborator with Apatow, in projects such as [Superbad (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0829482/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Pineapple Express (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0910936/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Funny People (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1201167/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He co-wrote [Superbad (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0829482/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), with Goldberg; the pair started the project when they were teens. They won the Canadian Comedy Award for Best Writing in a Film in 2008. They later wrote [Pineapple Express (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0910936/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [The Green Hornet (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0990407/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), also starring Rogen.  
  
A talented voice artist, Rogen is in the animated films [Horton Hears a Who! (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0451079/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Kung Fu Panda (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0441773/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and [Monsters vs. Aliens (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0892782/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and has voiced characters for [The Simpsons (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0096697/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [American Dad! (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0397306/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
Rogen was named the Canadian Comedy Person of the Year by the Canadian Comedy Awards in both 2008 and 2009.  
  
Rogen lives in Los Angeles with [Lauren Miller Rogen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1601643/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), whom he met in 2004. They became engaged in September 2010 and married in October 2011.

[](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0736622/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_sm)

An actor, comedian and writer, Seth Rogen has come a long way from doing stand-up comedy as a teen.  
  
Rogen was born in Vancouver, British Columbia, to Sandy (Belogus), a social worker, and Mark Rogen, who worked for non-profits. His father is American-born and his mother is Canadian. He is of Russian Jewish descent. He attended Vancouver Talmud Torah Elementary School and Point Grey Secondary School (although he dropped out of high school to move to Los Angeles) and was known for the stand-up comedy he performed at Camp Miriam, a Habonim Dror camp. At sixteen, Rogen placed second in the 1998 Vancouver Amateur Comedy Contest.  
  
Soon after that he landed his first role in [Judd Apatow](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0031976/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s short-lived but well regarded TV series [Freaks and Geeks (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0193676/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), taking on the role of Ken Miller. Though the show only lasted one season, it was the launching pad for many careers, including Rogen, Apatow, [James Franco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0290556/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and [Jason Segel](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0781981/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). This early work sharpened Rogen's keen improvisational skills, which he's used on many projects since.  
  
Following [Freaks and Geeks (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0193676/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), he participated in a few unsuccessful television projects, and then joined the American television version of [Da Ali G Show (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0241088/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as a writer during its second and last season, along with his childhood friend and writing partner [Evan Goldberg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1698571/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). The writing team received an Emmy nomination. As a huge fan of the first season, Rogen was thrilled to get the chance to work with [Sacha Baron Cohen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0056187/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
Continuing his work with Apatow, he joined the cast of Apatow's debut film [The 40-Year-Old Virgin (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0405422/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and is credited as co-producer. After that he took the lead in [Knocked Up (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0478311/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), Apatow's second movie and a huge success. He's since been a frequent collaborator with Apatow, in projects such as [Superbad (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0829482/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Pineapple Express (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0910936/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Funny People (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1201167/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He co-wrote [Superbad (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0829482/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), with Goldberg; the pair started the project when they were teens. They won the Canadian Comedy Award for Best Writing in a Film in 2008. They later wrote [Pineapple Express (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0910936/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [The Green Hornet (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0990407/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), also starring Rogen.  
  
A talented voice artist, Rogen is in the animated films [Horton Hears a Who! (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0451079/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Kung Fu Panda (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0441773/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and [Monsters vs. Aliens (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0892782/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and has voiced characters for [The Simpsons (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0096697/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [American Dad! (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0397306/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
Rogen was named the Canadian Comedy Person of the Year by the Canadian Comedy Awards in both 2008 and 2009.  
  
Rogen lives in Los Angeles with [Lauren Miller Rogen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1601643/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), whom he met in 2004. They became engaged in September 2010 and married in October 2011.

# Let's build a bridge

There was no industrial base on the island. No ironworks or engineering factories, so the bridge and the sheds had to be imported. They ordered the bridge from [David Rowell & Co.](http://www.bridgemeister.com/bridge.php?bid=1922) in London. It cost £2,281.00 and was shipped to the Falkland Islands on the SS Ballena. I wonder how much a replacement kit would cost these days?

The foreman, Mr. E. S. Crawford, was a mason so he directed the construction of the footings for the two towers and the bases for the ramp on the Southern bank.

There were only two machines available for the team to use. One was a cement mixer, and the other was a stone breaker. As you can imagine, the stone breaker was incredibly noisy. People could hear it all the way back in Goose Green when it was running.

Robert Rowlands has told me:

> "That same old rock crusher with a different engine was set up in Stanley by the FIC and I remember it in use when I was a boy in the 1960's in the middle of the town, you could not see some houses on Fitzroy road for dust when it was operating."

[![Image 5](https://bodiecreekbridge.com/images/FI0037_small.jpg)](javascript:OpenWin('Pic06.html'); "Click to enlarge")  
The cement mixer[![Image 6](https://bodiecreekbridge.com/images/FI0032_small.jpg)](javascript:OpenWin('Pic07.html'); "Click to enlarge")  
The stone breaker

[![Image 7](https://bodiecreekbridge.com/images/FI0038_small.jpg)](javascript:OpenWin('Pic08.html'); "Click to enlarge") The team of men who worked on the bridge were the local sheep farmers. They were the only workforce available, so everyone pitched in. A real team effort.

There were no cranes, no earthmovers, no trucks. Everything had to be done by hand. Apart from one engineer and a mason, the rest of the workforce were not skilled civil engineers – they were local sheep farmers. You can see the convoys of men with wheelbarrows as they moved the rubble or brought down the concrete.

My father (Charles' son, Pete) told me he visited the site from time to time. There was a hut that was used as an office. The office contained a table and a couple of benches. The benches were boxes which could open out to make a bed. Sometimes his father stayed on site overnight and slept in this makeshift bed. My dad was amazed to think that his Dad slept in a wooden box!

[![Image 8](https://bodiecreekbridge.com/images/FI0031_small.jpg)](javascript:OpenWin('Pic09.html'); "Click to enlarge") The foundations for the bases at both ends of the bridge had to be blasted out of solid rock using explosives. You can get an idea of how much material had to be removed from this photo. Every stone had to be taken away in a wheelbarrow.

One day there was a loud blast in the settlement at Goose Green. It turned out that some of the local boys had been over to the site at had found that the emptied explosive containers still contained some powder so they collected it, brought it back to Goose Green and set it off under a peat stack. Pete was with them at the time, but since he was only small he didn't manage to get away as fast as the other lads and he got spattered with the debris. After that a few new rules concerning Health and Safety were implemented. All the containers and charges had to be collected and emptied after each blast. The explosives were kept under lock and key.

[![Image 9](https://bodiecreekbridge.com/images/FI0044_small.jpg)](javascript:OpenWin('Pic10.html'); "Click to enlarge")There were no cranes, so how on earth could they lift the assembled 40 foot tall towers into place? Charles found an abandoned schooner-rigged yacht, probably the Gwendolin, and he adapted the twin masts to form an improvised lifting gear by means of ropes and pulleys. And it worked well, as you can see in the photos.

Construction was started in October 1924 and the bridge was completed in July 1925 – less than a year’s work.

After the bridge had been built, work on the approach roads was completed by the end of October 1925, enabling the first sheep to be brought across the bridge in time for the new shearing season.

[![Image 10](https://bodiecreekbridge.com/images/FI0028_small.jpg)](javascript:OpenWin('Pic13.html'); "Click to enlarge")

There are reports that the Bodie Creek Suspension Bridge is the most southerly suspension bridge in the world, and I am quite sure that this was true at the time it was constructed. In fact there is not much land on the planet south of this latitude and I haven’t seen any claims which counter this assertion, so I like to believe it is still true to this day. Even so, claims are now being watered down to “one of the most southerly ...” Pah. The only others that I have been able to find are timber and rope constructs for walkers in the mountains of Patagonia. Of course, I could be wrong. Does anyone actually know of a steel suspension bridge further south than this?

I have walked across the [Clifton Suspension Bridge](http://www.clifton-suspension-bridge.org.uk/), designed by the great Isambard Kingdom Brunel. It is a truly inspirational structure and a fantastic feat of engineering, but he did have rather more resources, men, equipment and materials at his disposal. With modern day technology and unlimited finances, the French have built the spectacular Viaduct de Millau [http://www.abelard.org/france/viaduct-de-millau.php](http://www.abelard.org/france/viaduct-de-millau.php) In my humble opinion, for what they have achieved the handful of hardy Falkland Islanders who had the enterprise, ingenuity and determination and sheer strength required to build the Bodie Creek Suspension Bridge can hold their heads up with pride amongst such illustrious company.

# Emmanuel Missionary College (1901–1960)

#### By [Meredith Jones Gray](https://encyclopedia.adventist.org/)

_×_
Meredith Jones Gray was born and raised in Michigan, U.S.A., where her father taught mathematics at Emmanuel Missionary College and then Andrews University in Berrien Springs. She attended the elementary and secondary schools on the Andrews campus, and earned a B.A. degree in French and an M.A. in English from Andrews University. She completed her Ph.D. in English Language and Literature at the University of Michigan and has taught in the Department of English at Andrews University since 1982.
