### Script

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Script")]

> ...I feel the tone of the movie is its own thing. I think there are elements of satire, but I don't think it should be categorized just as that. There are elements of parody in it, but obviously I don't think it's just that. I feel like hopefully it's its own thing, which has a lot of familiar stuff that we are playing off of.

—Ben Stiller reacting to the film being called a [spoof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parody "Parody")[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-PushBoundaries-21)

Ben Stiller developed the premise for _Tropic Thunder_ while shooting _[Empire of the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire\_of\_the\_Sun\_(film) "Empire of the Sun (film)")_,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ew-22) in which he played a small part. He wanted to make a film based on the actors he knew who became "self-important" and "self-involved" and appeared to believe that they had been part of a real military unit after taking part in boot camps to prepare for war film roles.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-FakeBoot-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-HollySpo-24)

Co-writer Justin Theroux revealed that the initial script concept was to have actors go to a mock boot camp and return with [post-traumatic stress disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-traumatic_stress_disorder "Post-traumatic stress disorder").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommPTSD-25) The final script was developed to satirize Vietnam War films such as _[Apocalypse Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apocalypse\_Now "Apocalypse Now")_, _[Rambo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rambo\_(film\_series) "Rambo (film series)")_, _[Missing in Action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missing\_in\_Action\_(film) "Missing in Action (film)")_, _[Platoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platoon\_(film) "Platoon (film)")_, _[Full Metal Jacket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full\_Metal\_Jacket "Full Metal Jacket")_, _[Hamburger Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburger\_Hill "Hamburger Hill")_, and _[The Deer Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Deer\_Hunter "The Deer Hunter")_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-TelegraphReviewDeer-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-MitchellFilms-27) Theroux pointed out that viewers have an increased awareness of the inner workings of Hollywood due to celebrity websites and Hollywood news sources, so the script was easier to write.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-HollySpo-24) Dialogue for unscripted portions of the storyboard was developed on set by the actors or was improvised.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommImprovise-28)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Casting")]

[![Image 11: A white man with a thin beard, wearing a suit, and looking to his right, smiling.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Robert_Downey_Jr_2014_Comic_Con_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Robert_Downey_Jr_2014_Comic_Con_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Robert_Downey_Jr_2014_Comic_Con_(cropped).jpg)

[![Image 12: A film screenshot showing the same man wearing extensive makeup to appear as an African American.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/c/cc/DowneyKirkLazarusTTCostume.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DowneyKirkLazarusTTCostume.jpg)

Robert Downey Jr. shown with his character Kirk Lazarus, himself in character as Lincoln Osiris. To portray the character, Downey required two hours of make-up application.

Stiller's original plan was to cast [Keanu Reeves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keanu_Reeves "Keanu Reeves") as Tugg Speedman and himself as Rick Peck.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-29)[Etan Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etan_Cohen "Etan Cohen") created the role of Kirk Lazarus as a way of lampooning the great lengths that some method actors go to depict a role.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ew-22)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-WarGamesDN-30) Robert Downey Jr. was approached by Stiller about the part while on vacation in [Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyHawaii-31) Downey said on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS")'s _[The Early Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Early\_Show "The Early Show")_ that his first reaction was, "This is the stupidest idea I've ever heard!" and that Stiller responded, "Yeah, I know– isn't it great?"[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-CBS-32) In another interview, Downey said that he accepted the part but, having no idea where or even how to start building the character of Lazarus, eventually settled on a [jive-esque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_Vernacular_English "African-American Vernacular English") speech pattern and a ragged bass voice; he then auditioned Lazarus's voice over the phone to Stiller, who approved the characterization immediately.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-WonderBoysAlley-10) Downey revealed that he modeled the character on actors [Russell Crowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_Crowe "Russell Crowe"), [Colin Farrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Farrell "Colin Farrell"), and [Daniel Day-Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Day-Lewis "Daniel Day-Lewis").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyCharacters-33) The initial script was written for Downey's character to be Irish, but was altered after Downey stated he could improvise better as an Australian, having previously played a similar outlandish Australian character in the film _[Natural Born Killers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural\_Born\_Killers "Natural Born Killers")_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-AustMate-34) Downey's practice of remaining in character between takes and even off the film set was also written into the script for his character to perform.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-PlayingWar-35) Downey required between one-and-a-half and two hours of makeup application.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommMakeup-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyEWMakeup-37) According to Downey, "One makeup artist would start on one side of my face and a second makeup artist would start on the other side, and then they'd meet in the middle."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyEWMakeup-37)

Downey acknowledged the potential controversy over his role: "At the end of the day, it's always about how well you commit to the character. If I didn't feel it was morally sound, or that it would be easily misinterpreted that I'm just [C. Thomas Howell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._Thomas_Howell "C. Thomas Howell") [in _[Soul Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul\_Man\_(film) "Soul Man (film)")_], I would've stayed home."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ew-22) Co-star [Brandon T. Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_T._Jackson "Brandon T. Jackson") stated: "When I first read the script, I was like: What? [Blackface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackface "Blackface")? But when I saw him [act] he, like, became a black man ... It was just good acting. It was weird on the set because he would keep going with the character. He's a method actor."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-PeopleJacksonQ-38) Stiller commented on Downey's portrayal of a white actor playing a black man: "When people see the movie– in the context of the film, he's playing a method actor who's gone to great lengths to play a black guy. The movie is skewering actors and how they take themselves so seriously."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-StillInterEmpire-39) Stiller previewed the film before the [NAACP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAACP "NAACP"), and several black journalists reacted positively to the character.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-PlayingWar-35)

[![Image 13: A man wearing a black shirt and smiling to his right.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/Tom_Cruise_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg/250px-Tom_Cruise_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tom_Cruise_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg)

[![Image 14: A film screenshot showing the same man wearing extensive makeup and accessories to appear bald, have extra hair on his chest and arms, and is overweight.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/7/74/TomCruiseLesGrossmanTTCostume.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TomCruiseLesGrossmanTTCostume.jpg)

Tom Cruise shown with his character Les Grossman. To portray his character, Cruise used a [fatsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatsuit "Fatsuit"), fake large hands, and a bald cap; many commented that the character's physical appearance was loosely based on film producers [Scott Rudin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Rudin "Scott Rudin") and [Harvey Weinstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Weinstein "Harvey Weinstein").

Tom Cruise was initially set to cameo as Stiller's character's agent, Rick Peck. Instead, Cruise suggested adding a studio head character, and the idea was incorporated into the script. Stiller and Cruise worked together to create the new character, Les Grossman, as a middle-aged businessman. The role required that Cruise don a [fatsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatsuit "Fatsuit"), large prosthetic hands, and a bald cap.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-TrailerEddie-7)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-AustMate-34) It was Cruise's idea to give the character large hands and dance to "[Low](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_(Flo_Rida_song) "Low (Flo Rida song)")".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-CruiseHandLow-40) Stiller intended to keep Cruise's role a secret until the film's release. In addition, [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures") refused to release promotional pictures of Cruise's character to the media.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-cieply-41) In November 2007, images of Cruise wearing a bald headpiece and a fatsuit appeared on _[Inside Edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside\_Edition "Inside Edition")_, as well as on the Internet.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-FatSuitTom-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-PeopleCameo-43) Cruise's attorneys threatened a lawsuit if photos showing Cruise in costume were published.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ninemsn-44) They approached various sites that were hosting the image and quickly had it removed.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SpoilSurprise-45) A representative for Cruise stated: "Mr. Cruise's appearance was supposed to be a surprise for his fans worldwide. [Paparazzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paparazzi "Paparazzi") have ruined what should have been a fun discovery for moviegoers."[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SpoilSurprise-45) The photography agency INF, who debuted the image, responded with a statement: "While these pictures were taken without breaking any [criminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal_law "Criminal law") or [civil laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_law "Private law"), we've decided to pull them from circulation effective immediately."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-FatSuitTom-42)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ninemsn-44)

Serving as a last-minute replacement, Tobey Maguire was available to be on set for only two hours to film his scenes in _Satan's Alley_.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommSatAll-46) Downey said he was amazed Maguire would agree to do the film and felt like they were creating a "[karmic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karmic "Karmic") pay-off" for their scenes together in the 2000 film _[Wonder Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder\_Boys\_(film) "Wonder Boys (film)")_, where Downey's character has a one-night stand with Maguire's character.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-WonderBoysAlley-10) After Cruise vacated the role of Rick Peck, [Owen Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Wilson "Owen Wilson") was cast to play the part. Following his [suicide attempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide_attempt "Suicide attempt") in August 2007, Wilson dropped out of the film and was replaced by [Matthew McConaughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_McConaughey "Matthew McConaughey").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-OwenRecast-47)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Filming")]

Southern California and Mexico were considered for the main unit filming, but Stiller selected the Hawaiian island of [Kauaʻi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaua%CA%BBi "Kauaʻi"), where he has a home, for the majority of the shooting.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SoCal-48) Kaua ʻ i was chosen over Mexico because a tax credit was negotiated with the Kaua ʻ i Film Commission for in-state spending.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-Kaua{{okina}}i-49) Cinematographer [John Toll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Toll "John Toll") stated that the island was also selected for its similarity to Vietnam, based on its dense foliage, variety of terrains, and weather.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-JohnKodak-50) Kaua ʻ i was first scouted in 2004 as a possible location to film _Tropic Thunder_. Stiller spent more than 25 hours over six weeks exploring the island, using all-terrain vehicles, boats, and helicopters.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SoCal-48)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommScout-51) DreamWorks gave the green light for filming in 2006, but preproduction lasted for six months, most of this time spent on scouting additional locations for filming.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-TrailerEddie-7)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SoCal-48) Filming occurred on sets at [Universal Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Studios_Lot "Universal Studios Lot") in Hollywood for the Los Angeles and interior scenes.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SoCal-48)

[![Image 15: An overhead view of a set of buildings located in a dense jungle. A river runs to the left of the buildings, and moving trucks are seen to the right of the buildings. There is a dirt road leading from the buildings to other buildings.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/TropicThunderSetAbove07.jpg/250px-TropicThunderSetAbove07.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TropicThunderSetAbove07.jpg)

Film set in Kaua ʻ i in September 2007

_Tropic Thunder_ was the first major studio production on Kaua ʻ i in five years. It is the largest production filmed on the island to date, and contributed more than $60 million to the local economy.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SoCal-48)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-CutsImpact-52) Tim Ryan, the executive editor of _Hawaii Film & Video Magazine_, commented on the filming on the island: "I think _Tropic Thunder_ will give Kaua ʻ i much needed and long idled publicity in the production arena.... It should put Kaua ʻ i back on the production consideration radar."[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-GardenIsland-53) Preliminary production crews were on the island starting in December 2006, and principal photography began in July 2007, with filming lasting 13 weeks over seven separate locations on the island.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-GardenIsland-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-StillerVogue-54) Much of the filming took place on private land as well as conservation status designated areas.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-CutsImpact-52) Casting calls on the island sought 500 residents to portray the villagers in the film.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-GardenIsland-53) Two units shot simultaneously on the island from the ground, and an aerial unit shot from helicopters.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-JohnTreks-55) Many of the sets and the bridge used for one of the final scenes were built in three months.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommSets3-56) The island's erratic weather hampered filming with rain and lightning.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommRain-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommLight-58) The crew also faced complications in moving the equipment and cast due to the difficult terrain.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-JohnKodak-50)

The film advising company [Warriors Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warriors_Inc. "Warriors Inc.") was enlisted to ensure that the war scenes looked authentic, including the attire worn by the actors. Former members of the U.S. military taught the actors how to handle, fire, and reload their weapons, as well as to perform various tactical movements.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-WarFilming-59) The opening war scene was filmed over three weeks and required 50 stuntmen.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDComm3Weeks-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommStuntMen-61)[Animatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animatic "Animatic") were used to map out the necessary camera angles for filming.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommStoryboard-62)

### Effects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Effects")]

Six companies working on different scenes and elements created 500 shots of [visual effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_effects "Visual effects") in the film. These were at times altered weekly due to the reactions of test audiences in screenings.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-VFXTT-63) CIS Visual Effects Group assisted with the _Scorcher VI_ faux trailer and twenty additional shots for the home media release.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-VFXTDVD-64) To expand on the comedy in the film, some of the explosions and crashes were embellished to look more destructive. The visual effects supervisor Michael Fink reflected on the exaggerated explosions: "We worked really hard to make the [CG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-generated_imagery "Computer-generated imagery") crashing helicopter in the hot landing sequence look real. Ben was adamant about that, but at the same time he wanted the explosion to be huge. When you see it hit the ground, it was like it was filled with gasoline! It was the same thing with Ben's sergeant character, who almost intercepts a hand grenade... Now, I was in the Army for three years and no hand grenade would make an explosion like that... But it was a big dramatic moment and it looks really cool... and feels kind of real."[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-VFXTT-63)

Filming the large [napalm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napalm "Napalm") explosion in the opening scene of the film required a 450-foot (140-meter) row of explosive pots containing 1,100 U.S. gallons (4,200 liters) of gasoline and diesel fuel. All the palm trees used in the explosion were moved to the specific location after the crew determined the impact of the lighting and necessary camera angles.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommTrees-65) Due to the size and cost of the 1.25-second explosion, it was performed only once and was captured from twelve cameras.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-WarFilming-59)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-Napalm-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDComm12C-67) For the safety of the crew and cast, the detonators were added one hour before the explosion and nobody was allowed to be within 400 feet (120 m) during detonation.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommOneHour-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommExplosion-69) The explosion was made up of twelve individual explosions and resulted in a [mushroom cloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom_cloud "Mushroom cloud") that reached 350 feet (110 m) in the air.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-WarFilming-59)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-Napalm-66) For the scene in the film, Danny McBride's character, Cody Underwood, was the only actor shown in the shot of the explosion. All the other characters were added digitally.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommCody-70) The explosion of the bridge in one of the final scenes used nine cameras to capture the shot, and the crew was required to be 3,000 feet (910 m) away for their safety.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCommStuntMen-61)

## Promotion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Promotion")]

[![Image 16: A crowd of people is all looking towards a man at the center who is signing a hat. The crowd is attempting to hand him posters to sign and others are taking pictures using cameras and cell phones.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/BenStillerTropicThunderPendleton.jpg/250px-BenStillerTropicThunderPendleton.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BenStillerTropicThunderPendleton.jpg)

Stiller signing autographs before a screening at [Camp Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Pendleton "Camp Pendleton") on August 3, 2008

A trailer for the film was released in April 2008. The _[Calgary Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calgary\_Herald "Calgary Herald")_ gave it a rating of 3/5, commenting: "This could either be good or very, very bad."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-CalHerVB-71) Gary Susman of _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ questioned whether the film would "...turn into precisely the kind of bloated action monstrosity that it's making fun of."[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-EWBloated-72) The trailer received the "Best Comedy Trailer" award at the 9th annual [Golden Trailer Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Trailer_Awards "Golden Trailer Awards").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-GTA-73)[DreamWorks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DreamWorks_Pictures "DreamWorks Pictures") also released a [red band trailer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_trailer#United_States_MPAA_rating_cards "Film trailer"), the first of its kind used by the studio to promote one of its films.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-Redband-74)

Stiller, Downey, and Black appeared on the seventh-season finale of _[American Idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Idol "American Idol")_ in a sketch as [The Pips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gladys_Knight_&_the_Pips "Gladys Knight & the Pips") performing with [Gladys Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gladys_Knight "Gladys Knight") (via [archival footage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archival_footage "Archival footage")).[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-EWInterview-75) The three actors also later performed a sketch at the [2008 MTV Movie Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_MTV_Movie_Awards "2008 MTV Movie Awards") which featured the actors attempting to create a successful [viral video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viral_video "Viral video") to promote the film with awkward results.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-EWInterview-75) In September 2008, Stiller and Downey attended the [San Sebastián International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Sebasti%C3%A1n_International_Film_Festival "San Sebastián International Film Festival") to promote the film. A screening was shown, but it was not chosen to compete against the other films at the festival.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SanSebast-76)

Between April 2008 and the film's commercial release in August 2008, the film had over 250 promotional screenings.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-NYTBoycott-77) On August 3, 2008, Stiller, Downey, and Black visited [Camp Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Pendleton "Camp Pendleton"), a [U.S. Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Marine_Corps "U.S. Marine Corps") base in [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), to present a screening to over a thousand military members and their families. The screening was on behalf of the [United Service Organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Service_Organizations "United Service Organizations") and included the actors heading to the screening by helicopter and [Humvees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humvees "Humvees").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-CampScreening-78) On August 8, 2008, a special 30-minute fictional _[E! True Hollywood Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E!\_True\_Hollywood\_Story "E! True Hollywood Story")_ aired about the making of _Tropic Thunder_. In video games, a themed scavenger hunt was incorporated into _[Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Vegas 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom\_Clancy's\_Rainbow\_Six:\_Vegas\_2 "Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Vegas 2")_, and Stiller allowed his likeness to be used in the online [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") application game based on the film.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-RainbowSix-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-FacebookGame-80)

As a tie-in for the film's release, Paramount announced it would market the energy drink known in the film as "Booty Sweat".[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BootySweat-81) Michael Corcoran, Paramount's president of consumer products, commented on the release: "We're very excited, because it has the potential to live for quite a while, well beyond the film."[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BootySweat-81) The drink was sold in college bookstores, on [Amazon.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon.com "Amazon.com"), and at other retailers.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BootySweat-81)

### Faux websites and mockumentary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Faux websites and mockumentary")]

Several faux websites were created for the characters and some of their prior film roles. A website for _Simple Jack_, a faux film exhibited within the film, was removed by DreamWorks on August 4, 2008, due to protests from disability advocates.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SimpleJackPulled-82) In addition, other promotional websites were created for "Make Pretty Skin Clinic", the fictitious company that performed the surgery of the film's character Kirk Lazarus, along with one for the energy drink "Booty Sweat".

In mid-July 2008, a faux trailer for the [mockumentary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mockumentary "Mockumentary")_Rain of Madness_ was released. The mockumentary was a parody of _[Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker's Apocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearts\_of\_Darkness:\_A\_Filmmaker's\_Apocalypse "Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker's Apocalypse")_.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-MadnessEW-83) It follows co-writer Justin Theroux as a fictitious documentarian named Jan Jürgen documenting the behind-the-scenes aspects of the[_[which?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Avoid\_weasel\_words "Wikipedia:Avoid weasel words")_][film within the film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Story_within_a_story "Story within a story"). Marketing for the faux documentary included a movie poster and an official website prior to _Tropic Thunder_'s release. The mockumentary was released on the [iTunes Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes_Store "ITunes Store") after the film's release and was also included on the home video release.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-RoMTT-84) Amy Powell, an advertising executive with Paramount, reflected on the timing of the release of _Madness_: "We always thought that people would be talking about _Tropic Thunder_ at the water cooler, and that's why we decided to release _Rain of Madness_ two weeks into _Tropic_'s run—to keep this positive buzz going."[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-RainMadnessQuote-85)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Release")]

### Theatrical release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Theatrical release")]

_Tropic Thunder_ held an early screening at the 2008 [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con"),[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-86) two weeks before it officially premiered on August 11, 2008, at the Mann Village Theatre in [Westwood, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westwood,_Los_Angeles,_California "Westwood, Los Angeles, California") and two days before its wide release. Members of several disability groups picketed before the premiere, protesting at the portrayal of [intellectual disability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_disability "Intellectual disability") shown in the film.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-USATProtest-87) The groups revealed that it was the first time that they had ever protested together at an event.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-USATProtest-87) As a result of the protest, the normally unobstructed views of the red carpet leading to the premiere were blocked off by 10-foot (3-m)-high fences and there was an increase in the number of security personnel present.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ProtestPremiere-88) No protests were held at the United Kingdom's September premiere.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ProtestPremiereUK-89)

The North American release was scheduled for July 11, 2008, but was delayed until August 15, before being brought forward to August 13.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ReleaseDateShuffle-90) As a result of the move from July, [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox") moved its [family comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_film "Family film")_[Meet Dave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet\_Dave "Meet Dave")_ in the open slot.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ReleaseDateShuffle-90) The August 13 release date was also the opening weekends for the animated family film _[Star Wars: The Clone Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Clone\_Wars\_(film) "Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)")_ and the horror film _[Mirrors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirrors\_(2008\_film) "Mirrors (2008 film)")_. Studios consider the third week of August to be a weaker performing period than earlier in the summer because of students returning to school.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-AugustWeekend-91) Previous [R-rated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_Picture_Association_of_America_film_rating_system "Motion Picture Association of America film rating system") comedies such as _[The 40-Year-Old Virgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_40-Year-Old\_Virgin "The 40-Year-Old Virgin")_ and _[Superbad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superbad "Superbad")_ were released in mid-August and performed well at the box office. Reacting to _Tropic Thunder'_ s release date, [Rob Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Moore_(executive) "Rob Moore (executive)"), vice chairman of Paramount Pictures, stated, "For a young person at the end of summer, you want to have some fun and forget about going back to school. What better than a crazy comedy?"[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-AugustWeekend-91)

## Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Home media")]

This Kaua ʻ i film set was used for the Tugg Speedman "Let's be friends" speech scene.

_Tropic Thunder_ was released in the United States on [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD") and [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") on November 18, 2008, three months after its release and a week after the end of its theatrical run in the US and Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BOXMOJO-6) The film was released on home video on January 26, 2009, in the United Kingdom. Special features include [audio commentaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_commentaries "Audio commentaries") (including one featuring Stiller, Downey, and Black, with Downey providing his commentary as Lincoln Osiris, a nod to a joke in the film that Lazarus never breaks character until he completes the DVD commentary), several featurettes, [deleted scenes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deleted_scene "Deleted scene"), and an alternate ending. A 2-disc director's cut, with 12 minutes of extended footage, was also released, containing additional special features and the _Rain of Madness_ mockumentary.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDAnnounced-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDHere-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyDVDCommentary-94)

For the film's first week of release, _Tropic Thunder_ placed on several video charts. It reached second place on the [Nielsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research "Nielsen Media Research") VideoScan First Alert sales chart and Nielsen's Blu-ray Disc chart, earning $19,064,959 (not including Blu-ray sales).[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDSales-95) In rentals, it placed first on the _[Home Media Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home\_Media\_Magazine "Home Media Magazine")'_ s video rental chart.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDCharts-96) The DVD sales in 2008 totaled $42,271,059, placing it in 28th for DVD sales for the year.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDSalesRank-97) By September 2009, 2,963,000 DVD units had been sold, gathering revenue of $49,870,248.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDSales-95)

In September 2008, the film's producer DreamWorks Pictures split from Paramount Pictures and became an independent studio again, with Paramount's parent company [Viacom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viacom_(2005%E2%80%932019) "Viacom (2005–2019)") having purchased DreamWorks in February 2006.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-98) However, after the split happened, Paramount still retained the rights to all of the live-action films DreamWorks had produced since 1997, including _Tropic Thunder_.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-99) It was later made available on Paramount's streaming service [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-100) In 2022, a [HDR Dolby Vision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolby_Vision "Dolby Vision") mastered [Ultra HD Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra_HD_Blu-ray "Ultra HD Blu-ray") was released through [Kino Lorber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kino_Lorber "Kino Lorber"), under license from Paramount.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-101)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Critical response")]

The review aggregation website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") gives _Tropic Thunder_ a rating of 82% based on 249 reviews and an average rating of 7.4/10. The website's critical consensus reads, "With biting satire, plenty of subversive humor, and an unforgettable turn by Robert Downey Jr., _Tropic Thunder_ is a triumphant late summer comedy."[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-RTfresh-102)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic") gave a film score of 71 out of 100 based on 39 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-MetaCritic-103) Audiences polled by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade of "B" on an A+ to F scale.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-104)

[Michael Cieply](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Cieply "Michael Cieply") from the _[New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_York\_Times "New York Times")_ stated that the film was "shaping up as one of [Paramount]'s best prospects for the summer."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-cieply-41) Claudia Puig of _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA\_Today "USA Today")_ gave the film a somewhat positive review: "There are some wildly funny scenes, a few leaden ones and others that are scattershot, with humorous satire undercut by over-the-top grisliness. Still, when it's funny, it's really funny."[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-USATReview-105)

Other reviewers were more critical. Todd McCarthy's review in _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ stated: "Apart from startling, out-there comic turns by Robert Downey Jr. and Tom Cruise, however, the antics here are pretty thin, redundant and one-note."[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-VarietyReview-106)[Glenn Kenny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Kenny "Glenn Kenny") of _[RogerEbert.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RogerEbert.com "RogerEbert.com")_ said that the film was "intermittently amusing but entirely smug and hateful."[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-GlennKenny-107) Rick Groen of _[The Globe and Mail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Globe\_and\_Mail "The Globe and Mail")_ said that it was "an assault in the guise of a comedy—watching it is like getting mugged by a clown."[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-GlobeReview-108) J.R. Jones of _[Chicago Reader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Reader "Chicago Reader")_ stated, "The rest of the movie never lives up to the hilarity of the opening, partly because the large-scale production smothers the gags but mostly because those gags are so easy to smother."[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ChicagoReaderReview-109)[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") of the _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_ gave 3.5/4 and wrote, "The movie is, may I say, considerably better than Stiller's previous film, _[Zoolander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoolander "Zoolander")_ (2001). It's the kind of summer comedy that rolls in, makes a lot of people laugh and rolls on to video."[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-EbertJr-110)

The faux trailers before the film also received mixed reviews. [David Ansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ansen "David Ansen") of _[Newsweek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsweek "Newsweek")_ approved of the trailers: "_Tropic Thunder_ is the funniest movie of the summer—so funny, in fact, that you start laughing before the film itself has begun."[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BudgetNewsweek-111) Christy Lemire of the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") called the trailers "the best part of the trip."[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-LemireTrip-112) Robert Wilonsky of _[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Village\_Voice "The Village Voice")_ was critical, saying that the trailers' comedy "resides in the land of the obvious, easy chuckle."[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-WioVillage-113)

Downey, Stiller, Black, and Cruise were repeatedly singled out for praise by numerous critics, claiming that they "stole the show", were "off-the-charts hilarious", and would bring viewers "the fondest memories" of their work.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-EbertJr-110)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-WeitzJr-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-PeteRoll-115) Scott Feinberg of the _Los Angeles Times_ criticized the concept of Downey's portrayal of a white actor portraying an African American: "I just can't imagine any circumstance under which a blackface performance would be acceptable, any more than I can imagine any circumstance under which the use of the N-word would be acceptable."[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ScottFace-116) Sara Vilkomerson said that Cruise did "an astonishingly funny and surprising supporting performance."[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SaraObser-117) Logan Hill of _[New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_York\_(magazine) "New York (magazine)")_ criticized Cruise's appearance, saying that it "just makes him look a little lost and almost pathetic—shucking and jiving, trying to appeal to the younger moviegoers who are abandoning him."[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-LogHillNY-118)

Several critics commented on the controversy over lines in the film about the mentally disabled. Duane Dudek of the _[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee\_Journal\_Sentinel "Milwaukee Journal Sentinel")_ wrote that the film "is just sophomoric enough to offend. And while it is also funny, it is without the empathy or compassion to cause us to wonder why we are laughing."[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DDWhy-119) Christian Toto of _[The Washington Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Times "The Washington Times")_ argued against the opposition: "_Tropic Thunder_ is drawing fire from special interest groups" for "its frequent use of the word 'retard', but discerning audiences will know where the humor is targeted. And they'll be laughing too hard to take offense."[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-TotoFire-120)

### Critics' lists

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Critics' lists")]

In January 2009, _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ included _Tropic Thunder_ in its list "25 Great Comedies From the Past 25 Years" for its "spot-on skewering of Hollywood."[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-25Great-121) The film also appeared on several critics' top ten lists of the best films of 2008.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-mctop08-122)[Stephen King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King "Stephen King") placed it at the fourth position, calling the film "the funniest, most daring comedy of the year."[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-King4-123)_[The Oregonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Oregonian "The Oregonian")_'s Marc Mohan, placed it sixth, and several critics placed it seventh: Elizabeth Weitzman of the _[New York Daily News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_York\_Daily\_News "New York Daily News")_, _[Premiere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premiere\_(magazine) "Premiere (magazine)")_ magazine, Mike Russell of _The Oregonian_, as well as Peter Hartlaub of the _[San Francisco Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Francisco\_Chronicle "San Francisco Chronicle")_.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-mctop08-122) David Ansen of _Newsweek_ placed it eighth and Lisa Schwarzbaum of _Entertainment Weekly_ included the film in the tenth position.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-mctop08-122) In 2025, it was one of the films voted for the "Readers' Choice" edition of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_' list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century," finishing at number 217.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-124)

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Box office")]

[Stacey Snider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stacey_Snider "Stacey Snider"), the chief executive of DreamWorks, suggested that the film would earn around $30 million in its opening weekend and go on to be as successful as _[Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borat:\_Cultural\_Learnings\_of\_America\_for\_Make\_Benefit\_Glorious\_Nation\_of\_Kazakhstan "Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan")_, which earned $129 million in the U.S. and Canada and $260 million worldwide.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-Redband-74)_[The Dark Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_Knight "The Dark Knight")_ had been the number one film at the box office for the four weeks prior to the release of _Tropic Thunder_. Bob Thompson, a writer for the _[National Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Post "National Post")_, speculated that _Tropic Thunder_'s opening weekend would outperform _The Dark Knight_ for the weekend.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-NationalKnight-125) In a list compiled prior to the summer's film releases, _Entertainment Weekly_ predicted that the film would be the tenth highest-grossing film of the summer at the American box office with $142.6 million.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-EWBoxOffice-126)

_Tropic Thunder_ opened in 3,319 theaters and, for its first five days of American and Canadian release, earned $36.8 million. The film placed first in the weekend's box office with $25.8 million surpassing _[Star Wars: The Clone Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Clone\_Wars\_(film) "Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)")_ and _[Mirrors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirrors\_(2008\_film) "Mirrors (2008 film)")_, which debuted the same weekend.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BOXMOJO-6) Reacting to the film's opening receipts, DreamWorks spokesman Chip Sullivan stated, "We're thrilled, quite frankly. It played out exactly how we hoped."[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-MSNBCBoxOffice-127) In foreign markets for the film's opening weekend, it was released in 418 Russian and 19 [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") locations earning $2.2 million and $319,000, respectively.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-VarietyForeignBOX-128)

The film maintained its number one position at the American and Canadian box office for the following two weekends, making it the second film in 2008 (after _The Dark Knight_) to hold the number-one position for more than two consecutive weekends.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-EWThreeWeek-129)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-LATThreeWeek-130) The film's widest release was in 3,473 theaters, placing it in the top 25 widest releases in the U.S. for 2008.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BOXMOJO-6) For 2008, the film was the fifth-highest-grossing domestic R-rated film.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BOXR-131) The film's U.S. and Canada gross of over $110 million made _Tropic Thunder_ Stiller's most successful film as a director.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BOXMOJOStiller-132) The film has had gross receipts of $110.5 million in the U.S. and Canada and $85.2 million in international markets for a total of $195.7 million worldwide.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BOXMOJO-6)

### Accolades

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Accolades")]

> "It's so funny to me that the role is a guy who is an Oscar-seeking moron. His whole motivation is Oscars ...Irony is synonymous with pretty much everything that is going on."

—Downey reacting to his Academy Award nomination for his portrayal of Kirk Lazarus.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-USADowneyQuote-133)

In October 2008, Paramount chose to put end-of-year award push funds behind _Tropic Thunder_ and began advertising for Downey to receive a nomination by the Academy Awards for [Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyBestSupport-134) In a November 2008 issue by _Entertainment Weekly_, Downey's film role was considered one of the three contenders for Best Supporting Actor.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyEWSupport-135) As a way of extending the film-within-a-film "universe" into real life, there were at least two online "For Your Consideration" ads touting Downey's character, Kirk Lazarus, for Best Supporting Actor; one of these contains "scenes" from _Satan's Alley_ that were not in the trailer as released in theaters. At least one of the ads was produced by Paramount Pictures and intended for early For Your Consideration awareness for Downey's role.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyAdsLazarus-136) On January 22, 2009, the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") nominated Downey for Best Supporting Actor.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyJanNom-137) At the [81st Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards"), Downey lost to [Heath Ledger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heath_Ledger "Heath Ledger"), who [won posthumously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_posthumous_Academy_Award_winners_and_nominees "List of posthumous Academy Award winners and nominees") for his role as [The Joker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joker_(The_Dark_Knight) "Joker (The Dark Knight)") in _[The Dark Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_Knight "The Dark Knight")_.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyLedger-138)

With the onset of the annual Hollywood film award season at the end of 2008, _Tropic Thunder_ began receiving nominations and awards starting with a win for "Hollywood Comedy of the Year Award" at the 12th annual [Hollywood Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Film_Festival "Hollywood Film Festival") on October 27, 2008.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-HollyComAwa-139)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-HollywoodComedyAward-140) The film was nominated for Best Motion Picture, Comedy or Musical, for the [Satellite Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellite_Awards_2008 "Satellite Awards 2008"). In addition, Downey was nominated for Best Actor in a Supporting Role.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-Satell2008Nom-141) The [Broadcast Film Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_Film_Critics_Association "Broadcast Film Critics Association") nominated Downey for Best Supporting Actor and awarded _Tropic Thunder_ Best Comedy Movie at the BFCA's Critics' Choice Awards.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BFCA2008-142) Both Downey and Cruise received nominations from the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association") for [Golden Globes for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor_-_Motion_Picture "Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor - Motion Picture").[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-HFPA2008-143) The [Boston Society of Film Critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Society_of_Film_Critics "Boston Society of Film Critics") recognized the cast with its Best Ensemble award.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BostonEnsemble-144) Downey was also nominated by both the [Screen Actors Guild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild "Screen Actors Guild") and the [British Academy of Film and Television Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_of_Film_and_Television_Arts "British Academy of Film and Television Arts") for Best Supporting Actor awards.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyBestSAG-145)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DowneyBestBAFTA-146)

A [spin-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin-off_(media) "Spin-off (media)") film centering on Grossman was announced in 2010.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-LesFilm-147) A script has been written by [Michael Bacall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bacall "Michael Bacall").[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-LesScript-148) In 2012, Bacall said the film will explore the origin of Grossman's anger issues.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-149) As of 2022, Cruise and frequent collaborator [Christopher McQuarrie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_McQuarrie "Christopher McQuarrie") are developing the spin-off, though it is not clear whether Grossman will be the protagonist or a supporting character.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-150)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-151)

## Controversy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tropic_Thunder&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Controversy")]

[![Image 18: A crowd of people at the left are standing behind a gated barrier. The crowd is holding protest signs and the majority are looking away from the camera. An obscured man is being interviewed at the right side of the image. The sky appears to be approaching night.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/TropicThunderprotest.jpg/250px-TropicThunderprotest.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TropicThunderprotest.jpg)

A group protesting against the film on August 11, 2008

_Tropic Thunder_ was criticized by the disability advocacy community. The website for _Simple Jack_ was withdrawn on August 4 amid several groups' concerns over its portrayal of [intellectual disability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_disability "Intellectual disability").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SimpleJackPulled-82) A spokesman for DreamWorks said, "We heard their concerns, and we understand that taken out of context, the site appeared to be insensitive to people with disabilities."[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SimpleJackPulled-82) A coalition of more than 20 disability advocacy groups, including the [Special Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Olympics "Special Olympics") and the [Arc of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arc_of_the_United_States "Arc of the United States"), objected to the film's repeated use of the word "retard".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-NYTBoycott-77) DreamWorks offered to screen the film for the groups on August 8 to determine if it still offended them.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DreamWorksMeet-152)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BusinessOffend-153) The screening was postponed to the same day of the premiere on August 11.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-PostPoneScreen-154) After representatives for the groups attended the private screening and were still offended by its content, the groups picketed outside the film's premiere.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-Mortified-155)[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-PremPick-156)[Timothy Shriver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Shriver "Timothy Shriver"), the chairman of the Special Olympics, stated, "This population struggles too much with the basics to have to struggle against Hollywood. We're sending a message that this hate speech is no longer acceptable."[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-ShrivOly-157)

Disability advocates and others who previewed the film reported that the offensive treatment of individuals with mental disabilities was woven throughout the film's plot.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-PostPoneScreen-154) Disability advocates urged people not to see the film, claiming it is demeaning to individuals with mental disabilities and would encourage bullying.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-BullyingWicked-158) Stiller responded, "We screened the movie so many times and this didn't come up until very late ...in the context of the film I think it's really clear, they were making fun of the actors and actors who try to use serious subjects to win awards."[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-StillerDefend-159) Co-writer [Etan Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etan_Cohen "Etan Cohen") echoed Stiller's rationale: "Some people have taken this as making fun of handicapped people, but we're really trying to make fun of the actors who use this material as fodder for acclaim."[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-EtanQuote-160) He went on to state that the film lampoons actors who portray intellectually disabled or [autistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autistic "Autistic") characters such as [Dustin Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dustin_Hoffman "Dustin Hoffman") in _[Rain Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain\_Man "Rain Man")_, [Tom Hanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hanks "Tom Hanks") in _[Forrest Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forrest\_Gump "Forrest Gump")_, and [Sean Penn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Penn "Sean Penn") in _[I Am Sam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Am\_Sam "I Am Sam")_.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-EtanQuote-160)

A DreamWorks spokesman stated that _Tropic Thunder_ "is an R-rated comedy that satirizes Hollywood and its excesses" and "makes its point by featuring inappropriate and over-the-top characters in ridiculous situations."[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-NYTBoycott-77) The film's advertising was altered, but none of the scenes in the film were edited as a result of the opposition.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-NYTBoycott-77)[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-PremPick-156) In response to the controversy, the director's cut of the DVD (but not the Blu-ray) includes a public service announcement in the special features that discourages use of the word "retard".[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-DVDPSA-161)

Another aspect that drew warning before the release of the movie and criticism afterwards was Downey Jr. playing a white Australian actor who dons blackface as part of his [method acting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Method_acting "Method acting") the [role of an African-American man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_representation_in_Hollywood "African-American representation in Hollywood"). He responded by pointing out that this was a case of donning blackface in order to point out how wrong it is.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-162) Others have pointed out that the wrongness of blackface is addressed within the movie itself by an actual African American, and that the climax of the movie pins on Downey Jr.'s shedding of his method acting. In this way, the movie mocks—rather than embraces—both blackface and the extreme and ridiculous things method actors sometimes do for their roles.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-163)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

Some have alleged that the film's characterization—and the non-Jewish Tom Cruise's portrayal—of the Jewish character Les Grossman is [antisemitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitic "Antisemitic"). In addition to his Jewish name, the character of Grossman also references the Jewish holiday of [Purim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purim "Purim"). Critics have also referred to this performance as "[Jewface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereotypes_of_Jews#Jewface "Stereotypes of Jews")" as early as 2008, calling it "vulgar" and "exploitation";[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-164) others, however, including the _[St. Louis Jewish Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St.\_Louis\_Jewish\_Light "St. Louis Jewish Light")_, which referenced _Tropic Thunder_ in particular, noted that Jewface was a "riff on the practice of blackface and is nowhere near its equivalent." Cruise was largely responsible for the final form Grossman took, including using him as an additional villain, the hairiness of the character, and the "fat hands".[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-165)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-166)

In February 2023, after a fan of the film suggested that Stiller "stop apologizing for doing this movie [...] [which is] [e]ven funnier now with [cancel culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancel_culture "Cancel culture") the way it is.[_[sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")_] It's a MOVIE. Ya'll can just get over it," Stiller responded on Twitter, "Don't know who told you that."[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-:0-167) Stiller additionally responded to the fan that the former "make[s] no apologies for Tropic Thunder" and is "proud of it and the work everyone did on it." Years before, in 2018, Stiller wrote on Twitter, "Actually Tropic Thunder was boycotted 10 years ago when it came out, and I apologized then [...] It was always meant to make fun of actors trying to do anything to win awards. I stand by my apology, the movie [...] [a]nd the great people and work of the @SpecialOlympics."[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-:0-167)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-168)

_Tropic Thunder_'s [score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score") and [soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundtrack_album "Soundtrack album") were released on August 5, 2008, the week before the film's theatrical release. The score was composed by [Theodore Shapiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Shapiro "Theodore Shapiro"), conducted by Pete Anthony and performed by the [Hollywood Studio Symphony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Studio_Symphony "Hollywood Studio Symphony"). William Ruhlmann of [AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic") gave the score a positive review, stating it is "...an affectionate and knowing satire of the history of Hollywood action movie music, penned by an insider."[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-TTScore-169) Thomas Simpson of [Soundtrack.Net](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundtrack.Net "Soundtrack.Net") called it "...a mixture of fun, seriousness, rock n' roll and great scoring."[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SNetScore-170)

Five songs—"[Cum On Feel the Noize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cum_On_Feel_the_Noize "Cum On Feel the Noize")" by [Quiet Riot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quiet_Riot "Quiet Riot"), "[Sympathy for the Devil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sympathy_for_the_Devil "Sympathy for the Devil")" by [The Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones"), "[For What It's Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_What_It's_Worth "For What It's Worth")" by [Buffalo Springfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Springfield "Buffalo Springfield"), "[Low](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_(Flo_Rida_song) "Low (Flo Rida song)")" by [Flo Rida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flo_Rida "Flo Rida") and [T-Pain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-Pain "T-Pain"), and "[Get Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get_Back_(Ludacris_song) "Get Back (Ludacris song)")" by [Ludacris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludacris "Ludacris")—were not present on the soundtrack despite appearing in the film. The soundtrack features songs from [The Temptations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Temptations "The Temptations"), [MC Hammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MC_Hammer "MC Hammer"), [Creedence Clearwater Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creedence_Clearwater_Revival "Creedence Clearwater Revival"), [Edwin Starr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Starr "Edwin Starr"), and other artists. The single "[Name of the Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name_of_the_Game_(The_Crystal_Method_song) "Name of the Game (The Crystal Method song)")" by [The Crystal Method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Crystal_Method "The Crystal Method"), featuring [Ryu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Styles_of_Beyond "Styles of Beyond"), has an exclusive [remix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remix "Remix") on the soundtrack.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-TTSoundtrack-171) The soundtrack debuted 20th on _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")'_ s Top Soundtracks list and peaked at 39th on its Top Independent Albums list.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-SoundtrackBillboard-172) James Christopher Monger of allmusic compared the music to other film's soundtracks such as _[Platoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platoon\_(film) "Platoon (film)")_, _[Full Metal Jacket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full\_Metal\_Jacket "Full Metal Jacket")_, and _[Forrest Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forrest\_Gump "Forrest Gump")_ and called it "...a fun but slight listen that plays out like an old late-'70s [K-Tel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-Tel "K-Tel") compilation with a few bonus cuts from the future."[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_Thunder#cite_note-AllmusicReview-173)

 #### [1. Will Smith](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000226/?ref_=ls_t_1) 

    *   Producer
    *   Actor
    *   Writer

[The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air (1990–1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098800/?ref_=ls_knf_1)

Willard Carroll "Will" Smith II (born September 25, 1968) is an American actor, comedian, producer, rapper, and songwriter. He has enjoyed success in television, film, and music. In April 2007, Newsweek called him "the most powerful actor in Hollywood". Smith has been nominated for five Golden Globe Awards, two Academy Awards, and has won four Grammy Awards.  
  
In the late 1980s, Smith achieved modest fame as a rapper under the name The Fresh Prince. In 1990, his popularity increased dramatically when he starred in the popular television series The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air. The show ran for six seasons (1990-96) on NBC and has been syndicated consistently on various networks since then. After the series ended, Smith moved from television to film, and ultimately starred in numerous blockbuster films. He is the only actor to have eight consecutive films gross over $100 million in the domestic box office, eleven consecutive films gross over $150 million internationally, and eight consecutive films in which he starred open at the number one spot in the domestic box office tally.  
  
Smith is ranked as the most bankable star worldwide by Forbes. As of 2014, 17 of the 21 films in which he has had leading roles have accumulated worldwide gross earnings of over $100 million each, five taking in over $500 million each in global box office receipts. As of 2014, his films have grossed $6.6 billion at the global box office. He has received Best Actor Oscar nominations for Ali and The Pursuit of Happyness.  
  
Smith was born in West Philadelphia, the son of Caroline (Bright), a Philadelphia school board administrator, and Willard Carroll Smith, Sr., a refrigeration engineer. He grew up in West Philadelphia's Wynnefield neighborhood, and was raised Baptist. He has three siblings, sister Pamela, who is four years older, and twins Harry and Ellen, who are three years younger. Smith attended Our Lady of Lourdes, a private Catholic elementary school in Philadelphia. His parents separated when he was 13, but did not actually divorce until around 2000.  
  
Smith attended Overbrook High School. Though widely reported, it is untrue that Smith turned down a scholarship to attend the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT); he never applied to college because he "wanted to rap." Smith says he was admitted to a "pre-engineering [summer] program" at MIT for high school students, but he did not attend. According to Smith, "My mother, who worked for the School Board of Philadelphia, had a friend who was the admissions officer at MIT. I had pretty high SAT scores and they needed black kids, so I probably could have gotten in. But I had no intention of going to college."  
  
Smith started as the MC of the hip-hop duo DJ Jazzy Jeff & The Fresh Prince, with his childhood friend Jeffrey "DJ Jazzy Jeff" Townes as producer, as well as Ready Rock C (Clarence Holmes) as the human beat box. The trio was known for performing humorous, radio-friendly songs, most notably "Parents Just Don't Understand" and "Summertime". They gained critical acclaim and won the first Grammy awarded in the Rap category (1988).  
  
Smith spent money freely around 1988 and 1989 and underpaid his income taxes. The Internal Revenue Service eventually assessed a $2.8 million tax debt against Smith, took many of his possessions, and garnished his income. Smith was nearly bankrupt in 1990, when the NBC television network signed him to a contract and built a sitcom, The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, around him.  
  
The show was successful and began his acting career. Smith set for himself the goal of becoming "the biggest movie star in the world", studying box office successes' common characteristics.  
  
 Smith's first major roles were in the drama Six Degrees of Separation (1993) and the action film Bad Boys (1995) in which he starred opposite Martin Lawrence.  
  
In 1996, Smith starred as part of an ensemble cast in Roland Emmerich's Independence Day. The film was a massive blockbuster, becoming the second highest grossing film in history at the time and establishing Smith as a prime box office draw. He later struck gold again in the summer of 1997 alongside Tommy Lee Jones in the summer hit Men in Black playing Agent J. In 1998, Smith starred with Gene Hackman in Enemy of the State.  
  
He turned down the role of Neo in The Matrix in favor of Wild Wild West (1999). Despite the disappointment of Wild Wild West, Smith has said that he harbors no regrets about his decision, asserting that Keanu Reeves's performance as Neo was superior to what Smith himself would have achieved, although in interviews subsequent to the release of Wild Wild West he stated that he "made a mistake on Wild Wild West. That could have been better."  
  
In 2005, Smith was entered into the Guinness Book of World Records for attending three premieres in a 24-hour time span.  
  
He has planned to star in a feature film remake of the television series It Takes a Thief.  
  
On December 10, 2007, Smith was honored at Grauman's Chinese Theatre on Hollywood Boulevard. Smith left an imprint of his hands and feet outside the world-renowned theater in front of many fans. Later that month, Smith starred in the film I Am Legend, released December 14, 2007. Despite marginally positive reviews, its opening was the largest ever for a film released in the United States during December. Smith himself has said that he considers the film to be "aggressively unique". A reviewer said that the film's commercial success "cemented [Smith's] standing as the number one box office draw in Hollywood." On December 1, 2008, TV Guide reported that Smith was selected as one of America's top ten most fascinating people of 2008 for a Barbara Walters ABC special that aired on December 4, 2008.  
  
In 2008 Smith was reported to be developing a film entitled The Last Pharaoh, in which he would be starring as Taharqa. It was in 2008 that Smith starred in the superhero movie Hancock.  
  
Men in Black III opened on May 25, 2012 with Smith again reprising his role as Agent J. This was his first major starring role in four years.  
  
On August 19, 2011, it was announced that Smith had returned to the studio with producer La Mar Edwards to work on his fifth studio album. Edwards has worked with artists such as T.I., Chris Brown, and Game. Smith's most recent studio album, Lost and Found, was released in 2005.  
  
Smith and his son Jaden played father and son in two productions: the 2006 biographical drama The Pursuit of Happyness, and the science fiction film After Earth, which was released on May 31, 2013.  
  
Smith starred opposite Margot Robbie in the romance drama Focus. He played Nicky Spurgeon, a veteran con artist who takes a young, attractive woman under his wing. Focus was released on February 27, 2015. Smith was set to star in the Sci-Fic thriller Brilliance, an adaptation of Marcus Sakey's novel of the same name scripted by Jurassic Park writer David Koepp. But he left the project.  
  
Smith played Dr. Bennet Omalu of the Brain Injury Research Institute in the sports-drama Concussion, who became the first person to discover chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) in a football player's brain. CTE is a degenerative disease caused by severe trauma to the head that can be discovered only after death. Smith's involvement is mostly due to his last-minute exit from the Sci-Fi thriller-drama Brilliance. Concussion was directed by Peter Landesman and-bead filmed in Pittsburgh, according to the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review. It received $14.4 million in film tax credits from Pennsylvania. Principal photography started on October 27, 2014. Actress Gugu Mbatha-Raw played his wife. Omalu served as a consultant.  
  
As of November 2015, Smith is set to star in the independent drama Collateral Beauty, which will be directed by David Frankel. Smith will play a New York advertising executive who succumbs to an deep depression after a personal tragedy.  
  
Nobel Peace Prize Concert December 11, 2009, in Oslo, Norway: Smith with wife Jada and children Jaden and Willow Smith married Sheree Zampino in 1992. They had one son, Trey Smith, born on November 11, 1992, and divorced in 1995. Trey appeared in his father's music video for the 1998 single "Just the Two of Us". He also acted in two episodes of the sitcom All of Us, and has appeared on The Oprah Winfrey Show and on the David Blaine: Real or Magic TV special.  
  
Smith married actress Jada Koren Pinkett in 1997. Together they have two children: Jaden Christopher Syre Smith (born 1998), his co-star in The Pursuit of Happyness and After Earth, and Willow Camille Reign Smith (born 2000), who appeared as his daughter in I Am Legend. Smith and his brother Harry own Treyball Development Inc., a Beverly Hills-based company named after Trey. Smith and his family reside in Los Angeles, California.  
  
Smith was consistently listed in Fortune Magazine's "Richest 40" list of the forty wealthiest Americans under the age of 40.

 #### [2. Angelina Jolie](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001401/?ref_=ls_t_2)

    *   Producer
